tom_tat: I and the Buddhas of the ten directions share the same true enlightenment. Did not the Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha once teach that: "All sentient beings are full of the Tathagata's wisdom and virtues?"
noi_dung:
It's also an autobiography

Lately, I've been thinking to myself:

I and the Buddhas of the ten directions share the same true enlightenment. Did not the Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha once teach that: "All sentient beings are full of the Tathagata's wisdom and virtues" !

From the beginning of the body, it is not that we are behind the Buddhas. Why are the Buddhas, who have liberated themselves and have immeasurable wisdom, merit, and miraculous powers, but we are still bound in the cycle of birth and death, full of boundless afflictions, karma, and misery? Is it because the Buddhas soon realized their true nature, while we are engrossed in worldly desires! What a shame! How reprehensible!

I thought to myself again:

Having already known for ourselves, we must now take care to be liberated, and must be liberated in this present life. If you are not liberated in this present life, your next life will be difficult to guarantee, and you may still be stuck in the cycle of reincarnation like past lives! Why is that? There are many things that hinder our path to liberation in the next life:

1.- Due to the merit of practicing in this life, will I be born in the heavens? In the Sutra, it is said: Gods of the Desire Realm, because the world of the five desires is so abundant and wonderful that it makes them enchanted, but there is no pain to awaken them, so it is difficult to develop the mind to endure hardship and practice virtue. If you enjoy blessings and happiness forever without cultivating, one day your blessings will run out and you will fall. As for the Gods in the realms of Form and Formless, because they forever stay in the realm of meditation, it is difficult for them to progress in cultivating the path of liberation. When their meditation power is complete, they still remain reincarnated.

Vinh Gia Zen Master said: Those who cultivate merit and are born in the heavens will reap the consequences of suffering in the future, like shooting an arrow into the air, but when the strength is exhausted, the arrow falls to the ground.

That is, being born in heaven in time and space ensures liberation.

2.- Will I be born as a human again? There are many blind, deaf, mute, and speechless people on the face of the earth; Man, Moi, barbarians with many people; There are so many lands without Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha; places full of pagans and pagans. If you have a human body and have one of the above things, it will be difficult to practice the right path, and you will definitely stray into evil ways. In addition, if we are blessed, we will become a king, a mandarin, or a millionaire: "To become rich and learn the Dharma is difficult," Buddha said clearly in the Sutra Forty-Two Chapters. Or maybe in a previous life you practiced meditation and became intelligent: "Worldly knowledge and understanding" is one of the eight tribulations. Not to mention the countless people who take advantage of their wealth and intelligence to commit heinous crimes, which we often hear about in life...

Even though our human body in the next life is free from these obstacles due to good roots, according to the Buddha's words, the Dharma is going deeper and deeper into the end times, and a good and genuine master who practices with moral power is very difficult to meet. If your teacher has liberated you, who is the one who will guide us to enlightenment? As the kalpa declines, human life span becomes shorter and shorter. In the next life, if we practice nothing and then die, what will happen in the third or fourth life? Where will we go?

So even if one is born as a human again, one cannot guarantee liberation.

3.- Buddha said: "Human beings have a human body like the soil stuck to their fingernails, but they fall into evil paths like the soil of the entire great earth." After leaving this body, do we dare to decide not to go down? The sutra says: "Committing a small crime (kylā) must fall into hell with the lifespan of the Four Heavenly Kings." What's more, karma from countless lifetimes up to now is hard to measure. I'm afraid that if the "Strongman of the Shield Immortal" takes one wrong step, he will definitely fall to the bottom of the deep pit. This is the fear of eternal damnation in the next life.

Oh! The human body is difficult to endure, and the Buddha Dharma is difficult to hear. Now, because of my good roots, I can enjoy a little bit of Tathagata's legacy. Martial arts knows two paths to liberation. What a great virtue! It's so rare! What are we waiting for without going straight to practice? What are we waiting for to stop the stream of birth and death? And all human beings, all other species, are also floating and sinking in the shoreless sea of ​​suffering. We must soon reach Buddhahood, so that we can use the boat of compassion and vows to save sentient beings, it cannot be done gradually.

Then I thought to myself:

Based on the Holy Teachings: Get rid of the three worlds of selfish views or only be able to escape samsara. If there is still a trace of affliction, the root of birth and death has not been cut off. This is the commentary of Hinayana and Mahayana.

As for the Mahayana, to be guaranteed on the path to liberation and Buddhahood, it must be led by a person of faith and non-regression. At this level, according to the Awakening of Faith, one must be capable of cultivating good roots, deeply believing in causes and effects, eliminating evil actions, serving good people, developing Bodhi mind, meeting Buddhas close to them, making offerings, and practicing Bodhisattva conduct. Practicing like this takes until ten thousand great kalpas of faith to achieve success.

Oh! What are the times like that? We are sentient beings of the Dharma Ending Age, seeing ourselves as having thin blessings, thick karma, deep obstacles and shallow wisdom. Can my wish to be liberated within my present life, my wish to go straight to perfect Buddhahood, become a dream?

But I console myself:

Buddha Tathagata taught a supreme method to ensure liberation but also to firmly ensure the path to Buddhahood for all sentient beings:

Pure Land Dharma, Reciting Buddha's Name to Pray for Rebirth in the Pure Land World!

According to the Buddha, even if you are an extremely evil person, if you return your mind and practice this method for a very short time (10 thoughts), you will still be reborn; Once reborn, you will attain the supernatural level of Sainthood, completely escape birth and death, and never retreat from Supreme Bodhi.

By relying on this method, we will surely be able to fulfill our original vows: liberation, Buddhahood, and salvation. Extremely evil people can still achieve success, not to mention I am not yet an evil person!

From that day on, I made up my mind to stay in the Pure Land and tried to practice. I entrust my dharma body and my life to the Buddha

Amitabha Buddha, considering the Pure Land as his home, spared time to concentrate on reciting Buddha's name...

Although it is only after attaining Buddhahood that the goal of saving sentient beings can be fulfilled, the desire to benefit others urges us, so we also depend on our part, while trying to save ourselves and at the same time encourage those with predestined relationships. Wanting all sentient beings to be liberated like me, wanting everyone to improve before me, that is the body and mind of this poor monk.

Therefore, I did not hesitate to clumsily collect the teachings of the "Pure Land Dharma" of Buddha, Bodhisattva and Ancient Virtue, in the official Sutras and Treatises, and describe the stories of Sangha, laity, and the four sentient beings who have been reborn in the official transmission books, to combine them into this "Road to Ultimate Bliss" series.

“The Path to Ultimate Bliss” is the dharma path that leads us and all sentient beings from the evil land of Saha to the pure world of Ultimate Bliss. It is also the “Pure Land Dharma” said in a different way.

This set is a collection work only. Because I want to maintain trust and introduce the Pure Land Sutras to everyone, I have not clearly quoted from which Sutra, which Commentary, or which book, each article and each paragraph is quoted. Even though there are some places here that need to be changed a little to straighten the paragraph or change the words to make the sentence simpler, but absolutely do not change the idea. It can be trusted that: this book is the words of Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and Ancient Virtues, and is absolutely not the personal opinion of this poor monk. What more do I want to add to the inheritance, since the Buddha's words and ideas are so complete in countless sutras and commentaries, and besides, the knowledge of ordinary people cannot compare with the wisdom of the Saints! Sometimes I add more, like in the "additional lyrics" passages, for example, the monks just rephrase the words of the previous article to make the meaning clear, emphasize important points, recall important things, or encourage book growth, to help people benefit while watching and reading.

Regarding the brief history of the Pure Land monks who were reborn, I chose stories that clearly recorded their achievements in practice, or accurate instructions, so that I could serve as a guide for those who are committed to practice, and help further enlighten the reader.

Read this entire book carefully, in addition to the great benefit of understanding the Pure Land and Pure Land Dharma; to develop faith, virtue, and vows if we have developed them; If we have achieved faith, virtue, and vows, if they have grown and become perfect, we can use this as a good friend to point out the right places and to warn us of what is wrong while practicing the religion, because our intelligence, temperament, circumstances, conditions, favorable conditions, or questions of each of us, more or less, decide whether we will be able to get into the stories in this series.

I sincerely pray that this book will bring the ultimate results to everyone, to all sentient beings as its name suggests: "Rebirth in Ultimate Bliss, remaining at the level of unsurpassed Bodhi".

Buddha taught:

“If there is anyone who has made a vow, is now making a vow, will make a vow, and wants to be born in Amitabha Buddha's Land of Ultimate Bliss, then they will all be irreversible in the Supreme Enlightenment, and either have already been born in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, are currently being born, or will be born.

Shariputra! Therefore, good men and women, if they have faith, should vow to be born in that realm."

Amitabha Sutra

Dharma Gate of Buddha's Remembrance

is the victory over Tathagata's means

All sentient beings have the same wisdom and virtue as Buddha. Just because the left awareness follows the dust, the entire wisdom and virtue turns into ignorance and afflictions. Then following the afflictions causes the creation of karma that results in the consequences of birth and death in the three worlds. From the karma of birth and death comes affliction and then causes the karma of suffering... Because of that, sentient beings from beginningless time until now, through countless eons, suffer forever in the cycle of birth and death.

Out of great compassion, the Buddha appeared in the world to preach the Dharma to save living beings. Buddha's original mind only wanted all sentient beings to completely escape the cycle of birth and death and attain Buddhahood. However, because sentient beings have different intelligence and stupidity, the Buddha had to follow the opportunity to teach. Therefore, the Buddha's teachings are immeasurable.

For sentient beings with great wisdom, the Buddha taught the Buddha Vehicle to immediately achieve Buddhahood. Like Thien Tai in the Hoa Nghiem Dharma Assembly, Dragon Lady in the Dieu Phap ashram...

To sentient beings with poor intelligence, the Buddha taught the Bodhisattva Vehicle, Pratyekabuddha Vehicle and Shravaka Vehicle, so that those people could practice in turn and gradually achieve results.

To sentient beings whose level is too low, the Buddha spoke of the Ten Good and Five Precepts, the Heavenly Vehicle and the Human Vehicle, for those people to follow so as not to fall into evil paths, so that they can still have human and heavenly bodies to gradually cultivate good roots. In the future, rely on that good root to cultivate the Holy Path; Or study the Bodhisattva vehicle and practice the six ten thousand virtues to attain Dharma body, or follow the Pratyekabuddha vehicle or Shravaka vehicle to realize the conditions of birth and the Four Truths to end afflictions and attain Nirvana...

All of these dharmas, whether they are Mahayana or Hinayana, Modern Buddhism or Eastern Buddhism, practitioners must practice by themselves until all afflictions are completely eliminated in order to escape the cycle of birth and death. If there is even a strand of view or thought left, then the root of birth and death has not yet been completely ended. Like the three saints (A-na-hat) after being born in the Immaculate Heaven, they still have to spend a lot of time to attain A-la-han status. Only by attaining Arhatship is the true end of the root of birth and death.

But A-la-Han is only a Hinayana Saint who still needs to turn his mind to practice Mahayana and pray for the Buddha way: practice compassion and vow to manifest himself in the six paths, practice the six degrees of ten thousand virtues, on the way to become a Buddha, on the bottom to save the sufferings of all living beings, one by one to attain the following levels: Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications, Ten Grounds and Fully Enlightened Bodhisattva. The Fully Enlightened One must use Vajra wisdom to destroy a part of ignorance in order to perfect his wisdom and attain Buddhahood (Wonderful Enlightenment).

The Buddha's teachings teach that each person cultivating from mortal to Saint, from Saint to Buddha, cannot go beyond the above mentioned week.

Our Master knows that if sentient beings only use their own power to escape from birth and escape death and become a saint, it will be very difficult for them to enter the saints, so in addition to the countless methods of self-reliance, he teaches a method of self-reliance on others that is very complete, very magical, easy to practice and highly successful, uses little effort and is quickly effective, all abilities are suitable, and all saints and mortals practice together. It is the Pure Land Dharma, reciting Buddha's name and praying for rebirth.

Because Amitabha Buddha has a vow to have the power to capture sentient beings while reciting the Buddha's name. Therefore, people who recite the Buddha's name with faith in their vows (self-power) will sympathize with the Buddha's power of prayer. Relying on the Buddha's power of prayer to take hold of them (other power), they will immediately escape the cycle of birth and death and be born in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Having been reborn means being highly promoted and a Saint who cannot retreat, so it is called very complete, very magical, and highly successful.

In this method, the practice method is very simple, everyone can practice according to their strength. As long as you practice the Dharma correctly, you will definitely achieve it. It is called using little effort, easy to practice and quickly effective. Patriarch Thien Dao believes that not one of a thousand people can practice. Master Vinh Minh recognized ten practitioners, received ten...

With this Pure Land Dharma, it doesn't matter whether you are wise or stupid, whether you are Sangha or lay person, whether you are rich or poor, whether you are old or young, men or women, whether you are scholars, farmers, workers, traders... All precepts in society can be practiced and can be achieved.

Manjushri Bodhisattva said: None of the practice disciplines surpass the practice of reciting the Buddha's name. Reciting Buddha's name is the "King" of all dharmas.

Avalokiteśvara said: Pure Land Dharma is superior to all other practices.

Master Ma Minh said: Concentrating on reciting the Buddha's name is the supreme means of the Tathagata.

Venerable Nagarjuna said: “Reciting the Buddha Samadhi” has great wisdom, has great merit, or eliminating all afflictions, or saving all sentient beings, “Reciting the Buddha Samadhi” or giving birth to immeasurable Samadhis up to “Samadhi Samadhi”.

Bodhisattva Bodhisattva said: The method of reciting the Buddha's name is the mind sect of the Buddhas, the shortest path to liberation of all beings.

Great Master An Quang once said: Because of Buddha's power, everyone, regardless of their karma, whether large or small, regardless of how shallow or deep their practice of practicing the Dharma, must believe firmly, pray firmly, and at the same time, all people who practice and practice will be reborn without missing a single one. If you are an already dead person or a certified person and wish to be reborn, then you will transcend the Ten Grounds. If you seek rebirth at the Ten Levels, you will quickly attain Buddhahood. That's why Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, Nagarjuna, etc., the great Bodhisattvas all vowed to be reborn. Even those who have created evil all their lives are about to fall into hell, but when they recite Buddha's name, they will also be liberated, like Mr. Truong Thien Hoa, Truong Chung Huc, Hung Tuan, Duy Cung, etc.

Those types of people who commit evil crimes can still achieve success, let alone those who are not too evil, let alone those who are good!

Therefore, it should be seen that this Pure Land Dharma gate captures all Saints, all good and evil, all sentient beings, like a great ocean containing countless streams.

Because the Pure Land Dharma has such vast benefits to sentient beings, all sutras and treatises always mention it, and all Saints and Sages vow to return together.

It's true:

Nine world sentient beings who leave this method cannot attain Buddhahood.

If the Buddhas of the ten directions abandon this method, they will not be able to save all sentient beings.

In the Great Collection Sutra, the Buddha has a mysterious statement: "At the end of the Dharma, with millions of people practicing, it is difficult for one person to be liberated. Only relying on the method of reciting the Buddha's name can escape samsara."

That is Buddha telling us to have faith in and practice this Pure Land Dharma. Are we not the people of that Dharma-Ending Age!

For the above reasons, we know that:

Besides the practice of “reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land”, it is decided that we cannot transcend birth and escape death in this life. If we follow this method of "reciting the Buddha's name and praying for birth" and practice, we will definitely be reborn in the Pure Land in this present life and be guaranteed on the path to Buddhahood.

In general: “For the sake of birth and death, develop the Bodhi mind, use deep faith and earnest vows, and specially uphold the name of Amitabha Buddha.” This is the main sect of this Pure Land Dharma. Right conduct of mind here is called cultivating the right Dharma.

When we hear the Buddha's teachings on the Pure Land, we think to ourselves: The Saha world is a place of five impurities and evils, the three realms are like a house of fire, the world of Desire that we are in here is like a deep hole full of mud. We and everyone of all species, now and in the past, have endured countless sufferings in the cycle of birth and death for many lifetimes. Today, we are born as humans and have heard that the dharma of liberation is quickly extinguished and transcendent. We must quickly resolve to follow the dharma and practice, so that we and everyone can simultaneously escape the suffering of birth and death, and simultaneously attain eternal happiness." This is "Due to birth and death, developing the Bodhi mind" is like this.

Then I admit to myself: This body and scene in Saha are full of obstacles: they easily give rise to afflictions, they easily become infected, they easily cause bad karma; Aging, sickness, death, and impermanence are enough to hinder our path to liberation. As for the body and the scene in Ultimate Bliss, it is very beneficial: often seeing Buddha, always hearing the Dharma sounds, so the mind is pure and concentration and wisdom are achieved; Living together with the Great Bodhisattvas, good people, while their Holy karma increases day by day, their righteous conduct grows day by day; He is neither old nor sick, has a life span of immeasurable and boundless kalpas, so within one lifetime he can ascend to the level of Enlightenment and attain Buddhahood.

I again commented: Amitabha Buddha's vow power is vast and inconceivable. Now I practice according to the method of reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. I am determined to be accepted by the Buddha, determined to be reborn, to be reborn means to attain Non-regression and quickly attain Buddhahood. Only the Buddha's vow is the magnetic boat that can take me out of the sea of ​​suffering! Only the Pure Land is the great university that can bring us to the shore of Great Enlightenment!

Confess yourself like that and then firmly commit to: vowing to escape the evil defilements of Saha, like a prisoner wanting to get out of the dungeon without any attachment; Wishing to return to the pure Paradise, it seems like a lost child longs to return home without hesitation.

Making such an assessment, making such a vow, that is “Deep faith and sincere vows” .

Starting from now until the rest of your life, depending on the case, depending on the circumstances, depending on the strength, depending on the part, wholeheartedly recite the six red words of the name “Namo Amitabha Buddha”, considering it as an extremely urgent public service that must be done with all your strength. If one is free and carefree, then day and night, when walking and standing as well as when sitting and lying down, maintain mindfulness: Buddha does not leave the mind, mind does not leave the Buddha; Either reciting out loud or silently, taking in all six senses, the Buddha's effect is always connected: this is continuous holding; If you meditate like this for a long time, you will automatically realize Samadhi: in the present you will see the Buddha's prediction, and at the end of your life you will be promoted to the highest level. If you are a person who has a lot of work: country work, housework, etc., and doesn't have many free hours, you should practice the "Ten Thoughts" method at night and early in the morning, keep it for the rest of your life without missing or giving up, and you will be reborn. Because the Compassionate Father has a vow: "All sentient beings in the ten directions hear my name, then believe with all their heart and wish to be born in my land for ten recitations. If those sentient beings are not born, then I will not be in the position of perfect enlightenment."

In addition, those who are in the middle stage should accept and maintain the teachings at the right time. Everyone must be respectful, single-minded, and careful while reciting, which is an essential condition. Practicing like this is called "specially maintaining Amitabha's name", and this is the right conduct.

People who recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land still need to do things

good things: having compassion and precepts to kill and protect living beings, to give alms, to help, to maintain good conduct, to keep the precepts, to be filial to one's parents, to respect the Master, to uphold the Three Jewels, to benefit oneself and benefit others, to suppress arrogance, greed and anger, to grow in joy and patience, to deepen faith in cause and effect, to develop right view... use this as an aid to conduct.

The faith in the vow is there, the right support is enough, at the time of death, the Father and the Holy Order will certainly come and receive the power of the original vow to personally lead them to rebirth in the Pure Land.

Although Faith, Prayer and Behavior must be all three to be reborn, like a three-legged crown, lacking a self, but we should further understand that: being reborn is due to deep faith, earnest prayer to sympathize with the Buddha's vows, and in meritorious deeds: few periods of low results, many periods of high achievements. Because of the unlimited merit that focuses on such faith and vows, the previous paragraph said: “All people in all social circles can practice and can achieve everything” because of deep faith and strong vows any type of person can establish it, the ten recitations of the Buddha's name can be practiced in any case.

The content of this “Road to Ultimate Bliss” is not outside the scope of “Vows of Faith”.

The first chapters recount Amitabha Buddha's past lives and clearly describe the correct retribution and solemn robes of the Pure Land world so that everyone can receive true recognition of the Buddha and the Pure Land. Real recognition means firm belief and earnest aspiration that will be established thereby. The chapters describe the brief history of the Bodhisattvas and great Patriarchs who successfully cultivated the Pure Land themselves, along with their teachings and reminders, so that everyone can maintain strong faith, resolute aspirations, and clearly understand the method of practice to progress diligently in practice. The chapters on the Four Beings are reborn, and finally, the appropriate chapter also has the same purpose.

noi_dung:
THE FIRST CHAPTER - THE PREVIOUS PRINCIPAL OF THE ULTIMATE FUNDAMENTAL TEACHER Amitabha Buddha

The original Master Shakyamuni Buddha has been a historical being in the Saha world. After several thousand years, His image is still deeply imprinted in the memory of mankind, due to stories and relics, especially the brilliant golden strokes in the Tripitaka. Buddha Amitabha Buddha is also a completely historical being in the world of Ultimate Bliss, over several decades, his name forever resounds in the mouths and hearts of all, based on the words of the Master, the true one.

Before the Original Master manifested to attain the Supreme enlightenment at the Bodhi tree, and then became the noble Patriarch of the Saha world, he was the Good Hue Bodhisattva offering flowers and spreading his hair to Buddha Dipankara and the Guardian Bodhisattva residing in the Tusita heaven, etc.

The same is true of the Buddha, before attaining perfect enlightenment and holding the throne of the Dharma King in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, he also had his own human realm: the King of Unavoidable Mindfulness during the period of the Buddha Treasure Store, the Prince of Winning Merit in the Dharma Assembly of the Buddha of the Treasure of Merit, the Bodhisattva Samādi, the son of the Great Wisdom of the Buddha, etc.

Before talking about the Buddha's present body and realm, we need to clearly understand His cause, to know that this Supreme result is all due to the superior cause of the past.

---o0o---

noi_dung:
I- SADI BODHISATTVA

Quoted from the Lotus Sutra

7th Hoa Thanh Du product

The Buddha, Great Wisdom and Victory, when he was still King, had 16 sons. When the King left the throne to become a monk and become a Buddha, 16 princes came to the Dharma Assembly and asked to become monks. After a period of study, the 16 novice monks realized the miraculous truth and were possessed of supernatural powers and wisdom.

After preaching the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma to the crowd in the dharma assembly, the Buddha of Great Wisdom and Victorious Wisdom immediately entered the sevenfold retreat in great concentration.

While the Buddha was sitting quietly in his retreat, the 16 Bodhisattvas and novices all ascended the throne to expound the meaning of the Lotus Sutra to the masses. Each Bodhisattva Saṅshā can save six hundred and eighty thousand billion na-dothas for thousands of people.

Those sixteen novice monks have now all become Buddhas, residing in ashrams in the ten directions of the world. The 16th novice monk who became Buddha in the Saha world was named Shakyamuni. And the 9th person currently becomes a Buddha in the Pure Land world, that is, Amitabha Buddha.

---o0o---

II- Crown Prince Thang Merit

Quoted according to the Sutra

“The One Direction of Bodhisattva Birth”

In the past, there was a Crown Prince named Bat Tu Nghi Thang Cong Duc. At the age of 16, the Crown Prince heard the Sutra "Dharma Origin Da-lani" from the Buddha's Precious Merit of the Star of the Kalpa King Tathagata.

After listening to the Sutra, the Prince diligently practiced for seventy thousand years, not sleeping or resting, nor lying down without support. Thanks to that bravery, the Crown Prince gradually met ninety billions of thousands of Buddhas. No matter how many Dharma teachings the Buddhas teach, the Crown Prince can accept and practice them all. Later, the Prince became a monk, practiced the "Dharma Dharma" for ninety thousand years and preached the Dharma to everyone.

Diligently cultivating and diligently teaching, in one lifetime of propagating the Dharma, the Prince saved eighty billion nadotha people to develop Bodhi mind and stay at the level without turning back.

Crown Prince Thang Cong Duc was the predecessor of Amitabha Buddha.

---o0o---

tieu_de: III- THE KING OF NO THANH NIEM AND THE TWO PRINKS
tom_tat: Countless eons ago, in the world of San De Lam, the son of General Bao Hai became a Buddhist monk, his name was Bao Tang Nhu.
noi_dung:
III- THE KING OF NO THANH NIEM AND THE TWO PRINKS

Quoted from the Bi Hoa Sutra

Countless eons ago, in the world of San De Lam, the son of Deputy Prime Minister Bao Hai became a Buddhist monk, with the name Bao Tang Tathagata.

At that time, King Vo Thanh Niem, along with Deputy General Bao Hai, the Princes and subjects, went to the ashram to make offerings to Buddha Bao Tang.

After listening to the Buddha's teachings, the King and his Deputy Prime Minister simultaneously developed Bodhi mind. The king vowed to dignify the Pure Land to receive sentient beings. The Deputy Prime Minister vowed to become a Buddha in the impure land to subdue all living things. (A)

Buddha Bao Tang said: "Over hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas to the West there is the world of Ton Am King Tathagata. In the next countless kalpas, that world will change its name to Ultimate Bliss; then the king will become a Buddha there with the name Infinite Life Tathagata. And the assistant minister Bao Hai will become a Buddha with the name Shakyamuni in the Saha world."

Quan Phu General is the predecessor of the original Master Shakyamuni Buddha. King Vo Thanh Niem was the predecessor of Tu Phu Amitabha Buddha.

When King Vo Thanh Niem made his vow and received his prediction, Crown Prince Bat Huyen, the king's eldest son, made his vow: "In the future, while I practice Bodhisattva conduct, will any sentient being encounter the terrors of suffering, etc., sad and worried that they have no one to save them, have no place to rely on, that person remembers me, proclaims my name, is heard by my heavenly ears, is seen by my heavenly eyes, if those beings are not freed from the terrors of sufferings, then I swear that I will never become an Enlightened One. And when my father becomes a Buddha in the Pure Land, I will often practice the Bodhisattva path and uphold the Dharma."

Bodhisattva Tathagata said to the Prince: "You observe all sentient beings and have great compassion. You want to end all the suffering of sentient beings, and you want to make all sentient beings happy. Now you should be named Avalokiteśvara. Later, when Infinite Life Buddha enters Nirvana, the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss will be renamed the World of One-Tie-Tie-Treasure-Accomplishment. You will become a Buddha there with the name of Transfiguration of One-Set Light of Merit. Mountain King Tathagata".

At that time, Prince Ni Ma, the king's second son, vowed to dedicate all his merits to Supreme Bodhi, and when Prince Bat Huyen became Buddha, he would be the first Bodhisattva to invite the wheel of Dharma to turn, and would always be by the side of Mountain King Tathagata to help propagate the Buddha.

The Treasure Treasury Tathagata immediately predicted that Prince Ni Ma would have his wish fulfilled. When Mountain King Tathagata entered Nirvana, he would protect the Dharma and eventually become a Buddha in that world, with the name Thien Truong Duc Duc Precious King Tathagata. Brightness, longevity, national salvation, and all Buddha's work are the same as the Mountain King Tathagata.

Prince Bat Huyen was the predecessor of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and Prince Ni Ma was the predecessor of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva.

(A) ADDITIONAL NOTES - Master Lien Tri once said that the Buddha's teachings have two subjects: 1.- Conquering. 2.- Photography.

Buddha taught: These are the three paths and six paths, three realms such as: a house on fire, birth, old age, illness, death, immeasurable suffering, impermanence of birth and death that lurks to harm people, desires and afflictions that cover the human mind, and methods to eliminate suffering, so that people can be bored and leave this impure and miserable body and world, and wish to be freed from etc. This is the discipline of "Conquering".

The Buddha pointed to the Pure Land, which is completely peaceful and happy, the goal of purity and liberation, and the Pure Land dharmas, for those who desire to return; This is the subject "Nhien Tho".

The Great Master's criticism is very consistent with the original vows of the two Buddhas: "Shakyamuni Buddha vows to stay in the impure land to subdue powerful sentient beings. Amitabha Buddha vows to adorn the pure land to take care of pure living beings."

*

And below is the story of a Pure Land monk who personally heard the above words of Duc Tu Phu.

---o0o---

MASTER HUI CANH

Excerpted from the series:

“The Three Jewels of Weak Touch”

Master Hui Canh from Liuzhou, lives at Ngo Chon Pagoda. The monk loved asceticism and the Pure Land. He created two statues of Shakyamuni and Amitabha to make offerings and worship every day.

When he was 67 years old, on the full moon night of the first month, he saw a monk with a golden-colored body appear and say, "Do you want to see the Pure Land?" The Master replied, “I want to see it very much.” The yellow-bodied monk asked again: “Do you want to see the Buddha?”. The Master replied: "I hope to see it." The monk immediately held out his bowl and told him to look. As soon as the monk looked into the bowl, he suddenly saw an extremely solemn and vast realm: the ground was full of pure gold, golden ropes lined the roads, precious nets were covered with golden trees, the palaces and temples were all made of seven brightly shining jewels, the Buddha was preaching the Dharma to countless Bodhisattva Saints.

At that time, the monk with a golden body went first, the monk followed, gradually approaching the Buddha. The monk suddenly disappeared, the monk clasped his hands and stood before the Buddha. The Buddha said: "Do you know who the monk who brought you here is? It is Shakyamuni Buddha! And I am Amitabha Buddha. Shakyamuni is like a father, I am like a mother, sentient beings in Saha are like children. For example, a child falls into a muddy hole, the father wades into the mud to bring the child to shore, the mother picks up the child and brings him back to raise and educate him, so that the child will never be lost or fall into the hole again. Buddha Shakyamuni brought the dharma. The Pure Land sect teaches sentient beings in the impure realms, while I continue to lead sentient beings to the Pure Land to abide without turning back."

After hearing the Buddha's words, his heart was filled with joy, he immediately bowed his head and bowed to the Buddha, but suddenly he could no longer see, like a person waking up from a dream. From then on, the Master believed in the Pure Land even more.

A little while later, the Master again saw the golden-bodied monk from before appear and say: "Twelve years later you will be reborn in the Pure Land."

Indeed, exactly 12 years later, Master Hue Canh passed away. Life expectancy is 79 years old. At the moment of the Master's death, a nearby monk saw countless saints flying from the West to welcome the Master, and everyone heard the melodious music in the sky.

---o0o---

tom_tat: One day, seeing the face of the Master Shakyamuni Buddha, brighter and brighter than usual, Venerable Ananda went to pay homage to the Buddha and asked for his fate.
noi_dung:
IV- Dharma Store Bodhisattva

Quoted according to the Sutra

“Buddhist Theory of Infinite Life”,

also called “Great Amitabha Sutra”

One day, seeing the face of the Master Shakyamuni Buddha, brighter and brighter than usual, Venerable Ananda went to pay homage to the Buddha and asked the reason.

The Master praised the words and questions here, the merit is greater than the merit of making offerings to countless Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, but also greater than the merit of giving alms to countless gods and people and animals for many lifetimes. Because Gods and people, even animals and animals, thanks to this confession, they are liberated by the Dharma.

Then the Master said that today he was thinking about the duties, vows, and virtues of the Lord of the Pure Land, Amitabha Buddha.

The Master continued:

Countless and countless eons ago, at the time when the Buddha Tathagata appeared in the world to teach and transform sentient beings, there was a King who was very pleased to hear the Buddha preach the Dharma. He immediately developed the Bodhi mind, renounced his throne and became a monk with the name of Pharmagarbha.

The monk Phap Tang came to pay his respects to the Buddha, and after chanting and praising the Buddha, he prayed to the Buddha to teach him the virtues of adorning the Pure Land to attract sentient beings, so that he could follow and practice.

Knowing clearly that the monks were highly intelligent and had far-reaching aspirations, Buddha World Self-Consciousness taught the dharma-garbha monks and the right retributions of the two hundred and ten billion worlds, and at the same time showed them all.

After hearing and seeing the solemn retribution of the robes of all countries, the monk Dharma Tang aroused the unsurpassed wish. Then, during the five lifetimes, the meditator chooses to practice solemn, pure Buddha-land deeds. (The Master told Ananda: During that period, the Buddha lived ten lifetimes).

When he finished practicing, monk Phap Tang came to pay homage to the Tathagata and asked the Buddha to witness for him to recite the 48 great vows that he had made an oath to fulfill to help all sentient beings.

When Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva finished making the 48 great vows before the Buddha, The Great Vow, the whole earth trembled, precious flowers rained down on his body, and in the middle of nowhere, music suddenly sounded: "I will definitely become a Buddha."

After that, after countless countless kalpas, Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva practiced and completely fulfilled the above vows, and the person who has become a Buddha for ten kalpas now is named Amitabha, and is currently preaching the Dharma in the Pure Land, ten thousand billion realms to the West.

---o0o---

tom_tat: The Sanskrit word Buddha, we often call Buddha, means the enlightened one (Enlightened One): here, the "self-realization", "enlightenment of others" and the act of enlightenment have been brought to perfection. To put it more clearly, that is, the enlightened person grasps the truth...
noi_dung:
CHAPTER TWO - TITLE

The Sanskrit word Buddha (Buddha), we often call Buddha, means the enlightened one (Enlightened One): here, “self-realization”, “enlightenment of others” and the deeds of enlightenment have reached their ultimate fulfillment. To put it more clearly, that is, the person who has awakened to the self accepts the principle of emptiness, puts an end to all negative thoughts and afflictions, and liberates the part of birth and death; Different from ordinary pagans who still have wrong views, delusion and attachment to self, creating afflictions and creating karma that forever sinks into the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death. And the one who has awakened to the Dharma accepts the Dharma of Emptiness, destroys ignorance, and completely escapes suffering and change; Unlike Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas who still cling to the Dharma, their true nature is obscured by ignorance, forever trapped in the cycle of suffering. But it is also different from Bodhisattvas, because even though Bodhisattvas have realized the truth, they have not yet reached perfection, even though they have broken through delusion, they have not yet ended it, while Buddhas have reached ultimate perfection.

According to the above meanings, the Buddha should be called the Unsurpassed (for Bodhisattvas) Complete (for the Second Vehicle) Enlightened (for ordinary, evil and foreign people). This is the noun Anuttara Sammyak Sambuddha that the Sutras always talk about. And it is also necessary to understand the meaning of the ten names: Tathagata, Sacrificial Offering, Perfectly Enlightened Knowledge, Perfection of Wisdom and Conduct, Good Tathagata, Understanding of the World, Supreme Being, Regulator of Men, Master of Heaven and Humanity, World-Honored Buddha. Only then can we clearly understand the Buddha's virtue and wisdom.

Respect for the Buddha is an important thing to have in people chanting Buddha's name. If you want to have true respect, you must accept the Buddha's noble views. So readers need to research thoroughly.

The above nouns are the common names of Buddhas. Now we discuss the nickname of Duc Tu Phu.

Sanskrit Amita. We read the camp Amitabha, which means Immeasurable.

In the Amitabha Sutra, the Buddha once defined the Buddha's name for the sake of the masses: "Sariputra! Why is that Buddha called Amitabha? Sariputra! That Buddha has immeasurable light, illuminating the ten directions without obstruction, so his name is Amitabha. That Buddha and the people in his country, whose lifespan is boundless and limitless asamyakalpas, should be called Amitabha."

Because of immeasurable light and immeasurable lifespan, in the Sutras Amitabha Buddha is called the Immeasurable Light Buddha ( Avatamsaka Sutra, etc.) and in some places it is also called the Immeasurable Life Buddha (Immeasurable Life Sutra, etc.).

In the Sutra "Buddha's Teaching of Infinite Life", the Master told Ananda: Amitabha Buddha has the most supreme and supreme divine power and light, the light of all Buddhas is unmatched, that is why Amitabha Buddha has 12 separate names:

1. Infinite Light Tathagata

2 Boundless Light Tathagata

3. Unobstructed Light Tathagata

4. Unmatched Light Tathagata

5. Diem Vuong Quang Tathagata

6. Tathagata Pure Light

7. Joyful Light Tathagata

8. Tathagata's Light Wisdom

9. Nan Tu Quang Tathagata

10. Unbroken Light Tathagata

11. Unworthy Light Tathagata

12. Super Sun Moon Light Tathagata
