tom_tat: During the period of cultivating humanity, our Compassionate Father, because of his great compassion for all sentient beings, not only wanted to make sure that all sentient beings are free from all suffering, but also weighed heavily with the concept: Let all sentient beings live forever in...
noi_dung:
CHAPTER THREE - HAPPY PRAYERS AND GREAT HAPPINESS

Narrated according to the Infinite Life Sutra

During the period of cultivating humanity, our Compassionate Father, because of his great compassion for all sentient beings, not only wanted to make sure that all sentient beings were free from all suffering, but also weighed heavily with the concept: So that all sentient beings can live forever in complete peace and happiness and be firmly assured on the path to Buddhahood.

Because of this concept of great kindness, when I was still a Bodhisattva, my Compassionate Father always guarded my heart with an unchangeable will: To create an extremely solemn, pure and joyful world, to be the home of all species, of all sentient beings in the ten directions.

That noble mind of great compassion caused King Vo Avoid Niem (the predecessor of Tu Father) to make a vow in the Treasure Store Tathagata, and also made the monk Phap Tang earnestly request that the Tathagata, the Self-sufficient King, manifest the two hundred and ten million worlds of the Buddhas of the ten directions for people to see and hear, and then he selected and selected only the purest solemnities in those worlds, to unite them into a Pure Land of the Buddhas. later people. And immediately, for a period of five lives, he diligently contemplated the deeds that must be practiced to realize that Pure Land.

This selection and meditation resulted in 48 propagating vows, which he solemnly proclaimed, under the testimony of Lord Buddha Tathagata.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Because of these 48 vows, the Buddha has good relationships with sentient beings in the ten directions, especially the impure, impure, and suffering realms. Reading and meditating carefully will bring you many great benefits
noi_dung:
I - HOANG NGUYEN

Because of these 48 vows, the Buddha has good relationships with sentient beings in the ten directions, especially the impure, impure, and suffering realms. Reading and meditating carefully will bring you many great benefits:

A. The trust in Duc Tu Father is deeper.

B. Growth of Bodhi mind

C. Clearly understand the solemn realm in the Pure Land.

D. Understand the noble characteristics of the Pure Land people.

E. Passionate about the Pure Land and enthusiastic about practicing.

Because of these many great benefits, Co Duc attached great importance to these 48 great vows. Some people know it by heart, some people worship it diligently. I hope readers will try to get past this boring concept.

1st vow.- When I become Buddha, if in my land there are hells, hungry ghosts, and animals, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

The 2nd vow.- When I become Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land fall into the three evil paths after receiving their last life, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

The 3rd vow.- When I become Buddha, if all the human beings and gods in my land are not all pure gold in color, then I will not be in perfect enlightenment.

The 4th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land have different bodies, good and bad, then I will not be in the position of Enlightenment.

The 5th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land do not have the ability to attain full life, at least clearly know the things of hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of nadotha kalpas, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 6.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land do not have the heavenly eye, at least the ability to clearly see hundreds of thousands of kotis of Buddhas' worlds, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

The 7th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land do not have the heavenly ear, at least to hear and accept all the teachings of hundreds of thousands of billions of kotis of na-dotha Buddhas, then I will not be in the position of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 8.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land are not spared their minds, or at least clearly know the thoughts of all living beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of nadotha worlds, then I will not be in the state of Perfect Enlightenment.

The 9th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land do not receive divine sustenance, for at least one thought, at least a glimpse of hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of na-dotha worlds, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

The 10th Vow.- When I become Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land still have the concept of attachment to the body, then I will not be in the position of Perfect Enlightenment.

The 11th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if all the human beings and gods in my land do not maintain perfect concentration and persevere until nirvana, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

12th vow.- When I become Buddha, if my light is still limited, at least it cannot penetrate hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of Na-do-tha worlds, then I will not be in the position of Perfect Enlightenment.

The 13th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if my life span is limited, at least not hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of kalpas, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

The 14th vow.- When I become a Buddha, if anyone in my land can calculate and count the number, even if it is countless Pratyekabuddhas counting in hundreds of thousands of kalpas, then I will not be at the Enlightenment.

Vow 15. - When I become a Buddha, if the lifespan of all human beings in my land is limited, except for those who have their own original vows, then I will not be in the position of Perfect Enlightenment.

Vow 16.- When I become a Buddha, if there are people in my land who hear the word unwholesome, then I will not be in the position of Enlightenment.

Vow 17.- When I become a Buddha, if the countless Buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions do not all praise and call my name, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 18.- When I become a Buddha, sentient beings from the ten directions who wholeheartedly believe and wish to be born in my land must endure ten recitations. If I am not born, then I will not be in the Enlightenment position, except for those who commit the five transgressions and slander the Dharma.

Vow 19.- When I become a Buddha, sentient beings in the ten directions will develop the Bodhi mind and practice the merits, vowing to be born in my land. At the time of death, if I do not appear before that person with the great assembly, then I will not be in perfect enlightenment.

20th Vow.- When I become a Buddha, sentient beings in the ten directions will hear my name, remember my land and practice the merits wholeheartedly to dedicate to be born in my land. If my wish is not fulfilled, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

The 21st vow.- When I become a Buddha, if all the human beings and gods in my land do not all have thirty-two great human appearances, then I will not be in the position of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 22.- When I become a Buddha, all Bodhisattvas in other realms will be born in my country, with the ultimate goal of reaching the First Being, except those who have their own original vows to freely manifest, for the sake of all sentient beings, to spread the vow to practice the merits of liberating all sentient beings, to travel throughout the worlds to practice the Bodhisattva conduct, to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, to enlighten countless sentient beings, to make all stand firmly on the path of Supreme Enlightenment, to excel in meritorious deeds. of ordinary people, now practice Samantabhadra's virtues. If not like that, then I will not be at the level of Perfect Enlightenment.

Vow 23.- When I become a Buddha, the Bodhisattvas in my land, with the Buddha's divine power, will go and make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. In the span of one meal, if I do not reach all countless countless billions of nadotha worlds, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

The 24th vow.- When I become a Buddha, the Bodhisattvas in my land, when in front of the ten directions the Buddhas show their merits, want to have offerings. If I do not get what I want, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

Vow 25.- When I become a Buddha, if the Bodhisattvas in my land cannot expound Omniscience, then I will not be in perfect enlightenment.

Vow 26.- When I become a Buddha, if the Bodhisattvas in my land do not all have a vajra body, then I will not be in the state of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 27.- When I become a Buddha, in my land, all human and heavenly objects, shapes and forms will be bright, beautiful, clean, extremely wonderful, impossible to know, even if one has the heavenly eye. If there were someone who could clearly state the number of those objects, then I would not be in the state of Enlightenment.

Vow 28.- When I become a Buddha, if the Bodhisattva in my land, even if he is the one with the least merit, cannot see and know the ashram tree four hundred thousand yojanas high and immeasurable in light and color, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

Vow 29.- When I become a Buddha, if the Bodhisattvas in my land receive, uphold, read, recite, and preach the Dharma without gaining wisdom and eloquence, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

30th Vow.- When I become a Buddha, if anyone can limit the wisdom and eloquence of Bodhisattvas in my land, then I will not be in the Enlightenment position.

31st Vow.- When I become a Buddha, my land will be pure, and everywhere I can see all the immeasurable, countless, immeasurable worlds in the ten directions, like seeing my face in a bright mirror. If that were not possible, then I would not be in the state of Enlightenment.

32nd Vow.- When I become Buddha, in my land from the golden ground to the void, palaces, water ponds, flowers and trees, all things will be immeasurable precious substances and hundreds of thousands of fragrances combined to form. All things are wonderfully beautiful, the fragrance pervades the worlds of the ten directions, and Bodhisattvas everywhere smell that fragrance and practice the Buddha's practice. If it weren't like that, I wouldn't be at Enlightenment.

Vow 33.- When I become Buddha, all sentient beings in the immeasurable worlds in the ten directions will be touched by my light, and their bodies and minds will be softer and gentler than the gods. If it weren't like that, then I wouldn't be in the position of Enlightenment.

Vow 34.- When I become a Buddha, if all sentient beings in the immeasurable worlds in the ten directions hear my name but do not receive the Dharma of No Birth and the profound teachings, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

35th Vow.- When I become a Buddha, all the women in the countless and immeasurable councils in the ten directions will rejoice, believe, love, and develop the Bodhi mind, and will hate the body of women. If, after my death, I were to take on the body of a woman again, then I would not be in perfect enlightenment.

Vow 36.- When I become a Buddha, the Bodhisattvas in the immeasurable worlds in the ten directions will hear my name and continue to practice holy conduct until they become Buddhas. If it were not so, then I would not be in the position of perfect enlightenment.

Vow 37.- When I become a Buddha, all the human beings and gods in the immeasurable and immeasurable worlds in the ten directions hear my name, bow their heads, bow their heads, plant their five limbs on the ground, joyfully believe and practice the Bodhisattva conduct, then the gods and people will respect that person. If it weren't like that, then I wouldn't be in the position of Enlightenment.

Vow 38.- When I become a Buddha, every human being in my land wants to have clothes. Good and dharma-compliant clothes will naturally come to the body according to that person's thoughts. If I still have to cut, sew, dye and wash, then I will not be in the state of Enlightenment.

Vow 39.- When I become a Buddha, if the human beings and gods in my land enjoy joy unlike those of Bhikkhus, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

40th Vow.- When I become a Buddha, the Bodhisattvas in my land can see the immeasurable pure worlds of the Buddhas in the ten directions at will, and will immediately be able to see clearly the entire place within the jeweled tree according to their wishes, like seeing their own faces in a bright mirror. If it weren't like that, then I wouldn't be in the position of Enlightenment.

Vow 41.- When I become a Buddha, Bodhisattvas in other worlds will hear my name. From then on, until I become a Buddha, if my physical faculties are still lacking and bad, then I will not be in the position of Perfect Enlightenment.

Vow 42.- When I become Buddha, when Bodhisattvas in other worlds hear my name, they will all be liberated from Samadhi. That Samadhi, in the space of one thought, makes immeasurable offerings to the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, without losing right concentration. If it were not like that, then I would not be in the state of Enlightenment.

Vow 43.- When I become a Buddha, Bodhisattvas in other directions will hear my name. After my death, I will be reborn in a noble family. If that is not the case, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

Vow 44.- When I become a Buddha, Bodhisattvas in other directions will be happy and joyful when they hear my name and practice Bodhisattva conduct with full merit. Otherwise, I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

Vow 45.- When I become a Buddha, the Bodhisattvas in other directions who hear my name will all attain Universal Samadhi, stay in this Samadhi until I become Buddha, and often see immeasurable and impartial views of all Buddhas. If it were not so, then I would not be in the state of Enlightenment.

Vow 46.- When I become a Buddha, whatever Dharma the Bodhisattvas in my land want to hear will naturally be able to hear that Dharma. If it weren't like that, then I wouldn't be in the position of Enlightenment.

Vow 47.- When I become a Buddha, if Bodhisattvas in other worlds hear my name but do not reach the state of irreversibility, then I will not be in the state of Perfect Enlightenment.

Vow 48.- When I become a Buddha, if the Bodhisattvas in other worlds hear my name and do not immediately attain the first stage of Renunciation of Sound, the second stage of Forbearance, the third stage of Non-birth Dharma forbearance, and in the Buddhadharma do not immediately attain the state of non-regression, then I will not attain perfect enlightenment.

---o0o---

tom_tat: In the Infinite Life Sutra, after narrating the 48 vows of Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva, the Buddha continued.
noi_dung:
II - DAI HANH

In the Infinite Life Sutra, after recounting the 48 vows of Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva, the Master continued:

After making this vow, Phap Tang Bodhisattva focused on solemnizing the pure land. The land of the cultivator is very vast and beautiful, superior to all, always established, unfailing, unchanging. During the immeasurable time of countless kalpas, one cultivates immeasurable Mahayana virtues. No remembrance : desire, anger, harm. Never indulge in the six senses: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma. People who achieve patience do not count hardship. People always have few desires and are content: no greed, no anger, no ignorance. The human mind is usually quiet in right concentration, with unobstructed wisdom. People never have the heart to lie. His facial expression is always happy, his words are gentle, and he warmly asks questions. The aspiration to always be diligent and courageous is never tiring: one who diligently seeks the perfect dharma to benefit all sentient beings. People pay respect to the Three Jewels. With the Master, he worshiped. He uses his great, dignified and perfect deeds to help sentient beings achieve merit. People who observe all dharmas are like illusions, like transformations, uncreated, unborn, always remaining in the door of liberation: empty, formless, wishless. He is far away from harsh words: harming oneself, harming others, harming oneself and others. People who practice fully should speak kindly: benefit themselves, benefit others, benefit others. People throw away wealth and stay away from material things. He practices the six paramitas: almsgiving, precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, wisdom, and teaches everyone to practice. He who educates and establishes countless sentient beings so that they all stand firmly on the path of Supreme Enlightenment. For the sake of saving sentient beings, he incarnates in all species, with the same body, with the same language, to guide and guide...

Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva has such countless merits that it is impossible to count them all. The person who carried out and completed the vows he had made: He became a Buddha with the name Amitabha in the Pure Land world, ten thousand billion realms to the West, and is currently preaching there...

ADDITIONAL WORDS.- Of the 48 vows, each vow has the same great compassionate purpose:

Make sentient beings live forever in a state of complete happiness and ensure certainty on the path to Buddhahood.

When it comes to the great act of helping others to fulfill the above four vows, in that, there is so much bravery and diligence, so much patience and hard work. How can you describe the place of pure conduct! Told how noble wisdom is! No hardship, no toil. It's about doing things that are difficult to do, tolerating things that are difficult to endure.

Why do we have to spend countless lifetimes practicing the Bodhisattva conduct like that while cultivating humanity? Just for sentient beings! Because to save suffering and bring happiness to all living beings, just for us!

We already know about the virtues of the Father. Now we should read the pages of the Sutra, where our Master preaches about Tu Father's earth.

A. The outstanding physical appearance of Amitabha Buddha and his two supporting Bodhisattvas.

B. The solemn Pure Land scene: "World of Ultimate Bliss".

---o0o---

CHAPTER FOUR - THE BODY OF THE GENERAL

Below is the narration according to the words of the Original Master Shakyamuni Buddha in the Infinite Life Sutra, Infinite Life Contemplation Sutra, and Amitabha Buddha Sutra.

tieu_de: I - THE GOOD PRIMARY OF Amitabha Buddha
tom_tat: Amitabha Buddha's body is like hundreds of thousands of billions of times the golden color of the Da Ma heaven, sixty thousand billions of billions of na-dothas in height, thousands of thousands of miles long. The white hair between the eyebrows gracefully swirls to the right like five Tu mountains...
noi_dung:
I - THE GOOD PRIMARY OF Amitabha Buddha

Amitabha Buddha's body is like hundreds of thousands of billions of times the golden color of the Da Ma heaven, sixty thousand billions of billions of na-dothas in height, thousands of thousands of miles long. The white hair between the eyebrows gracefully swirls to the right like the five mountains Meru. His white and blue eyes were as clear as the four oceans. The pores in the body emit light like Mount Meru. The Buddha's light is like hundreds of billions of Great Thousand realms. In the light there are hundreds of millions of Na-do-tha, countless countless Buddhas. Each Buddha has countless Bodhisattvas following him.

The Buddha's body has eighty-four thousand good appearances, each of which has eighty-four thousand good appearances. Each perfect image has eighty-four thousand rays of light. Each ray of light shines throughout the ten directions of the world, capturing the Buddha-reciting sentient beings without leaving them.

The beauty of the rays of light, along with the Buddha Transformation, cannot be described in words...

If you want to visualize the Buddha's good appearance, you should first visualize the white hair between the eyebrows. If the appearance of white hair appears clearly, then many other good appearances will appear one after another.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is the great Bodhisattva who often attends the left side of the Buddha, and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, the winged one. The two Great Monks help the Buddha in the teachings of the world, and spread themselves throughout the ten directions to save all suffering...
noi_dung:
II - Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva

Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is the great Bodhisattva who often attends the left side of the Buddha, and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, the winged one. The two Great Monks help the Buddha with teachings in the world, and spread themselves throughout the ten directions to save the suffering of all living beings, and receive people with pure destiny to the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Below is the Bodhisattva's true form, narrated according to the Infinite Life Sutra. In addition, other forms, as ordinary people perceive, are all bodies that appear according to the feelings of sentient beings.

Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara's body is eighty billion nadotha yojanas tall, and his skin is purple-gold. On the top of the head there is a humiliating plan. There is a circular halo of light on each side that is hundreds of thousands of yojanas wide. In that round halo of light there were five hundred Transformation Buddhas, each Transformation Buddha's appearance was as good as Shakyamuni Buddha, and there were five hundred Transformation Bodhisattvas waiting.

The entire body of light shines throughout the ten directions, and the forms of all living beings in the six paths are clearly reflected in that light.

Above the Bodhisattva's head is a heavenly coffin. In the celestial palace there was a Buddha who was twenty-five yojanas tall.

The Bodhisattva's face is golden yellow.

The white hair between the eyebrows is full of seven beautiful precious colors, radiating eighty-four thousand kinds of rays of light penetrating all ten directions. In each ray of light there are countless Buddhas and countless Bodhisattvas.

The Bodhisattva's arms were as colored as pink lotuses, with eighty billions of beautiful rays of light woven into a string of pearls. The five hundred thousand hands are the color of pink lotus flowers. The fingertips have eighty-four thousand lines. Each line has eighty-four thousand rays of light. That ray of light gently illuminates the ten directions.

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva uses this precious hand to lead sentient beings to the Pure Land.

When the Bodhisattva raised his foot, from the place of thousands of vortices on the soles of his feet, it naturally transformed into five hundred billion bright light platforms. When Bodhisattva put his feet down, wish-fulfilling diamond flowers were suddenly sprinkled everywhere.

If you want to contemplate the Bodhisattva's good appearance, you should start by contemplating the heavenly body first, then gradually contemplate the other appearances...

---o0o---

tom_tat: The body size of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva is the same as the body size of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. The light in the neck is 125 yojanas wide on each side and shines 250 yojanas away. The light of the entire body is purple-gold, illuminating the ten directions...
noi_dung:
III - THE GREAT BODHISATTVA BODHISATTVA

The body size of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva is the same as the body size of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. The light in the neck is 125 yojanas wide on each side and shines 250 yojanas away. The light of the entire body is purple-gold and shines through the ten directions of the world, and those who are predestined can see it. Just seeing the light in a single pore of the Bodhisattva, immediately sees the pure and wonderful light of countless Buddhas in the ten directions. Therefore, the Bodhisattva's name is Boundless Light.

Bodhisattva uses the light of wisdom to shine on all living things, causing sentient beings to escape the three paths to become supremely powerful, so he is called Great World Will.

Bodhisattva's heavenly organ has five hundred precious flowers. Each flower treasure has five hundred jewels. The appearances of the pure worlds of the Buddhas in the ten directions are clearly visible in each palace.

On top of the head, thistle is shaped like a pink lotus flower. On the next step there is a treasured vase full of light. The light in the vase radiates out into Buddha's deeds. In addition, other good appearances are similar to Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.

When Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva left, it shook the worlds of the ten directions. At the same place where the earthquake occurred, there were five hundred million precious flowers. Each flower is as noble and dignified as the Pure Land world.

When the Bodhisattva sat, the entire Pure Land shook at the same time. From the world of Vajra Buddha in the Lower direction to the world of Lord Buddha of Light in the Upper direction, in which countless earthly incarnations of Amitayus Buddha, Avalokiteśvara's and Mahasthamaprapta's clones all gather in the Pure Land world, crowded into space. Each avatar sits on a precious lotus throne, performing in unison, speaking wonderful Dharma, saving sentient beings...

---o0o---

MR. LY TRIEU DAI

Ly Trieu Dai was from Ung Chau. He believed in Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva very much and diligently recited Buddha's name.

His father did not believe in Buddhism and rejected it. Not long after, his father suddenly fell ill and died.

Mr. Dai mounted the three-meter-tall gold statue of Mahasthamaprapta to pray for the salvation of his father's soul. The day the statue began to be built, the whole ground suddenly trembled.

Two months later, the statue was completed. That night, while sleeping, Mr. Dai saw a golden-colored body with a heavenly crown on his head and said: "Do you know why the earth trembled the other day? I am the Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva. You ascended the bone statue, so I came to prove it. When I walked, the whole world shook. Many sentient beings in the evil realms were freed from suffering. I rely on the method of reciting the Buddha's name to attain the patience of non-birth, capturing sentient beings reciting the Buddha's name in the ten directions. Thanks to you ascending the bone statue and Diligently chanting Buddha's name, your father was released from hell, I will lead you by the hand to the Pure Land."

After listening to the Bodhisattva's teachings, Mr. Dai quickly bowed his head in respect. Suddenly woke up. In my heart, I was filled with joy and emotion. From then on his meditation became more diligent.

--- o0o ---

CHAPTER FIFTH - COUNTRY

Quoted from the “Infinite Life” Sutras,

“Amitage of Infinite Life”, “Amitabha”

WORLD BLISS

Identification : In the Jetavana Assembly, the Master Shakyamuni Buddha told Sariputta: "Why is that realm called Ultimate Bliss?". Then the Master explained himself: "Because the sentient beings in that world do not have suffering, they only enjoy pure joy, so it is called Ultimate Bliss."

---o0o---

tom_tat: The entire Pure Land, the land of crystal clear glass. Below is a supporting diamond rosary. That diamond necklace has eight regular roots, each face has a hundred kinds of jewels. Each jewel releases thousands of rays of light. Each ray of light has 84,000 colors, dazzling...
noi_dung:
A - SCENE

1. SECURITY

The entire Pure Land, the land of crystal clear glass. Below is a supporting diamond rosary. That diamond necklace has eight regular roots, each side has hundreds of gems. Each jewel releases thousands of rays of light. Each ray of light has 84,000 colors, dazzling lapis lazuli as bright as thousands of billions of suns. The lapis lazuli surface is flat, with pure gold wires and seven precious stones strung up to divide the area and roads. Each precious string radiates light of a hundred colors. That ray of light looks like a flower, like a star, like the moon, shining up and forming a bright platform in the middle of the sky. Next to those bright platforms are hundreds of millions of flower garlands, along with countless musical instruments. From the bright platform blew eight cool breezes, causing the musical instruments to vibrate and ring out the Dharma-speaking voices "Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, Selflessness, Compassion, Joy and Equanimity, the Paramitas".

---o0o---

2. BAO THO

On the Treasure Land, there are countless Sandalwood Trees, countless Auspicious Fruit trees, in straight rows, with branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all neatly arranged. Each tree is 8,000 yojanas tall. Stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all seven treasures. Or a tree that is pure gold, pure silver, pure lapis lazuli, pure crystal, pure sapphire, pure agate, pure pearls. Or a tree with a golden root and a silver trunk, with branches and leaves and fruits that are also divided into gold and silver. This is a tree of two precious qualities. There is a tree with a golden root, silver trunk, lapis lazuli branches, and leaves and fruit with gold, silver, and lapis lazuli. This is a tree of three precious qualities. Or the type of tree with four precious qualities, the type with five precious qualities, the type with six precious qualities, the type with seven precious qualities, are also mixed together to form.

All the Buddha's deeds in the Pure Land are clearly reflected in the tree, and the entire world of the ten directions are also clearly reflected in the tree, like in a bright mirror.

Each leaf is 25 yojanas wide, a thousand colors, and emits beautiful light, making the leaf veins like a string of pearls.

Beautiful, match-yellow flowers are interspersed among the leaves, shining like rings of fire. On the natural flower there are seven precious fruits that look like the precious vase of the Heavenly Emperor. From the left, great light is emitted, condensing into countless phantoms and treasures. In that treasure, all the Buddha's things in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and all the worlds of the ten directions shine through.

Seven layers of net made of wonderful pearls are spread over each treasure. Each grid has a beautiful palace like Pham Vuong's heavenly palace. In the natural palace there are Heavenly Bronzes. Each Thien Dong wears a string of five hundred Mani pearls. Each seed of Mani shines a hundred yojanas, making the tree shine like a hundred billion suns and moons united.

---o0o---

3. MAINTENANCE

The Pure Land world has bathing ponds everywhere. The pond wall is made of seven precious stones. The bottom of the pond is covered with multi-colored diamond sand. The pond is hundreds of thousands of yojanas wide and looks like the ocean.

Each pond has sixty billion seven-jeweled lotus flowers. Each large round flower is 12 yojanas long, with all beautiful colors, each color radiating different colors of light. In the pond, the water of the bowl of merit comes from the wish-fulfilling pearl king, the color of seven jewels, rising and falling along the lotus stem flowing into the flower petals. The ethereal sound of flowing water demonstrates the magic of Dharma: Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, Anatta, the Paramitas.

Where the wish-fulfilling pearl king radiates pure golden light. In the light, they transformed into beautiful birds of all colors, flying, singing gracefully, speaking Dharma: Five Senses, Five Powers, Seven Bodhisattvas, Eightfold Path, praising the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.

The surface of the water, the ripples, appeared many gentle voices: the voices of Buddha, Dharma, Sangha; the sound of Emptiness, Selflessness, Great Compassion; Paramita; the sound of ten powers, no fear, no community; the sound of supernatural powers and wisdom; the sound of no creation, no birth and death, no birth and patience; endure the sound of nectar empowerment, along with boundless wonderful dharmas. People who hear these sounds will immediately have a pure mind, mature good roots, and will not regress in the path of Supreme Bodhi.

The noble people, people of Ultimate Bliss, when entering the pond to bathe, if they wish to reach their feet, the water will only cover their feet. If they wish the water reaches their stomach, the water will reach their waist, and if they wish the water reaches their neck, the water will rise up to their neck. The pond water depends on each person's wishes, being deep and shallow, warm and cool, and very comfortable. The person bathing, the body feels light and refreshed, the mind is happy and calm and clear.

---o0o---

4. BAO LAU

On all four sides of the treasure pond, the steps and roads are made up of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, etc. There are countless palaces above.

These castles are all made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, etc., with countless precious substances.

The lecture halls, monasteries, palaces of Amitabha Buddha, the Bodhisattvas, and the people are hundreds of thousands of times more precious than the palace of the Heavenly King of Liberty in this Saha world.

In those temples, there are things floating in the middle like clouds, growing and growing depending on the wishes of the residents. There are people who do not follow their will but stay on the treasured ground. Whether the practice is profound or less profound, the place of residence is so different. But the benefits such as clothing, etc. are all equal.

All four sides of the temple are solemn with flower garlands and countless musical instruments. The cool breeze gently vibrated those musical instruments in harmony to form the sound of Dharma: Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, Selflessness, Compassion, Joy and Equanimity, the Paramitas.

---o0o---

5. SECURITY

In the world of Ultimate Bliss, Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and people all sit on precious lotus thrones. Those lotus flowers, from one precious substance, two precious substances, together to countless precious substances, have strangely beautiful colors, bright light, large and small according to the body of the person sitting.

Below is the Buddha's precious lotus throne.

This lotus has 84,000 petals. Each wing is 250 yojanas wide, 100 colors. On each lotus petal there are 84,000 veins emitting 84,000 rays of light. Included in each lotus petal are hundreds of billions of pearls

Mani. Each Mani pearl emits thousands of rays of light. These light rays gather together like a parasol.

The lotus stem is made of Sakyamuni Bhikkhu. Adorned with eight thousand kinds of diamonds, mani gems, and net curtains made of pearls.

On the lotus base, there are naturally four treasured pillars. Each treasure pillar is as tall and beautiful as hundreds of thousands of millions of millions of Mount Meru. On top of the four treasured pillars, a veil of treasured nets is spread as wide as the Da Ma heaven. That precious net contained five hundred million pearls. Each jewel emits 84,000 rays of light. Each ray of light has 84,000 types of gold. Those golden colors shine all over the surface of the treasure, everywhere transforming into different appearances: or turning into diamond platforms, or turning into pearl nets, or turning into bright clouds of beautiful flowers, etc., manifesting Buddha's work everywhere in the Pure Land...

When he finished teaching about the great beauty and wonder of the precious lotus, the Master concluded that: that precious lotus came to be because of the power of the previous incarnation of Amitabha Buddha, Bodhisattva Phap Tang.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Every body that exists is initially placed in one place by consciousness. Different from people of the Saha world who live in their mother's womb, people who practice pure karma when reborn in the Pure Land world will have their body placed in a precious lotus flower in a protected place...
noi_dung:
B - PEOPLE

1. LEN FLOWER HOA SANH

Every body that exists is initially placed in one place by consciousness. Different from people in the Saha world who enter their mother's womb, those who practice pure karma when reborn in the Pure Land world will have their bodies placed in the precious lotus where they are preserved and transformed. Pure Land Luan says: “The pure people of Amitabha Buddha were born from the precious flower of wisdom and enlightenment.”

When the Buddha and Bodhisattva's consciousness is taken to the Pure Land, it is immediately attached to the lotus flower. When the flower still has buds, it is called being in the lotus state. Even though the body has not yet emerged from the flower bud, the sights and enjoyments within the flower are already more joyful than the heavens in Saha.

The precious flowers that are born are different in their preciousness and beauty, and the time they bloom is not the same. That is because the merit and wisdom of each consciousness that is born are not the same in terms of silver and depth.

Due to this discrepancy, the Pure Land world has nine tiers of lotus flowers: three tiers Upper, three tiers Middle, three tiers Lower.

The top three levels of lotus flowers are made of diamond, purple gold, or purple gold. The time the flower blooms is as soon as it blooms, or every other night, or a day and a night. This is the portion of those who, before rebirth, practice the Mahayana practice, develop Bodhi mind, deeply understand the wonderful principle of non-birth, self-transform others, have great merit, have deep wisdom, and dedicate the vow to be born in the Pure Land.

The six grades below the lotus flower are made of seven-jeweled material. Time for flowers to bloom: either bloom continuously, or seven days and nights, or twenty-one days or forty-nine days, etc.

The three intermediate level lotus flowers are the portion of men who are strictly precepted, filial people, and philanthropists, who who wholeheartedly seek the Pure Land.

The three lower levels are the portion of those who do not know how to practice, do not know how to do good, to those who are in an evil life, when they are about to die, when they are dying, they know how to repent of their sins and then wholeheartedly recite "Namo Amitabha Buddha" earnestly seeking rebirth in the Pure Land.

Just by looking at the nine-level lotus flower here, one can see that the World of Ultimate Bliss is the home of all Saints and mortals in the ten directions. Not only is it the ashram of Mahayana Bodhisattvas, of great-minded Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, of those who diligently practice, of philanthropists who do good and avoid evil, but the Pure Land of Bliss is also the home of criminals; patience with all species. If anyone firmly believes in reciting the Buddha's name and then dedicates it to seek rebirth, they will all be able to return home, thanks to the power of receiving and guiding the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas. Except for those who commit the five transgressions and slander the Dharma. After being reborn in the Pure Land, he became a good person, lived in a state of non-regression, and attended the sea assembly.

In the Pure Land, people are born from lotus flowers. Buddha, Bodhisattva and people all sit on precious lotus thrones. That's why the Ancient Ones called the Pure Land world "Lien Ban" (lotus realm), called the Holy Assembly "Lien Tri Hai Hoi" called the Pure Land sect "Lien Tong", called the Buddha recitation assembly "Lien Xa", called Buddha recitation friends "Lien Huu" (lotus friends).

---o0o---

2. BODY

The people of the Pure Land world, with diamond bodies born from precious lotus flowers, have skin the color of gold. Everyone has the 32 characteristics of great humanity and is equally beautiful.

The Master once asked Venerable Ananda: "Like a beggar standing next to the Emperor, are the images of two people the same?"

The Venerable replied: "World-Honored One! The image of a beggar is ugly and dirty, and cannot compare to the Emperor."

The Master said: "Even though the Emperor is beautiful and luxurious, compared to the Holy King of Chakravarti, he is like a beggar. The hundred thousand times the beauty of the Holy King of Chakravarti is not as good as the Heavenly Deity Thich. The hundreds of thousands of times the beauty of the Heavenly Deity Sakyamuni is not as good as the Heavenly King of Self-Satisfaction. The hundred thousand times the beauty of the Heavenly King of Self-Satisfaction is not as good as the Supreme Good People in the Pure Land, the people of Amitabha Buddha."

---o0o---

3. PURE HAPPINESS WITHOUT SUFFERING

The people of the Pure Land world do not have all suffering, they only enjoy pure joy.

The sufferings of all living beings are immeasurable. In short, there are eight things:

1.- Suffering at birth. 2.- Suffering when old and weak. 3.- Suffering when sick. 4.- Suffering about death. 5.- Suffering from having to separate from loved ones. 6.- Suffering from encountering enemies. 7.- Suffering because of not being satisfied. 8.- Suffering because the body and mind demand indulgence.

In the world of Ultimate Bliss, people born from precious lotus flowers are not "born in suffering". The diamond body is always young and beautiful, it is not "suffering from old age" and is not "suffering from illness". To live a life span of immeasurable, boundless asang-kalpas until the land of attaining Buddhahood is without "death and suffering". Without parents, wife and children, there is no "love and separation from suffering". All good people often gather together, so there is no "resentment and suffering". If you pray for anything or any object, you will immediately be satisfied, then you will not "seek without suffering". Without self-view but the mind is always pure, there is no "five skandhas and suffering".

What suffering can there be in the world, where the solemnity and purity have reached its ultimate destination!

In the Pure Land world, in addition to material pleasures such as clothes, bathing ponds, houses, etc., the people of Pure Land also enjoy rare and noble joys:

1.- Buddha is often seen near Buddha. 2.- Great Bodhisattvas are teachers and friends in the same association. 3.- Always listen to the teachings of the Dharma, no matter where or when, if you want to listen. 4.- Often protected by Buddhas. 5.- Live for countless eons together with Buddha. 6.- No longer worry about falling into evil realms. In Ultimate Bliss, the word evil path is not even a reality! 7.- Forever escape from reincarnation. 8.- Enjoy life naturally, avoid being busy and procrastinating in practicing the religion. 9.- Entering the stage of right concentration and no longer regressing from the seven Supreme Paths. 10.- Become a Buddha in one lifetime.

---o0o---

4. NATURAL ENJOYMENT

The world of Ultimate Bliss, from the palaces, temples, maintenance, and longevity to all objects, are created by seven naturally occurring treasures, not by artificial construction.

When the Pure Land person wants to wear natural dharma clothes, it is on his body.

When it's time to eat, if someone wants golden dishes, golden dishes will immediately appear in front of them. People want silver dishes, or lapis lazuli, glass, moon pearls, wish-fulfilling pearls, etc., then the desired dishes will appear in front of them. Delicious food and drinks are available in plates and bowls, suitable for the number of people eating, without too much or too little. After eating, the dishes hide themselves, and when it's time to eat, they appear again, not being put away. The food that enters the body naturally dissipates gradually, turning into fragrant vapor that is excreted through the pores, without any residue, nourishing the body and making it healthier, the mind is happy like an asrava.

---o0o---

5. MIND AND SPIRITUAL POWER

In the world of Ultimate Bliss, everyone is wise and clear, with unhindered eloquence. No one is stupid. Whenever I think, it is purely a moral concept. Therefore, the words spoken are purely Dharma. Everyone loves and respects each other. No greed, no anger, no ignorance, no self-view. The senses are pure, not distracted, not false.

Everyone has five types of magical powers:

1.- Heavenly eyes can see throughout the ten directions, even the weakest person can see hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of na-do-tha worlds.

2.- The heavenly ear is clear and can hear in all ten directions. Even the poorest person can hear the teachings of hundreds of thousands of billions of kotis of Buddhas. After listening, I can remember and understand everything.

3.- Understanding other people's minds, clearly knowing the thoughts of others, even the least able person can know the thoughts of all living beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of na-dotha worlds.

4.- Sufficient life, remember clearly previous lives. Even the poorest person knows clearly the past and future events of hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of kalpas.

5.- Divine power, in the time it takes one thought to travel throughout the ten directions, the weakest person can travel hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of na-do-tha worlds.

---o0o---

6. DAILY WORK

The people of Ultimate Bliss, every early morning, bring beautiful precious flowers to make offerings to Amitabha Buddha and countless Buddhas in other worlds. If they want to make offerings of flowers, incense, music, or want to make offerings of clothes, jewels, garlands, etc., while in front of Buddhas in other worlds, due to Amitabha Buddha's majestic vow power, the beautiful and precious offerings will appear in the air like clouds, then gracefully fall down to the ashram. become an offering. They also use wonderful sounds to praise the merits of the Buddhas and respectfully listen to the teachings of the Buddhas' Dharma. After making offerings and listening to the Dharma, he suddenly flew back lightly, arriving at his native land (the Land of Ultimate Bliss) still before meal time.

The Pure Land person, after finishing his meal, meditates and meditates on the wonderful Dharma, or recites Buddha's name, Dharma's name, and Sangha's name.

The Pure Land person, after bathing in the maintenance place, then sat on a precious lotus flower to practice the Dharma.

In the world of Ultimate Bliss, some people preach the Sutras in the void, some people recite the Sutras, some people preach the Sutras themselves, some people teach the Sutras, some people listen to the Sutras, some people think of the wonderful meaning, some people sit in meditation, some people do walking meditation, etc.

Or there are people on the treasured grounds who preach the Sutras, chant the Sutras, preach the Sutras, teach the Sutras, listen to the Sutras, or contemplate the wonderful Dharma, meditate and meditate, and walk in meditation, etc.

Due to this practice, those who have not yet attained the four fruits will attain the four fruits, those who have not entered the stage of non-regression will attain the stage of non-regression...

---o0o---

7. VIRTUE

In the world of Ultimate Bliss, everyone lives in the realm of Ultimate Bliss, meaning that after being born in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, everyone stands firmly on the path of Supreme Enlightenment, no longer regressing or falling, progressing to the level of One Birth and Supplementing the Land (Equality of Enlightenment) and becoming Buddha.

This is because the state of the Land of Ultimate Bliss is solemn and pure, purely on the one hand, helping to increase moral conduct: (The seven good conditions below are excerpted from the volume "Ten Reasons for Thought" by Great Master Tri Jia).

1.- Often see the Buddha and receive the power of the Buddha's vow. Like being on a big ship, not drowned by the waves,

2.- Buddha's light often shines on the body, causing the Bodhi mind to increase. Like having sunlight, avoiding falling into a pit and collapsing.

3.- Often close to Avalokiteśvara, Mahasthamaprapta, great Bodhisattvas, guided and protected by Bodhisattvas, everyone around me is purely good and not evil or evil. It's like the lights are on.

4.- Water, birds, trees, nets, wind, music, light, etc. all always perform and speak the Dharma. When you hear the Dharma, your mind immediately becomes pure.

5.- Food, drink, and bathing water all make good roots grow.

6.- A complete mind does not cling to false predestined relationships, does not have negative thoughts or afflictions, and mindfulness is always present.

7.- The body is an indestructible diamond. Not old or weak, not sick, living a long life for immeasurable and boundless kalpas. Don't get old or sick to hinder your practice. There is no need for impermanence to interrupt morality.

With all the above conditions, it is impossible to withdraw from the path of enlightenment without deciding to become a Buddha.

As the Amitabha Sutra says: "All sentient beings born in the Pure Land world are irreversible." It says again: "Those who vow to return to the Pure Land will attain the unsurpassed path of Bodhi without turning back."

In the Awakening of Faith there is a saying: "People who are born in the Pure Land because they often see the Buddha, are completely irreversible."

ADDITIONAL NOTES - The Pure Land Dharma, in addition to the practice of reciting Buddha's name, places great importance on "Faith" and "Vow".

Knowing clearly the cause and earth of the Buddha and the two Great Beings, the good Father and my wise teachers in the future, I have firmly realized that: Their compassionate vows are embracing me, their light is shining on me and all those who recite the Buddha's name, therefore my trust will be warm and deep.

Understanding clearly the wonderful and solemn scene of Ultimate Bliss is our eternal home in the future, knowing clearly that the body and mind of the people of Ultimate Bliss are pure and transcendent, which will also be our eternal retribution, therefore my aspirations will be fervent and strong.

"Faith" is deep, "will" is established, all of our actions are self-directed. So we already have the nine levels of golden lotus in our hands.

Moreover, if anyone sees and hears the robe and the true report in the Pure Land and then earnestly wishes to return, always remembers it clearly in his heart without a moment of distraction, he will certainly achieve contemplation. Now I can see the Pure Land with Buddha and Bodhisattva, and when I die, I will be reborn at the highest level.

Because of such great benefits, our Master repeated it over and over again in dharma assemblies such as when preaching the Sutra: Hoa Nghiem, Phap Hoa, Bao Tich, Bi Hoa, Amitabha Minor, etc. The most complete were the dharma assemblies preaching the Avalokiteshvara and the Infinite Life Sutra.

In the following books of this "Road to Ultimate Bliss" series, we will read stories of people before us who have achieved good results as mentioned above.

I hope everyone will respectfully pay attention to the chapters "Physical General" and "National Status".

--- o0o ---

CHAPTER SIX - THE GREAT BODHISATTVA ADVISE PEOPLE TO REMEMBER BUDDHA AND PRAY FOR BEING BIRTH

tom_tat: Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva achieved enlightenment by reciting the Buddha's name, and patiently practiced the Bodhisattva path to teach and transform sentient beings without leaving the method of reciting the Buddha's name. We should try to follow suit
noi_dung:
I - GREAT THE CHI

Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva achieved enlightenment by reciting the Buddha's name, and patiently practiced the Bodhisattva path to teach and transform sentient beings without leaving the method of reciting the Buddha's name. We should try to imitate him.

During the Shurangama Dharma Assembly, when the Master asked about the reason for the Holy Assembly's attainment of enlightenment, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva said: "I remember countless eons ago when the Supreme Moon Tathagata taught me the method of "Reciting the Buddha's Samadhi".

For example, there are two people: "A always remembers B, and B forever forgets A. Two people like that, even if they meet each other, they will never see each other, even if they see each other, they will never see each other. If two people miss each other dearly, they will forever be close to each other like a picture and a shadow.

Buddhas miss living beings like a mother misses her children. If you keep running away, even if you remember, you won't be able to do anything. If the child also misses the mother, as the mother misses the child, then the mother and child will never be apart.

If the minds of sentient beings remember the Buddha's name and recite Buddha's name, in the present and future they decide to see the Buddha and be close to the Buddha, without needing to practice any other method to enlighten their minds and see their nature. Just like a person embalming incense, when his body has a scent, this is called “Dignified fragrance”.

In the past, when I practiced cultivating, because of my mind reciting Buddha's name, I was able to attain the Endurance of Incarnation. Now in this world, people recite Buddha's name to the Pure Land.

The World-Honored One has perfected it, wherever I am, I will be able to absorb all six senses in pure mindfulness together, to achieve right concentration, this is the first."

Technique according to the Shurangama Sutra

ADDITIONAL NOTES. – Avatamsaka Sutra says: “Due to great compassion and wanting to save all sentient beings, there is Bodhi mind, and due to Bodhi mind, one attains perfect enlightenment.”

From the root of “Great Compassion” to become a Buddha, the heart of the Buddha, or our Father, never leaves us and all sentient beings. If we single-mindedly want to see Buddha, think about Buddha and chant Buddha all the time, we will definitely see Buddha and be close to Buddha.

As the Bodhisattva taught: If the minds of sentient beings remember the Buddha and recite the Buddha's name, in the present and future they will decide to see the Buddha near the Buddha. "Present"... is the present because the mind is mature in reciting the Buddha's name, which corresponds to the Buddha, so when the mind is pure, the Buddha appears, or the spirit travels to the Pure Land to worship the Buddha.

"The future"... is to be born in the Pure Land next to Buddha in the next life. Seeing the Buddha, listening to the Buddha's teachings, naturally his wisdom is bright and clear, he penetrates the original mind, and attains the patience of Non-birth.

People who sincerely recite Buddha's name, even though they have not yet become Buddha, already have Buddha's merits. Just as we embalm incense, our body is not yet incense but already has the fragrance of incense.

Because of the above reasons, the Saints and Sages all praise the Buddhist recitation method as simple and superior among all methods. "Simple", because it can be practiced by anyone, "superior", because it quickly surpasses the sainthood, requires little effort but high results, and will definitely become a Buddha.

Bodhisattva taught: “Buddha loves sentient beings like a mother misses her children.” How touching!

We should earnestly remember the Buddha and recite Buddha with all our hearts, not to disappoint the Buddha's love and remembrance!

noi_dung:
II - Universal Sage

In the midst of the Avatamsaka Dharma Assembly, in front of the motes, a great number of Bodhisattvas and a great assembly of Shravakas and countless human beings, gods, and eight families, under the presiding testimony of the World-Honored Master. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, after praising the Buddha's merits, said to the crowd and Thien Tai's disciples: "Dear Sirs! If anyone wants to achieve the Buddha's merits, he must practice the ten great vows: one is "reverence to the Buddhas", two is "praising the Tathagata", three is "widely cultivating offerings", four is "repenting of karma", five is "rejoicing in the merits", six is "inviting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel", seven is "inviting the Buddha to abide." Eighth is "constantly depending on Buddhist learning", nine is "constantly obeying sentient beings", ten is "universal dedication".

If Bodhisattvas comply with these ten great vows, they will be able to mature all sentient beings, then they will be able to comply with the Supreme Enlightenment and will be able to fully achieve the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

Or there is a person who deeply believes in these ten great vows, then accepts them, recites them, patiently writes them down, and teaches them to everyone. This person will be reborn in the Pure Land. At the time of death, the body's organs are damaged; relatives, status, power, money, etc., all are left behind, only this great vow does not leave the person. In a moment, it guides the person to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, immediately seeing Amitabha Buddha, Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, etc. That person sees himself being born in a precious lotus flower, receiving prophecies from the Buddha. Having received the prediction, from then on for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of nadotha kalpas, he used his wisdom to conform to the nature of sentient beings in the countless worlds of the ten directions to bring about benefits. Not long after that person will sit on the Bodhi tree, subdue demons, become Supremely Enlightened, turn the great wheel of Dharma, and endure to benefit all sentient beings until the end of time...

Then he recited the verse:

May I come when my life is about to die

Eliminate all obstacles

Meeting Amitabha Buddha

Immediately be reborn in the Pure Land

I have been reborn in Ultimate Bliss

Now we can achieve this great wish

Complete everything with no leftovers

Benefit all sentient beings

The Buddha's assembly is pure

I was immediately reborn in a lotus flower

Seeing Tathagata Infinite Light

Right now, it is predicted that I will become a Buddha

Got the prediction from the Tathagata

Transformed into countless hundreds of branches

Vast intellectual power in all ten directions

Benefits all sentient beings.

And finally, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva concluded that sermon with a verse of merit dedication, praying for all living beings to return to the Pure Land.

Here is my virtuous conduct of Samantabhadra

Boundless blessings are dedicated

May all sentient beings sink

Quickly be born in the Buddha Land of Infinite Light.

The Bodhisattva finished speaking and immediately praised the Buddha: "Good ear! Good ear!"

Excerpt from the Hoa Yan Sutra

Hanh Nguyen products

ADDITIONAL NOTES - Avatamsaka Dharma Assembly, the largest and most complete Dharma assembly in the life of the Master. Samantabhadra, the foremost Bodhisattva of this dharma assembly. The assembly is the Mahayana masters of teachings, remaining in the realm of liberation without hesitation.

Bodhisattva Samantabhadra volunteered and led the entire assembly to pray together to the Pure Land world to quickly complete blessings and wisdom, quickly attain Supreme Bodhi, and only with the ultimate goal of Buddhahood can one fully and completely save sentient beings.

Because of this, we can see that the Pure Land is a great university that guarantees quick Buddhahood, so the great Bodhisattvas all vow to go there together.

so.

II B - Universal Sage Teachings on the Samadhi of Buddha's remembrance

Technique according to Sutra:

"Tathagata's Unreflective Realm"

... At that time, the World-Honored One entered into the right concentration of "The Tathagata does not care about the realm". Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said to Bodhisattva Tang: "If anyone who develops the Bodhi mind wants to attain this right concentration, he must first cultivate wisdom. Because this right concentration comes from wisdom.

This is cultivating wisdom: Must stay away from false talk and useless distractions. Then go to the Buddha hall, see the pure gold Buddha statue, or the gold-plated Buddha statue, with all the good signs and the Buddha's transformation stone. Immediately bowed his head and bowed, thinking like this: "I heard Amitabha Buddha is currently preaching in the Western world of Ultimate Bliss." Then, with reverence and trust, I thought that the image was the real body of the Buddha. With all your heart and soul, the Buddha appeared. Then, with one mind, look carefully from the top of your head to the bottom of your feet.

After watching, go to a deserted place and sit upright, visualizing the Buddha appearing as tall as one hand. Always remember it in your mind and don't forget it. If you temporarily forget, go to the Buddha hall and look again. When you look at it, it seems like

Therefore, the heart must be very respectful as to the real Buddha, not to have the concept of being an image.

Then buy beautiful, fragrant flowers and offer them. Always think that the Buddha is in front of you. And think: The World-Honored Buddha is Omniscient, he sees everything, hears everything, he probably knows his own mind.

When the visualization is successful, immediately return to a secluded place, sit and remember forever without forgetting. If you practice diligently for 21 days, if you are a virtuous person, you will see the Tathagata appear.

Or if people in previous lives have created bad karma but cannot see the Buddha, if they can diligently practice without giving up their minds and not thinking about other things, they will soon be able to see the Buddha.

Because if anyone prays for Supreme Bodhi and specializes in practicing one dharma, they will all achieve success. Like someone who drinks a sip of sea water, that is, he has tasted the water of all the rivers on earth. If a Bodhisattva can practice this method, then he has practiced all the Samadhi, the rings, the levels, and the dharanis. Therefore, you should always practice diligently, don't be lazy, don't be lazy, and single-mindedly meditate so that you can see the Buddha in the present.

When you see the Buddha, you should realize that the mind and thoughts are born, that only the mind exists, and there is no difference. My mind becomes the Buddha's mind, leaving the non-Buddha mind. The same is true for the Buddhas of the ten directions, they all rely on their own mind. If a Bodhisattva can clearly understand that all Buddhas and all dharmas are mind-only, he will be able to attain patience or enter the first level. At the time of death, he will be reborn in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, often seeing the Buddha, being close to the Buddha, listening to the Dharma and making offerings to the Buddha.

ADDITIONAL NOTES. - The method of reciting Buddha's name has four: A.- The true form of reciting Buddha's name; B.- Contemplating Buddha's memory; C.- Contemplating Buddha statues; D.- Reciting Buddha's name.

A subject A belongs to theory. The three subjects below belong to mindfulness, including theory.

In the above article, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva taught to contemplate the statue first, then to commemorate it. And finally, when the practice of contemplation has been achieved, the mindfulness of true form is achieved, that is, idealism and equality. This is before achieving Samadhi, after realizing the Buddha's name Samadhi.

In the Minor Sutra, the Master teaches the subject of reciting the Buddha's name. Holding on to the name until one's mind is undisturbed is to attain Samadhi of reciting the Buddha's name, achieving "mindfulness means non-thought" is the proof of Samadhi. The results are on the same level as the above subject of contemplation. But the practice of cultivating and reciting names is somewhat simpler. “Simple”, is because the red names have six or four words that are easy to remember, not as many as the hard-to-remember good appearances. “Convenient” is because you can hear famous names anywhere and at any time, not just at the Buddha hall

and must be as bright as contemplating a statue. Besides, if you recite the name, you can recite it silently, or recite it out loud. Thanks to reciting out loud, you can practice in noisy places. Don't meditate, you must stay in a quiet place.

For the above reasons, the subject of contemplation must be of a highly wise person to be sure of success. The practice of reciting names can be suitable for all types of people, and anyone, if they practice diligently and diligently, can achieve it. We will see the experience in the biographies of Buddha-reciters in the next book.

As the Bodhisattva taught: “If anyone prays for Supreme Bodhi and specializes in practicing one dharma, they will all achieve success.” So, because they want to become Buddha to save sentient beings, they specialize in reciting Buddha's name.

If we want to succeed in the Dharma of reciting Buddha's name, that is, to attain Samadhi and be reborn in Ultimate Bliss, we must follow the teachings of the Bodhisattva: A- "Set your mind to become a Buddha". B- "Diligence in practicing Buddha's name".

noi_dung:
III- MANjushri

Manjushri is a Bodhisattva. During the time of the Buddha's incarnation, he was the leader among the Bodhisattvas, and also the leader of the entire assembly. He often made requests to the Buddha for the sake of the assembly. He is also the person who often represents the Master to explain the wonderful Dharma to the assembly.

Below are his words encouraging the congregation to often recite Buddha's name, quoted from the Sutra "Buddha Contemplation Samadhi Sea"

When the World-Honored One finished preaching the Dharma "Contemplation of Buddha Samadhi". Manjushri Bodhisattva told the assembly:

In the past, during the time of Buddha Tathagata, Gioi Ho, the son of a wealthy man, received the Three Refuges Dharma while still in his mother's womb. When he was eight years old, one day his parents invited the Buddha to come home and make offerings. Gioi Ho's pupils saw the Buddha walking slowly and respectfully. At the Buddha's feet, with each step, lotus flowers grew and the Buddha's body radiated bright light. He was filled with joy and reverence, and immediately bowed his head in respect. After paying homage to the Buddha, his sincere disciples stared at the Buddha without leaving him.

Because of seeing the Buddha and looking at that Buddha, the disciples of the Precepts can eliminate the sins of birth and death of hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of kalpas. From then on, I will always meet Buddhas forever, as many as hundreds of billions of billions of billions of Buddhas. Those World-Honored Ones all taught the Dharma "Buddha Samadhi" exactly as the Buddha had just preached today.

After that, hundreds of thousands of Buddhas were born under the same name Chien Dan Hai. The disciples adored all the Buddhas, often bowing to the Buddha, making offerings, clasping their hands and looking at the Buddha. Due to the merit of contemplating the Buddha, he then met hundreds of thousands of asankhyas. The Buddha immediately attained hundreds of thousands of memories of "reciting the Buddha's Samadhi", and attained hundreds of thousands of asankhyas "the dharani gate". When the pupil has realized the Samadhi and dharani subjects, the Buddhas will immediately manifest themselves and preach the formless dharma to them. When the pupil heard the formless dharma, in a moment he realized the "Surangama Samadhi".

After finishing the recitation, Manjushri Bodhisattva concluded: "The disciple of Precepts at the beginning, thanks to receiving the Three Refuges Dharma, once sincerely bowed to the Buddha, contemplated the Buddha, and his mind was not tired, so he was able to meet countless Buddhas. What's more, a person who is dedicated to always thinking of the Buddha!

That Gioi Ho pupil is not a strange person, he is my predecessor!

Manjushri Bodhisattva finished speaking, the Master said to Ananda: "You should bring Manjushri's words back to the entire assembly and to all countless generations to come.

If anyone can worship the Buddha, anyone can recite the Buddha's name, anyone can contemplate the Buddha, then that person will be the same as Manjushri Bodhisattva."

Like Samantabhadra, Manjushri Bodhisattva once made a vow about the Pure Land, recorded in the Sutra "Manjushri Makes Vows".

I wish to die at the same time

Eliminate obstacles

Meeting Amitabha

Reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss

Born in the Buddha's country

Fulfill all great wishes

Amitabha Tathagata

Presently, the life of the ego is present

Strictly pure Samantabhadra conduct

Manchu Van Thu vows

Enjoy the future and sacrificial life

Saving Bodhisattva conduct.

tom_tat: During the Tang Dynasty, Thich Phap Chieu was the abbot of Van Phong Pagoda in Hoanh Chau, practicing diligently every day without hesitation
noi_dung:
IV - TWO GREAT SAINTS RESPONSE

Excerpted from the series "Song Cao Tang"

and “Lac Ban Van Loai”

During the Tang Dynasty, Thich Phap Chieu was the abbot of Van Phong Pagoda in Hoanh Chau, practicing diligently every day without delay.

In the second year of the Great Calendar, one morning, he saw in the bowl of porridge in the monk's house the shadow of five-colored auspicious clouds. In the clouds, a scene of a pagoda appears. To the northeast of the pagoda alley, there is a mountain range, at the foot of the mountain there is a stream of water. To the north of the ravine, there is a stone gateway. In the stone alley, there is a large pagoda with the name "Great Saint Truc Lam Tu".

A few days later, he again saw in the bowl of porridge a scene of a massive pagoda, garden, pond, and castle, and ten thousand Bodhisattvas in them.

He then brought the scene he saw and asked the intellectuals.

A Venerable said: "The appearances of the Saints are inconceivable. But if we talk about the direction of mountains and rivers, then it is the scene of Ngu Dai Mountain."

Hearing what the Venerable said, he wanted to visit Ngu Dai Mountain.

In the fourth year of Dai Lich, Mr. Phap Chieu met an old man and said: "You once wanted to go to the Golden World (Wantai) to pay homage to the Great Saint (Manjushri), why haven't you gone yet?" He then went with his Dharma friends to Ngu Dai.

On the fifth day of the Great Lich, on the sixth day of the fourth month, he went to Phat Quang Pagoda in Ngu Dai district. That night, at the fourth watch, he suddenly saw a strange light coming from afar to shine on him. He immediately followed the rays of light and walked. After going fifty miles, we came to a mountain range. At the foot of the mountain there was a ravine, and on the north side of the ravine was a stone alley. In the alley, there were two boys standing ready, calling their names Thien Tai and Nan Da. The two boys led him to a large temple, on the signboard was the name "Great Saint Truc Lam Temple", golden soil, and very solemn precious trees. Exactly like the scene seen in the bowl of porridge before.

He entered the temple, went up to the lecture hall, saw in the West the time of Manjushri, the East in the time of Samantabhadra, two great Bodhisattvas both sitting on tall thrones, preaching the Dharma to ten thousand Bodhisattvas.

Mr. Phap Chieu respectfully came before the court to pay homage and said: "Ordinary people are at the end of the dharma, far away from Buddha, their karma is deep and heavy, their blessings are thin and their wisdom is shallow. Even though we have enough Buddha nature, we cannot discover it. The Buddha Dharma is too vast, it is not clear which Dharma method should we practice appropriately?".

Manjushri taught: "Now is the right time for you to recite the Buddha's name. No practice practice includes the practice of reciting the Buddha's name. Then add offerings to the Three Jewels, including cultivating both merit and wisdom. These two subjects are very essential.

In the past, thanks to contemplating the Buddha, reciting the Buddha's name, and making offerings to the Buddha, we attained Omniscience.

That's why all the dharmas: Prajnaparamita, even profound meditation, even Buddhahood, are born from Buddha's name. Therefore, you should know, "Reciting the Buddha's name is the king of all dharmas."

His Holiness Phap Chieu explained: "How should we recite Buddha's name?".

Manjushri taught: "To the West of this world there is Amitabha Buddha, the leader of the Pure Land. The power of that Buddha's vow is inconceivable. You should concentrate on reciting Amitabha Buddha without interruption, and at the time of death, decide to be reborn, forever without turning back from the Supreme Path."

Having finished speaking, the two Great Saints raised their golden hands to pat Phap Chieu's head and said: "Because of you reciting Buddha's name, you will soon attain Supreme Bodhi. If any good man or woman wishes to quickly become Buddha, there is nothing better than reciting Buddha's name. Reciting Buddha's name will quickly attain Supreme Bodhi."

After the two Great Saints received their predictions, Phap Chieu happily bowed and then withdrew.

His two disciples took him out of the temple alley. He raised his head to look back, and suddenly the people and scenes disappeared. He then erected a stone to mark that spot and then returned to Phat Quang pagoda.

On April 13, he went with fifty monks to the Diamond Cave to sincerely bow to the names of 35 Buddhas. Mr. Phap had just completed the 10th ceremony when he suddenly saw the large, solemn and pure Diamond Cave, with a palace made of lapis lazuli, and saw Manjushri and Samantabhadra residing together there.

Another day, Phap Chieu went alone to the Diamond Cave to pray to see the Great Saint, then threw himself down and bowed. He suddenly saw the Holy Monk introducing himself as Buddha Ba Loi leading him into a monastery, the sign read "Vajra Prajna Tu". The entire palace is beautiful and dignified with sparkling light.

Although he had seen strange things many times, he had not told anyone about it.

In December of that year, he entered the ashram to recite Buddha's name at Hoa Nghiem pagoda. He went on a hunger strike and vowed to be reborn in the Pure Land. On the seventh day, early in the evening, while reciting Buddha's name, he saw a Holy Monk come in and say: "You have seen the realm at Ngu Dai Mountain, why don't you pass it on to the world to know!". Having finished speaking, the Holy Monk immediately hid.

At dawn, he again saw the Holy Monk entering the palace like he did earlier in the day. He then replied: "It's not that I have the Holy Path hidden in my heart, I'm just afraid that if I say it out loud people don't believe in it, it will only cause criticism!".

The Holy Monk said: "The Great Saint Manjushri is currently in Wutai, but there are still people who can slander him. You should bring the precepts that you personally saw in the Five Precepts, spread them to everyone, let everyone hear about them and develop Bodhi mind."

Mr. Phap Chieu obeyed, remembered carefully what he had seen, then wrote it down and passed it on to everyone.

The following year, Mr. Thich Hue Tung and the monks of Hoa Nghiem Pagoda accompanied Mr. Phap Chieu to the Diamond Cave to worship Buddha, then to the previous stone place to admire the old relics. Everyone was admiring and pensive when suddenly they heard a bell ringing from the cliff, the bell ringing and ringing clearly. Everyone was surprised and agreed that Phap Chieu's words were true.

Because they wanted people to develop a spiritual mind, the Sangha engraved the story of Phap Chieu seen on the cliff.

A few years later, the monks built a pagoda right at the place where Phap Chieu marked, naming it "Truc Lam pagoda", where Phap Chieu was taught and predicted by Venerable Manjushri and Pho Hien.

(About his practice and propagation, see the chapter "The Patriarchs of the Lotus Sect").

ADDITIONAL NOTES. – Manjushri Bodhisattva taught: "Of all the practices, none surpasses the practice of reciting the Buddha's name." And he taught again: "Reciting the Buddha's name is the king of all methods."

Contemplating the Bodhisattva's words, if we, people of the Dharma Ending Age, who develop the Bodhi mind: “Praying to become Buddha and vowing to save sentient beings”, must obey the Bodhisattva's words and practice reciting the Buddha's name. Because “reciting the Buddha's name will quickly become a Buddha.” The words of the two Great Saints when patting Phap Chieu's head.

How should we recite? Bodhisattva taught: “Concentrate on reciting Amitabha Buddha without interruption.”

We should focus on the place of “concentrated recitation” and “uninterrupted” practice, because that is the practice that must be present in those who recite Buddha's name.

“Specialized in reciting” means purely reciting Buddha's name without mixing it up with other things, but also without letting the mind think about other things.

“Uninterrupted” is the title of Buddha, always continuing in the mind, Patriarch Thien Dao and Great Master Lien Tri call it “continuous” also called “non-thoughtful self-recitation”. This is the result of “concentrated mindfulness” and the starting point of “undisturbed single-mindedness” or “Buddha-reciting Samadhi”. Reciting the Buddha's name "without interruption" is guaranteed to be reborn and attain non-regression status. If you have "one mind" or attain "Samadhi", your dignity will be higher.

---o0o---

tom_tat: During the Tang Dynasty, during the time of King Trung Ton, Venerable Thich Hue Nhut saw Dharma Master Nghia Tinh go to the Western Regions to seek Dharma, and was filled with admiration.
noi_dung:
V - Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Hanh Thanh

Excerpted from “The Story of Song Cao Tang”

and “Buddha's Records”

During the Tang Dynasty, during the time of King Trung Ton, Venerable Thich Hue Nhut saw Dharma Master Nghia Tinh go to Tay Vuc to seek Dharma, and he was very impressed.

He then took a boat across the sea, three years later he arrived in Thien Truc (India), then in turn went to worship at the relics of the Buddha Shakyamuni, and requested Sanskrit Sutras.

From the time he was in his home country until he came to Thien Truc, he witnessed many scenes of human suffering, and he himself also experienced many hardships.

That's why he thought: which country, which world is only pure joy without suffering? Which dharma is the practice to quickly see the Buddha? Then he asked that matter to all the famous and virtuous people in Thien Truc. The famous and virtuous people allude to the Western the Land of Ultimate Bliss world, and together advise one to practice the Pure Land Dharma. Hue Nhut immediately respectfully obeyed the advice of the famous virtues and specialized in reciting Buddha's name.

Shortly after that, he went to the country of Kandala in North India. In the northeast of the king's citadel, there is a large mountain range. On the mountain there is a statue of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Anyone who prays sincerely will often see the Bodhisattva appear. He then went up to the mountain to bow for seven days and nights, then fasted, vowing: If he cannot see the Bodhisattva, he would rather die in that place.

On the seventh night, in the void, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared in a purple-gold form, more than one meter tall, sitting on a precious lotus throne, with bright light. Bodhisattva reached down and patted Hue Nhut's head and said:

"If you want to transmit the Dharma to save yourself and save others, you should concentrate on reciting the Western Pure Land, Amitabha Buddha's world and vow to be reborn.
