When you return to Pure Land and see the Buddha and I, you will receive great benefits. You should know that the Pure Land Dharma is superior to all other practices."

After the Bodhisattva finished teaching, he immediately hid.

Because Hue Nhut was on a hunger strike for seven days, his strength was exhausted that night, but after the Bodhisattva patted his head and listened to his teachings, his body suddenly became strong and his mind clear.

After that, he took the Sutra he requested back to his native country. When you're busy, take the mountain road. From the day we left until we returned home, it took 18 years and we traveled to more than seventy countries.

In the 7th year of Khai Nguyen, when he returned to Truong An, he went to court to present Buddha statues and Sanskrit scriptures.

From then on, he diligently cultivated his karma and transmitted it to prosperity for a time. The royal court's title is Tu Man Tripitaka Dharma Master.

Thanks to his guidance, many people who chant Buddha's name attained Samadhi and were reborn in large numbers.

He edited the book "Rebirth in the Pure Land" that was engraved and transmitted during his lifetime.

In the 7th year of the Huu Dynasty, when he passed away, the assembly saw a lotus flower as bright as the sun appearing in front of his seat.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Great monk, from Tang Ky Da country of Dong Thien Truc. There was a herd of horses that heard the voice of the Great Master preaching the Dharma and felt sad and howled, so people at that time called the Great Master Ma Minh Ton
noi_dung:
VI- MA MINH DOCTOR

Excerpted from the series: "The Legend of Light"

and “Mahayana Awakening of Faith”

Great monk, from Tang Ky Da country of Dong Thien Truc. There was a herd of horses that heard the sound of the Great Master preaching the Dharma and felt sad and howled, so people at that time called the Great Master the Venerable Ma Minh.

Regarding the lineage of the Patriarchs, starting from Mahakasyapa as the First Patriarch, Anan Da as the Second Patriarch... at the time of the Great Master as the 12th Patriarch, he attained the Dharma from the 11th Patriarch, Venerable Phu Na Da Xa.

The great monk once authored the collection "Awakening of Faith in the Mahayana", based on "the minds of living beings" he displayed the "Mahayana meaning". All the contaminated dharmas of mortal life and death, and all the pure liberated dharmas of the Saints, are created by the "mind" alone, depending on whether it is pure or contaminated. Deluding the "mind", ignorance arises, discriminating and clinging to views, then causing karma and suffering the consequences of birth and death. Enlightenment of the "mind" will end karma, destroy attachment to views, end ignorance and attain liberation and happiness.

Realizing one's own mind, true faith that is one's own nature, forever not being confused and forgetting that self-nature, this is called the "unremitting faith" of the Mahayana. Bringing people to the Mahayana level, with faith and non-regression, is the main purpose of the "Awakening of Faith in Mahayana".

To reach this level of "non-regression", according to the commentary, one must be capable of cultivating good roots, deeply believing in cause and effect, eliminating evil actions, serving good people, developing Bodhi mind, meeting Buddhas close to them, making offerings, and practicing Bodhisattva conduct. Practicing such virtues is enough for ten thousand great kalpas, and with faith, one can achieve the level of non-regression.

If you are a person who does not meet all of the above conditions, you may still be regressed, and the Supreme Path is not yet guaranteed.

Finally, the Great Master advised people to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land to quickly achieve faith and be sure to stay at the "non-regressing" level.

This is the Great Master's advice:

"Because living beings are in this Saha world, they are afraid that they will not be able to often meet Buddhas to be close to them and make offerings, for fear that their faith will be difficult to achieve. We must know that our Lord Shakyamuni Tathagata has taught a supreme means to protect our faith. That is, the Master teaches to concentrate on reciting the Buddha's name. Because of concentrating on reciting the Buddha's name, we should, according to our wish, be born in the Pure Land, always close to the Buddha, and forever leave the evil path. As in the Sutras. : If a person specializes in reciting the Western Pure Land, the world of Amitabha Buddha, and all the good roots of merit he cultivates dedicate and pray to that world, he will be reborn when he is born in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, because he often sees the Buddha, he will never be regressed.

Because of such causes and conditions, our Master, at the Ky Vien dharma assembly preaching the Amitabha Sutra, three or four times thoroughly advised everyone to make a vow to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land. The Master said that any sentient being born in the Pure Land world is "irreversible". "In the world of Ultimate Bliss, sentient beings attain the highest level of wisdom."

Later, the Great Master gave the dharma to the 13th Patriarch, Kapi Ma La Venerable, then entered the right concentration of "Long Chanh Tan Samadhi", his body soared into space, round and bright like the sun, and momentarily returned to the dharma throne to sit cross-legged and enter nirvana.

According to the ancients, the Great Master is a Dharmakaya Bodhisattva on earth.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Bodhisattva from South India once practiced meditation in the mountains. On that mountain there is a very tall ancient tree, under the tree there are 500 dragons. Bodhisattva manifests his divine power to subdue dragons, and preaches the Dharma every day. Therefore,…
noi_dung:
VII - Nagarjuna Bodhisattva

Excerpts from the series:

“The Legend of the Dang Luc”, “Piba Sa Luan”

“Great Wisdom Treatise”, “Entering the Old Tomb Sutra”

Bodhisattva from South India once practiced meditation in the mountains. On that mountain there is a very tall ancient tree, under the tree there are 500 dragons. Bodhisattva manifests his divine power to subdue dragons, and preaches the Dharma every day. Therefore, people called him Venerable Nagarjuna.

He attained Dharma with the 13th Patriarch, Venerable Kapi Ma La, and then succeeded him as the 14th Patriarch. He had the intention of widely spreading the Sutra teachings.

At that time, Great Dragon Bodhisattva took him to the Dragon Palace in the ocean, opened the seven treasures, and let him freely read and read the Sutra Pitaka. He focused on watching for 90 days and nights and understood a lot. After 90 days, Great Dragon Bodhisattva took him back to Thien Truc to preach the Dharma.

The Sutra "Great Square Buddha Avatamsaka" (Sanskrit) was written by him himself after returning from Dragon Palace.

He has a collection of works called "Piba Sha Luan". In that treatise, there is a statement praising Amitabha Buddha, summarized as follows:

If anyone wishes to become Buddha

Mindfulness of Amitabha

Buddha immediately appeared

So I surrender

Due to Buddha's original vow

Bodhisattva of the ten directions

Come make offerings and listen to the Dharma

So I bowed my head

Bodhisattva in Ultimate Bliss

Beautiful and dignified body

All good generals

Now I pay my respects

Bodhisattva in Ultimate Bliss

Every day in three times

Make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions

So I bowed my head

If the person planting the roots is good

Suspicious when the flowers do not bloom

People with pure faith

When the flowers bloom, you see Buddha

Currently Buddha in the ten directions

Because I want to save sentient beings

Which praise Amitabha

So I surrender to the ceremony

That realm is very solemn

More pure than heaven

The merit is very deep

So I bowed to Buddha's feet.

He created the "Tri Do Luan" series. In that treatise, in the chapter on the Dharma method of reciting the Buddha's name, there are words like this:

"Reciting the Buddha's name in Samadhi" eliminates the afflictions and sins of previous lives.

Of the other Samadhis, there are some that can eliminate lust but cannot eliminate anger; There are methods that can eliminate anger but cannot eliminate lust; There are subjects that can eliminate delusion but cannot eliminate lust and anger; There are methods that can eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance, but cannot eliminate past karma.

This "Reciting the Buddha's Samadhi" eliminates all kinds of afflictions and all kinds of karma.

Furthermore, the "Buddha-reciting Samadhi" has great merit and virtue that can save sentient beings.

Bodhisattvas want to save sentient beings, and other samadhis are not as blessed and virtuous as "reciting the Buddha's name"; This samadhi quickly eliminates all evil obstacles.

Furthermore, Buddha is the Dharma King, and Bodhisattvas are like Dharma Generals. The Bodhisattva's place of respect is only Buddha, World-Honored One, so one must often recite Buddha's name.

For example, a mandarin is loved by the king, so he often remembers his king. Bodhisattvas, too, know that merits

and my immeasurable wisdom all come from the Buddha. Because the Buddha's grace is very heavy, I often recite the Buddha's name.

Because Bodhisattva always recites the Buddha's name and his mind never leaves the Buddha, he often meets Buddhas.

Question: Bodhisattvas must transform sentient beings, so why do they want to meet Buddhas often?

Answer: Those who have not entered the "Bodhisattva's position", have not attained the "irreversible" stage, have not received the "Buddha's prediction", if they leave the Buddhas, their good roots will be destroyed and they will sink into the abyss of afflictions. You can't save yourself yet, you can't save others. Like a boatman, in the middle of the river, his boat broke down and wanted to save others, but he was sinking. In the mind, we want to get it, but in the situation, we don't get it, but it's even more harmful. It's like pouring a little boiling water into a large frozen pond. The oil melts a little, but then the boiling water instead freezes into frost!

If a Bodhisattva has not yet entered the Dharma position, if he is far away from the Buddhas and does not have means and means, but uses a little merit to save sentient beings, even though he may get some results, he will instead fall into hell. That's why these Bodhisattvas must always be close to the Buddha and never leave him!

Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, even though they have attained Nirvana, cannot guide the Bodhisattvas because they do not have all-element wisdom. Only Buddhas have achieved Omniscience so they can teach and guide Bodhisattvas. Like an elephant stuck in a quagmire, only using an elephant can save it. If Bodhisattvas fall into the wrong path, only Buddha can save them, because they are of the same Mahayana path. For the above reasons, Bodhisattvas must be close to Buddha!

Furthermore, the Bodhisattva thinks to himself that if he does not have the Buddha's eye, he is no different from a blind person. If he is not guided by the Buddha, he will be lost in another path because he cannot see the path. Suppose you hear the Buddha's Dharma, but practice it because you live in a different place from the Buddha's, then there will be harm because it is not clear whether the teachings are right or where the Dharma should be practiced more or less. Therefore, Bodhisattvas must always be close to Buddha.

Furthermore, a Bodhisattva is close to the Buddha, or he sees the Buddha with his eyes and his mind is pure, or when he hears the Buddha's teachings, his mind immediately enjoys the taste of the Dharma and gains great wisdom. Then he practices the Dharma and attains great liberation.

Being close to the Buddha brings such immeasurable great benefits, shouldn't we single-mindedly seek to see the Buddha and be close to the Buddha?

Like a child who should not leave his mother; People on long journeys should not leave food behind; During the hot season, you should not leave the cool wind and cold water; When the season is too cold, you should not leave the fire; If you cross a deep and wide stream, you should not leave the boat; Patients should not leave the doctor.

Bodhisattvas should not leave the Buddhas, which is a more essential issue than the above.

The benefits that come from parents, relatives, intellectuals, human kings, heavenly kings, all of them, are not equal to the benefits from the Buddha. The Buddha brought great benefit to the Bodhisattvas: they were freed from the paths of suffering and found peace in the Buddha land.

Question: How to avoid leaving the Buddhas?

Answer: All sentient beings have karmic causes and conditions for countless lifetimes. Even though they practice merit, their wisdom is shallow. Even though they practice wisdom, their merit is thin. Bodhisattvas who seek the Buddha way must practice Samsara and Dharma forbearance. Because of the practice of Sanh Sanh, to develop a mind of compassion for all sentient beings, we can destroy immeasurable sins and increase immeasurable blessings. Because practicing the Dharma patiently destroys ignorance, one gains immeasurable wisdom. Having both the virtues of Birth-forbearance and Dharma-forbearance, one can attain eternal life without leaving the Buddhas.

Furthermore, because Bodhisattvas often like to recite Buddha's name, they will always meet Buddhas forever.

For example, any living being whose lust is too strong will take on the body of a lustful bird (a sparrow, a duck, etc.). Living beings whose anger is too strong will be born into poisonous insects (snakes, centipedes, etc.).

In the same way, Bodhisattvas do not care about the wealth and blessings of people of heaven, they only like to often recite Buddha's name, because they often recite Buddha's name, they wish to be born in the Pure Land according to their heart.

Furthermore, because Bodhisattvas often skillfully practice “Buddha-reciting Samadhi,” wherever they are born, they often meet Buddhas. The Sutra "The Eightfold Samadhi" says: "The Bodhisattva enters this Samadhi and in this present life is reborn in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha..."

Later, the cause and effect of teaching was fulfilled, Nagarjuna Bodhisattva gave the Dharma to Venerable Ca Na De Ba and entered Samadhi and passed away.

During the Mausoleum Dharma Assembly, the Buddha once told Bodhisattva Maha Hue that: "Great Hui should know: After the Buddha's passing, in the future there will be someone who will uphold the Buddha's Dharma, a man named Nam Thien Truc with the great Bhikkhu named Nagarjuna. That Bhikkhu can break through the sects of sects and non-sects, to display the Buddha's Supreme Mahayana Dharma. That Nagarjuna will attain the status of Bodhisattva of Joyful Land and be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss." This is the mysterious prediction of the Great Master, but also the prediction for Nagarjuna Bodhisattva.

---o0o---

tieu_de: VIII- AWARENESS OF THE MIRACULOUS HOPE OF THE BODHISATTVA
tom_tat: During the Ming Dynasty, in the 16th year of Chong Trinh, Bodhisattva descended to Ngo Mon. Qing Dynasty, in the fourth year of Shun Tri, Bodhisattva responded to the opportunity to preach and teach the Pure Dharma
noi_dung:
VIII- AWARENESS OF THE MIRACULOUS HOPE OF THE BODHISATTVA

Excerpted from the series: “Western Xa Chi”

During the Ming Dynasty, in the 16th year of Chong Trinh, Bodhisattva descended to Ngo Mon. Qing Dynasty, in the fourth year of Shun Tri, Bodhisattva responded to the opportunity to preach and teach the Pure Land Dharma.

He taught that: The essence of the Dharma of the Buddhas is so wonderful and secret that it is inconceivable. Because it's inconceivable, no one can do it all.

The original Master Muni Buddha had compassion on sentient beings and said things that could not be said, to teach and guide in this life and the next.

The Buddha again used special means to display the Pure Land, telling people to vow to be reborn in order to quickly escape samsara.

Due to the great vow power of Amitabha Buddha to accept all living beings, whoever hears the name Amitabha Buddha and diligently accepts and upholds it will be determined to be reborn in the Pure Land.

If anyone is courageous and diligent in reciting the mind most often, then they will achieve the "Buddha Recitation Samadhi" and will also be able to see Amitabha Buddha.

Today we follow the Buddha's teachings and teach Pure Land. I think because you people are confused, you only know the true path. This is not a small cause, you must try to respect it. The road to Ultimate Bliss is ten thousand billion miles away, a single thought is certain, that is it.

He taught again: This Pure Land Dharma is truly the heart sect of the Buddhas. It is the shortest path to liberation for all species.

Nowadays, even though you pray for rebirth, your heart is not interested. It is like a person entering the sea but not being able to get a jewel, your efforts are in vain. Let me tell you my past life clearly:

During the Jin Dynasty, during the reign of Emperor Ming, I was a poor man. Because I was so miserable and lacking, after I learned about the Pure Land Dharma, I made a great vow like this: "Because I created bad karma in my previous life, I now bear this miserable retribution. If I cannot now see Amitabha Buddha being born in the Pure Land to achieve all my merits, then even if this body dies, I will not rest." After vowing, I diligently remember Buddha's name day and night. On the seventh day, my mind suddenly opened and I saw Amitabha Buddha's beautiful light shining in the ten directions. The Buddha touched my head with his golden hand and told the prophecy. At the age of 75, I sat cross-legged and chanted Buddha's name and left my body. Taken by Buddha and Saints to the Pure Land. But because the original vow to save sentient beings is heavy in my heart, I return to this impure realm and, depending on the opportunity, manifest and educate. There was a time when I became a Bhikkhu, a lay person. Sometimes I become a king or a mandarin. Many times we become a woman or a beggar, etc. Using means that are either hidden or obvious, favorable or unfavorable, we guide people into the Dharma.

Up to now, for your sake, I teach the Pure Land. You must be single-minded and persistent in practicing this method and you will definitely get great benefits. If you are diligent and single-minded, you will not have to wait for the next life to be close to the Buddha, and even in the present you will be able to see the Buddha.

He spoke verses:

Rarely tells a story

Reciting a Buddhist phrase many times

Kill false thoughts

The human Dharma body is revealed.

Someone asked: What should I do if I recite the Buddha's name but cannot achieve one-pointedness of mind?

He taught: You must stop thinking and stop worrying, then slowly meditate. We have to make sure that the sound harmonizes with the mind, and the mind follows the sound. Reciting like this for a long time will allow the false thoughts to stand still, and the mind will be completely illuminated, entering the "Samadhi of reciting the Buddha's name". But every day you need to recite regularly, from a thousand to ten thousand, the mind should not be interrupted, then it is very easy to master. If you try to force your mind to be one, you will never be able to be one.

Then he taught again: The cessation of false thoughts is the eternal true mind of the Buddhas. If false thoughts remain, it is the karma of the life and death of sentient beings. If you can diligently practice without a single gap in your mind, then you will be able to get some satisfaction.

We must be careful not to practice for half a year or ten months and then consider ourselves to have merited our practice. We must know that this self-righteous concept is the obstacle to the path. Be very careful ! Even though you have tried diligently, if your mindfulness is not as steady as a copper mountain, as strong as an iron wall, not pushed over, not shaken, then it has not yet become one piece. Don't stop when you just get a little help, but you will make the mistake of "selling junk", sometimes you will have to ruin your previous efforts. This is a big disease of monks, you need to know. You should understand that: Buddhism is like the ocean, the deeper you go, the deeper you go, it doesn't take a little bit of knowledge to fully understand it. We must practice for the rest of our lives, going all the way to the source and the bottom as our goal. We should not underestimate it.

There was Mr. Co Dinh Thanh who asked for advice.

Bodhisattva teaches: The mind is inherently thoughtless. Reciting according to thought arises. Because thoughts are false, they circulate in birth and death.

You should realize: this Amitabha Buddha sentence is not born from thoughts, does not exist from memories, is not inside, is not outside, has no appearance. That is to eliminate all delusions, along with the Tathagata's pure, wonderful true body that is neither the same nor different, unable to distinguish between the same and different. By reciting the Buddha's name like that, the afflictions of the world do not end and are not affected by any negative effects, only one mind remains. Having a single mind must be "holding the name", then it can be called "one-minded, undisturbed". At this point, you will successfully purify your karma and go straight to the "Top Rank" level.

First of all, you should make a great vow: "May I be born in the Pure Land". Then sincerely and earnestly recite Amitabha Buddha's name. The sound of chanting must be conditioned by the mind, the mind of chanting must be conditioned by the sound. The voice and the mind must be tightly intertwined, like a cat pouncing on a mouse. If you recite the Buddha's name like this for a long time without distraction, you will attain the "Samadhi of Right Memory." After attaining Samadhi, if you want to advance further, you should consult with highly knowledgeable people to realize for yourself the wonderful truth of "The Buddha's Mind".

He told Mr. Vo Hu: People who practice pure karma should turn their faces to the west when walking, standing, sitting, lying down, when living, when the opportunity arises, and good roots will mature quickly. In the interior, there is only one Buddha statue, one set of Sutras, one altar, one incense burner, one bed, and one chair. There should not be many other objects. Outside the yard, you should sweep it clean and clear for convenient walking. We need to make sure that our mind is no longer busy with anything else, except focusing on reciting Buddha's name, and not worrying about anything, being free and carefree. No memory of body, no fate. Up until now, while reciting Buddha's name and practicing the Dharma, I still don't have the notion that I practice. If we do so, we will become closer and closer to the path while life's affairs will become farther and farther away, and we will be able to achieve pure karma. While you are living here, if you clear your mind of all the worldly matters without the slightest entanglement, then when your fate comes, you will be free and happy to go. Isn't that the attitude of a great man?

I say this because I want you to stop worrying about trivial things and practice with one mind. Because that is the important condition.

As for the Pure Land cultivation method, there are no more than two words “expertise” and “need”.

“Professional” time does not care about anything else.

“Need” time without wasting a minute or a second.

From now on, every early morning, after waking up, he recites a volume of the Amitabha Sutra, recites the Buddha's name a thousand sentences, then bows to the Buddha and dedicates it with the essay "One-minded surrender to life", because this essay is concise but full of meaning. If you can bow to Buddha a hundred times, even better. This is a one-time recitation course.

At first I wasn't used to it, so it was day and night all the time. Once you get used to it, increase it to six times, then to twelve times. Every day, the city added twelve books of Sutras and one hundred and two thousand Buddhist verses, using this number as a daily lock. It can also be combined and divided into four periods. Besides this number, other time-honored efforts are not mentioned.

Regarding chanting, either out loud or silently, it's all right. Just need to remember to make sure.

Again, the practice of reciting names requires that every word and sentence be clear and distinct, with the voice and mind in harmony, without the slightest remembrance of worldly events mixed up. From time to time, he matures and decides to be born in the Pure Land, sitting on a jeweled lotus throne with the "irreversible" level. You must try to get it!

The Bodhisattva preached the Dharma in 24 assemblies. His disciple, Mr. Thuong Nhiep, copied his teachings into the set "Western Xat Chi", engraved and handed down.

ADDITIONAL WORDS.- Regarding the meticulous practice in the Pure Land Dharma, the teachings of Bodhisattva Giac Minh Dieu Hanh are very clear and very effective. We can grasp the outline like this:

The principles of the Pure Land dharma are “faith”, “virtue” and “vows”. Faith and vows are the basis for virtue.

1. Regarding “Faith”, he taught:

Pure Land is miles away, one thought is certain and that is it!

In the teachings above, we should pay attention to the two words "confidence". I firmly believe that the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is pure and dignified. Believing in the power of Amitabha Buddha's vow to take care of all living beings. I firmly believe that by practicing the Dharma, I will be able to attain rebirth at the "irreversible" level. With the above three things, without the slightest doubt, without a single thought of hesitation, that is called “confidence”.

2. Regarding "Vow", he taught:

You should make the great vow "Vow to be born in Ultimate Bliss".

Wishing to be born in Ultimate Bliss is a great event. Because we, or sentient beings in the Saha world of the five defilements and evil worlds, for countless lifetimes, countless kalpas, have been rolling in the quagmire of the five desires, infatuated with the six mundane worlds, desires filling our minds, afflictions filling our bellies, love that is difficult to end, greed that is difficult to leave. If one is not a person who repents of evil thoughts and is determined to escape, then the wish to be reborn in Ultimate Bliss is difficult to establish. This is the first difficult vow to make. If you want to return to the Pure Land, you must have the Mahayana mind: the upper reaches the lower. But where we are, our ego is too thick and we are used to being selfish. Now we must put aside our ego to pray for Buddhahood, abandon our selfishness to achieve our ambition to save sentient beings. If we are not a great man or a virtuous woman, then our vow to return to the Pure Land will be difficult to establish. This is the second most difficult vow to make. That's why Bodhisattvas call the wish to be born in Ultimate Bliss the making great vow. Here we should pay attention to "establishing a firm vow", meaning that no situation can change our wish for rebirth, whether it is suffering like a ring of red fire on the head, or joy like the throne of the Wheel King with the Heavenly Emperor. Bodhisattvas have a commandment: "Even though you pray for rebirth together, your mind is not interested." And he himself set an example: "If today I cannot see Amitabha Buddha or be born in the Pure Land to achieve all my merits, then even if this body dies, I will not rest." Thanks to making a strong vow, the Bodhisattva was accomplished!

3. Regarding “Happy”, he taught:

A- At the scene: We must stay away from all conditions that can disturb the mind and hinder the path. Accommodation must be simple, to avoid being busy. Every day you have to be free and carefree, so you don't have to worry about anything.

B- In the mind: Must not worry, stop thinking, stop thinking.

C- Regarding practice: You must set a schedule for each day. According to his teachings, every day and night there are at least four times. Each time there is at least one variation of the Amitabha Sutra and a thousand verses of Buddha's name. So every day and night there are at least four repetitions of the Amitabha Sutra and 4,000 Buddha chants. Then gradually increased to 12 sutras and 12,000 Buddha chants every day and night. You have to bow again to Buddha or 100 bows or less each time. And after each session, one must dedicate the merit and vow to be born in the Pure Land with the poem "One-pointed mind and life".

But here we can take advantage of it if we are a person because of inconvenient or weak circumstances, we can also spend less time each day and night and chant less, that is a reluctance, not a solution. If you are a person with great strength and favorable circumstances, you can also increase more, that is diligence, not haste. The important thing is that once you have decided, you must keep it constant, not change it from time to time. It's better to start a little less and then increase it a little more, rather than rush into wanting more and then losing a little. There should also be no interruptions, meaning no meals or no meals. You can also read the text "The Buddha of the Ten Directions and Three Worlds" or other prayers about Ultimate Bliss, according to your preference. If you are healthy and have a lot of hours, you should read the article "Defying the West An Lac Quoc". Because of this song, the words and meaning are very full and passionate.

The first condition, while chanting, must be clear and clear.

Clarity means words and sentences that are clear and not confused. Clear, clear voice, no noise.

The second condition is, the sound must be in harmony with the mind, the mind must be in harmony with the sound, the mind and the sound must be in harmony with each other.

The third condition is, we must be sincere and sincere, with the Father, our heart is like a child missing his mother, with the Pure Land, our heart is like a guest missing his homeland.

The fourth condition, not allowing any commemoration of worldly affairs to be mixed up, means that one must always concentrate on the sound of reciting the Buddha's name, without distraction. If you are distracted, you must immediately record it. In this case, paying attention and reciting with your own voice is the most effective.

The Bodhisattva also told us that when walking, standing, lying down, sitting, eating, drinking, etc., we should face west, so that our mind always remembers the Pure Land, to help the practice of purifying karma quickly come to fruition. Regarding this, we can except when spitting, defecating and urinating, all times we should face the West.

If you follow the conditions taught above and practice, for a period of time, it will continue without interruption and you will be "free of self-recitation". Patriarch Thien Dao and Patriarch Van The call it continuous power of mindfulness. With this continuous power of mindfulness, if you can maintain it for the rest of your life, rebirth is guaranteed. Going further, if you practice diligently and earnestly in reciting without any gaps, inside you forget your body and outside you forget the scene, then you will attain the "Samadhi of Right Memory" also called "Samadhi of Buddha's Recitation" which is also "Single-minded non-chaos". Having received this Samadhi, in the Samadhi, one can be present and see the Compassionate Father along with the Bodhisattva Saints and the Pure Land. That is, "Seeing the Buddha now" is what he taught above, which is also the words of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva in the Shurangama Dharma Assembly.

D- Regarding contemplation: he taught, "The mind is inherently thoughtless". Mindfulness is not external to the mind, so mindfulness is non-thought. Remembrance already means non-thought, so the sentence Amitabha Buddha appears here, does not come from thought, is not due to memory, is not internal, not external, has no appearance, the three times are final, the four are unattainable, free from all illusions, the whole is the true mind. Since the whole is the true mind, it is not the same or different from the wonderful true body of the Buddhas, indistinguishable. Realizing that the whole mind is the mind, the whole mind is the Buddha, the mind and the Buddha are not two, ignorance is destroyed, the dharma body is revealed, the dust of birth and death turns into Nirvana, afflictions and delusions or turns into Bodhi. This is the “The theory of reciting the Buddha with one mind without confusion”, which is also the “The theory of reciting the Buddha with Samadhi”. The person who achieves this "Samadhi" will be reborn in the High Rank, residing in the "Permanent Light of the Pure Land".

E.- After teaching the virtues of “cultivation” and “contemplation” finished, he used the two words “diligence” to summarize.

“Diligence” means diligence. “Specializing” is the time to practice one discipline of reciting the Buddha's name, without interfering with other things. “Need” diligence wins over diligence, don't waste any time, don't waste even a minute or a second. If you practice the Dharma correctly and are diligent and diligent, your merit will surely be achieved.

We can use his verse to combine with the teachings on this part of merit.

Talk less about a story: It means not to interfere with other things so that you can concentrate on practicing Buddha's name on the one hand.

Reciting a Buddha's name many times: Reciting the Buddha's name a lot is being diligent, but also being dedicated to reciting the Buddha's name.

Thus, the first two sentences of the verse summarize the "cultivation" part, meaning he teaches to diligently recite the Buddha's name. If you practice according to this, you will achieve continuous mindfulness and reach the level of "Buddha-reciting Samadhi", where all delusions and afflictions have been suppressed:

Kill false thoughts

The human Dharma body is revealed.

The last two sentences of the verse refer to the part of witnessing the “Recital of Buddha Samadhi”. Achieving the wonderful principle of "All thought is mind, whole mind is Buddha", is to realize the Dharma body, and all delusions and afflictions have been eliminated.

Bodhisattva Enlightenment Miraculous Conduct teaches about the Dharma of reciting Buddha's name, which covers faith, conduct, and vows. First is the virtue, from the predestined environment to the mind, both the practice and the principles are very clear, accurate and very complete. We should read and reread every day, reviewing our meritorious deeds of reciting the Buddha's name, so that they are completely in accordance with what the Bodhisattva taught: If we use our efforts completely in accordance with what the Bodhisattva taught, then we will definitely achieve pure karma, and the nine levels of golden lotus will be firmly held in our hands.

--- o0o ---

tieu_de: CHAPTER SEVEN - THE PATRIARCHS OF THE CONTACT sect
tom_tat: In this chapter, we briefly describe the biographies and teachings of the Patriarchs who preserve and spread the Pure Land Dharma of the Original Master in Eastern Asia. Starting from Patriarch Hui Vien to Patriarch Triet Ngu, the general transmission is...
noi_dung:
CHAPTER SEVEN - THE PATRIARCHS OF THE CONTACT sect

In this chapter, we briefly describe the biographies and teachings of the Patriarchs who preserve and spread the Pure Land Dharma of the Original Master in Eastern Asia. Starting from Patriarch Hui Vien to Patriarch Triet Ngu, there were a total of 11 transmissions. Before Patriarch Huiyuan, the Pure Land Dharma had already been passed down in the East and many people practiced it, but the systematic organization and regulation was in its infancy during Patriarch Huiyuan's time. Therefore, he is the First Patriarch of the Pure Land sect in the East.

After Patriarch Triet Ngo, there were certainly many Patriarchs who succeeded him, because the Patriarch passed away in the 15th year of Gia Khanh in the Qing Dynasty, from then until now it has been more than a century; Moreover, during the Republic of Korea period, this method was very popular and the four groups of people were successful and had countless experiences (see the book The Four Groups of Rebirth, which is the next volume of this series). But because the documents for help can only go to Patriarch Triet Ngo, we have to temporarily stop at the 11th Patriarch.

---o0o---

tieu_de: I. EARLY ANCESTOR HUE VIEN GREAT MASTER
tom_tat: Master Hue Yuan's family name is Co, from Nhan Mon. When he was young, he was naturally studious and learned Confucianism and was very good at Taoist doctrine.
noi_dung:
I. EARLY ANCESTOR HUE VIEN GREAT MASTER

Master Hue Yuan's family name is Co, from Nhan Mon. As a child, he was naturally studious and learned Confucianism and was very good at the doctrines of Lao and Zhuang.

At that time, Dharma Master Dao An established Hang Son pagoda and gathered monks to preach the Dharma. He heard the sound of loving virtue, so he went to Hang Son to take refuge with the Dharma Master.

When he heard Dharma Master Dao An preach the Prajnaparamita Sutra, his mind opened and he understood the wonderful truth. He then lamented: "Who would have thought that Buddha's vehicle is profound and wonderful! All this time, I have spent all my effort chasing after the waste of Confucius, Strong, Lao, and Zhuang!"

Then he asked to become a monk, taking the Dharma name Hue Vien.

From then on, he devoted himself day and night to reading, thinking, and practicing. Dharma Master Dao An saw that he was diligent and praised him: "Buddhism will be circulated in the Middle East, it's all because of this place in Hue Vien."

In the 6th year of Thai Nguon, Tan Dynasty, when he came to Tam Duong, he saw the spacious and quiet Lo Son mountain, a place to practice religion, so he established a monastery there, named Long Tuyen.

At that time, Dharma Master Hue Vinh, his fellow monk, established Tay Lam Pagoda in the West of Lo Son and invited him to return to Tay Lam Pagoda with him.

After a while, there were too many students following him, Tay Lam pagoda did not have enough space, so he wanted to establish another temple in the East of Lo Son. The mountain god came to ask for offerings of wood. Then, after a night of heavy rain and strong wind, the trees piled up in disarray. The Governor Hoan Y was determined to build a forest for him. Because the Mountain God offered wood and to the Tay Lam pagoda, he named it "Dong Lam Than Van pagoda".

When the place was quiet, he immediately urged the crowd to practice the religion and dug a pond to plant lotus. On the surface of the water float a 12-petalled wooden lotus. Every hour the water floods one wing, using timed practice. Called Contraband.

Visit the great intellectuals who are devoutly religious

in the four directions, like Giac Hien and Buddha Da Gia

Xa, Luu Di Dan, Vuong Kieu Chi, etc. heard his voice so they came to join the group to practice. There were 123 people. He said: "Are you people who are determined to go to the Pure Land if you come to this place?". He then created statues of Amitabha, Avalokiteshvara, and The Chi. Established a Lien Commune Association and asked Mr. Liu Di Dan to write a vow to engrave it on a stone stele. Those who attended the meeting diligently practiced the Dharma, day and night in the six periods without delay, all attained Samadhi one after another, and were all reborn. At the time of death, there was always a dialogue.

He once had words to promote the meaning of Samadhi:

- What do you call that Samadhi? That is, “specializing in thoughts” so.

“Concentrate” when the mind is in the first place. “Remembering the President” is a time when the spirit is empty and divine. When air is empty, wisdom is found in reason. The spirit of light is not penetrated into any hidden place.

Again, there are many Samadhis, but they are easy to obtain and the merit is high. Only the Buddha-reciting Samadhi is the best. Because in the same illusory place, the ultimate place of transcendence, the title “Tathagata” is proclaimed. “Universe union”, “Divine transformation” are incomparable. That's why people who enter this Samadhi are mentally absent from all knowledge. It is in that predestined scene that one becomes wisdom. Bright wisdom shines throughout the place and all phenomena appear so clearly. Where eyes and ears cannot reach, you can still see and hear. Still seeing and hearing but the mind is still absent, absent but naturally clear. Because of clarity, when studying the original mind, stagnation immediately becomes absent-minded...

He saw that the Sutra collection in Jiang Dong was lacking, so he sent his disciples across the mountains and forests to Tay Thien to request the Sutras. There are nearly a hundred Sutras circulating from Lo Son.

He has a collection of works called "Dharma Nature Treatise" that invents the eternal pleasure of Nirvana. This treatise was transmitted to Quan Trung. Dharma Master Kumarajiva saw it and immediately praised: "Mr. Vien in the border area has not read the "Great Nirvana Sutra", but the reasoning is in line with reason."

He lived in Lo Son for more than 30 years, but never stepped foot down the mountain once. Day and night, he focused his attention on the Pure Land, quietly contemplating.

Three times he saw the Buddha and the Saints appear, but he was quiet and did not say anything.

In the 12th year of Nghia Hy, on the night of July 30, he sat in meditation at the Prajnaparamita. As soon as he came out of concentration, he opened his eyes and saw Amitabha Buddha appearing in the void with countless saints. In the light there are countless transformed Buddhas. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva appears on the left, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva appears on the right. Buddha and Bodhisattva both sit on beautiful, bright jeweled lotus thrones. Fourteen rays of light swirled up and down like a faucet, resounding with voices speaking the dharmas: Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, Anatta, the Paramitas..."

The Buddha told him: "Because of the power of my vow, I have come to comfort you now. After seven days you will be born in my country."

He again saw friends in Lien Xa who had passed away before, such as Buddha Da Gia Xa, Hue Tri, Hue Vinh, Luu Di Dan, etc., all standing behind the Buddha. They stepped forward and clasped their hands to greet him and said to him: "Master, you soon made up your mind to return to the Pure Land, why is it so late?"

The next day, he told his disciples: Phap Tinh, Hue Buu, etc. and said: "I was here in Lo Son, in the first 11 years, three times I saw the Buddha and the Saints appear. Now I see the Buddha's prediction again. I will definitely be born in the Pure Land."

Then he composed his own regulations for the masses to follow and practice together.

On August 6, he said goodbye to the assembly, then sat down and passed away, at the age of 83.

Excerpts from the series:

“The Tale of Dong Lam”, “The Book of Lo Son”

---o0o---

tieu_de: II. SECOND PATRIARCH THIEN DAO GREAT MASTER
tom_tat: Master Thien Dao was from the Tang Dynasty. During the year of Trinh Quan, he saw the text "Pure Land Nine-Level Path Trang" by Zen Master Dao Xuoc, and was very happy and said: "This is the real path to quickly become a Buddha. Practicing other practices around the world...
noi_dung:
II. SECOND PATRIARCH THIEN DAO GREAT MASTER

Master Thien Dao was from the Tang Dynasty. During the year of Trinh Quan, he saw the text "Pure Land Nine-Level Path Trang" by Dao Xuoc Zen Master, and was very happy and said: "This is the real path to quickly become a Buddha. Practicing other disciplines around the world is difficult to achieve. This Dharma-only discipline quickly escapes birth and death."

From then on, he devoted himself diligently to chanting day and night. Not long after, he went to Truong An to encourage the four groups to recite Buddha's name.

Every time he went into the hut and knelt down to recite Buddha's name, if he was not exhausted yet, he did not rest. When the time comes, I will explain the Pure Land Dharma to them.

Needing to practice hard himself and diligently teach others, for thirty full years, he did not sleep or rest.

He also had strict morality and never made any mistakes, even if they were small.

When he was offered food, good food, he told them to serve it to them, but he only used bad things.

With all the resources he donated from the altar, he used to describe more than 100,000 Amitabha Sutras and three hundred paintings of Pure Land scenes. In addition, it is used to repair pagodas and towers, light lamps, and not leave any residue.

There were so many monks and laymen who came to worship him that they numbered tens of thousands. Everyone felt his teachings, so everyone diligently practiced. People at that time recited the Amitabha Sutra from ten thousand to fifty thousand times. People recite Buddha's name every day and night from ten thousand to ten thousand sentences. There are countless people who have attained Samadhi at the moment of death and will be reborn. The number is indescribable.

Someone asked: "Does reciting Buddha's name ensure rebirth?"

He replied: "If you try to recite Buddha's name, your wish will be fulfilled."

After answering, he chanted "Amitabha Buddha" to himself, and immediately a ray of light shot out from his mouth following the chanting sound. He recited ten to a hundred sentences, and for each sentence, a long ray of light flashed out one after another, illuminating the entire temple.

This miracle was transmitted to the court, King Cao Tong served a sign declaring the pagoda "Quang Minh Tu".

He has a verse of advice for life like this:

Gradually, my hair turns gray

Slowly walking in clumps

Even though: the house is full of gold and gems

There is no cure: old age, sickness and suffering

Even though he was happy with everything

Death will come eventually

There is only a shortcut to practice

Just recite “Amitabha Buddha”

Someone asked: "Why doesn't the Venerable teach people to visualize the Buddha, but only tells people to recite the Buddha's name?".

He replied: "The karma of sentient beings is heavy, their minds are rough, but the Holy scene is very subtle and wonderful. With a bustling consciousness, it is difficult to achieve insight. For that reason, the Buddha mercifully advised those who specialize in claiming the name.

Because claiming a name is an easy practice, the mind quickly gains continuity. If one can recite continuously for the rest of one's life, then if ten people recite, ten people will be reborn, if a hundred people recite, a hundred people will be reborn.

Why is that so?

Because there are no impurities, one can be mindful. Because it is compatible with Amitabha Buddha's original vow. Because it does not go against the Bible. Because it follows Buddha's teachings.

If we abandon the practice of reciting the Buddha's name and practice many other mixed karma practices, it will be difficult for hundreds of thousands of practitioners to have three or four people liberated.

Why so?

Because of mixed conditions, one loses mindfulness. Because it is not compatible with Buddha's original vow. Because it goes against the Bible. Because they do not follow Buddha's teachings. Because photography cannot be continuous. Because the mind does not often remember Buddha's gratitude. Because even practicing Buddhism is often associated with fame and profit. Because liking to pursue miscellaneous things hinders the right conduct of rebirth for oneself and others.

Recently, we have seen that monks and laypeople in different places practice different practices: some people specialize in practicing, others like mixed practices.

If you concentrate on reciting the Buddha's name, then ten people will be determined to be reborn. As for miscellaneous conduct without single-mindedness, it will be difficult for thousands of practitioners to attain liberation.

I hope that everyone should think carefully, walk, stand, lie down, sit, and hold their thoughts firmly on the Buddha, day and night, do not let them slip, and swear until their last breath. If one recites before death, the next one immediately gives birth to Ultimate Bliss. From now on, for countless kalpas of asankhyas, I will enjoy the Dharma of endless happiness until I become a Buddha. Isn't that so much fun?

He once taught a method to aid mindfulness for people at the time of death:

Every person at the time of death wants to be reborn in the Pure Land, and must not be afraid of death. You should think to yourself like this: this retribution is the root of suffering. It is a leather bag filled with dirty things. It is the root of all suffering. If we can leave this pile of stinking meat and be reborn in the Pure Land, receive a golden and diamond body, enjoy immeasurable pure joy, and be completely liberated from the cycle of birth and death. Like taking off a torn shirt and exchanging it for respect, there's nothing more pleasant than that.

Thinking like that, then let go of your body and mind, don't have thoughts of attachment. As soon as he got sick, he meditated on impermanence and recited Buddha's name single-mindedly, waiting for death.

It is also necessary to tell family members and visitors to recite Buddha's name whenever they come near you. Make sure not to talk about life or that, or about housework. There's no need to wish for peace and happiness, because it's all useless.

If the patient is seriously ill and is about to die, relatives should not cry or cry, their eyes and nose should not have runny eyes, which would disturb the patient's mind and destroy the patient's mindfulness. We should only remind people to remember Buddha, recite Buddha's name, meditate on Buddha, and recite Buddha's name loudly together to help the patient be mindful. Thus, it is always time for the patient to stop breathing. But you should not rush to touch the body, you should take turns chanting for as long as possible.

From illness until death, if someone who understands the Pure Land Dharma often comes to remind and advise you, you will be very lucky.

Using that method of supporting recitation, there is no doubt about rebirth.

Dying is a very big thing, you need to work hard and make an effort to do it yourself. One wrong thought will surely lead to suffering for many lifetimes. Who can replace me? You should judge for yourself! So think for yourself!

One day, He quickly told everyone: "This body is boring, I am about to return to the Pure Land."

Then he climbed to the top of the willow tree in front of the pagoda, clasped his hands facing the West and prayed: "Please Buddha guide me, Bodhisattva help me not to lose mindfulness so I can be born in the Pure Land."

After praying, he threw himself down. The body gently falls and naturally sits cross-legged upright on the ground.

The crowd rushed over, he had already passed away.

Excerpts from the series:

“Buddhist Patriarch Ky” “Lac Ban Van Loai”

A story of rebirth due to the power of recitation, confirming the Patriarch's words.

---o0o---

DUONG LIEN HANG

Excerpted from the series: “The Tale of Modern Life and Rebirth”

Mr. Duong Lien Hang is from Triet Giang. The family was poor, and when he was young, he worked as a trader.

In the 2nd year of the Republic of China, he often went back and forth to study Buddhist principles with lay people Giac Hang. Although his literature was limited, the places he understood were better than others.

In September of the Year of the Pig, friends in the Buddha Recitation Association in the village together took the oath to "Develop the Bodhi mind". Mr. Lien Hang immediately asked to attend the meeting and took the oath.

In the year of the Rat, at the end of Spring, due to illness, he secretly broke the precept of not killing, and from then on distanced himself from his friends.

That July night, his illness got worse. His friends came to visit and gave him advice. As for him, he also knew that he could not be strong, so he repented deeply. On July 8, he recovered from his illness and came before the Buddha to reveal the city. I surrendered myself to repentance, vowing not to dare to violate the precepts again. From that moment on, I quit everything, stopped craving, and focused on reciting Buddha's name, waiting for death.

His friends knew that he was not good at reciting Buddha's name, so on the 11th, they invited people to come to his house to help him recite. On the full moon day, the Dharma friends take turns coming to help recite; Also from this full moon day, his spirit gradually became brighter and his body became healthy.

On the 17th, he told everyone that in his dream he saw light like five or six electric lights. In the evening, seeing that he was still as bright as usual, his friends thought he was okay. So after a while of loudly reciting Buddha's name, the Dharma friends were about to go home to rest. Who would have thought that at that time, the recital aid was effective. He heard silence, then called out, "I haven't been to the West yet, I need to ask my friends to help me recite all night long."

Everyone heard what he said had a strange meaning, so they loudly recited Buddha's name together. After half an hour, he suddenly laughed and said: "I have reached the Pure Land. Oh! The lotus is so beautiful! Oh! The treasure pond is so vast! The light is so beautiful!" Then he instructed everyone to try to help him chant. From now on, he lay still without moving, his eyes staring at the Buddha statue on the table in front of his bed. In the early morning of the 18th, his eyes closed once and his breathing was complete. There were only 4 of his fellow monks, but the whole night they chanted without stopping. They chanted until an hour and a half after he was out of breath, then called others to recite for him and did not let his relatives mourn. At ten o'clock in the afternoon, everyone examined his body, all places were cold. Only the top of the head was still warm.

Mr. Duong Lien Hang was reborn thanks to the help of his friends. That year he was 30 years old.

ADDITIONAL NOTES - Mr. Lien Hang's recitation of the Buddha was poor but he broke the precept of "no killing". Thanks to his fellow monks who tried their best to assist him in reciting, he was able to be mindful in the present and was reborn. When he was reborn, he experienced two things: 1.- Even until he stopped breathing, his mindfulness remained steady. 2.- The whole body is cold, only the top of the head is still hot. When a human being dies, the top of his head becomes hot at the end, which is a symptom of becoming a saint. People who are reborn in the Pure Land immediately join the ranks of Saints, stay at the "irreversible" level, and completely escape the cycle of birth and death, so the top of their head is the last to get hot.

Why is supporting recitation so powerful?

Because everyone, in addition to the body of the four elements, everyone has a consciousness, which is the nature of understanding. That nature of understanding is the function of the mind's own body (eighth consciousness). This mind body includes all the powers of all uses, and depending on the pure, good and evil conditions, it manifests the bodies and scenes of all Holy mortals. When you are about to die, it is the time when your functions appear, your current body is about to end, and it is also the time when another energy will follow the predestined conditions to become your use to form a future body.

Thanks to the strong support of mindfulness, even though the person is about to die, the Holy karma of rebirth has not yet been achieved, but the supernatural power is available, the mind immediately follows the conditions of mindfulness and successfully uses it to form a pure body: the right retribution and the retribution in Ultimate Bliss.

This good result is due to two things: A.- Supporting conditions. B.- Righteousness.

Supporting conditions1. Get rid of all worries such as family and career matters, relatives crying, etc.

2. The person supporting the recitation must be sincere and dedicated to following the Dharma.

Righteousness1. The dying person must forget all life matters.

2. We must single-mindedly and earnestly remember Buddha and recite Buddha's name, like a child falling into a deep pit, hoping for his mother to come save him.

The first supporting condition is to help the first right person, because only by eliminating all preoccupations can the dying person be able to forget all things in life.

The second part of supporting conditions is to help create the second right cause, because if the person who supports reciting is devoted to the right Dharma, only then can mindfulness arise in the person about to die.

People who are about to die, if they have enough support and righteous causes, now decide to be reborn, regardless of whether they are long-time practitioners or those who have just converted to faith, and also regardless of whether they are good people or evil people. In the next volume of this series, we will see many experiences in the brief history of the four reincarnated beings.

---o0o---

tieu_de: III. GREAT MASTER OF THE THREE VETERANS
tom_tat: The great master first studied with Tang Zen Master in Chengdu, then studied with New Zen Master in Sichuan, then went to Kinh Chau to study with Chan Zen Master in Ngoc.
noi_dung:
III. GREAT MASTER OF THE THREE VETERANS

Excerpted from the series:

“Liu Tzu Hau Van Tap”

The great master first studied with Zen Master Tang in Chengdu, then studied with Tan Zen Master in Sichuan, then went to Kinh Chau to study with Chan Master in Ngoc Tuyen.

After achieving great enlightenment and achieving spiritual power, Chan Master told him to come to Hoanh Son to save people.

At first, he came to live under the rocks on the southwest side of Mount Hoanh. When someone donated rice and porridge, every day he didn't donate, he ate mud and never donated, until he was thin and pale, with only a tattered robe on his body.

As for evangelism, he stood in the middle and taught people the method of reciting Buddha's name to quickly achieve success.

He wrote the Buddha's teachings on the side of the road and ravine. Engrave the Dharma on rocks and walls. Devotedly advise people who are not tired.

Not long after, people believed in him and counted them in tens of thousands. Then some people brought money and rice, some people cut down trees and used wood, everyone agreed to build a temple and a temple. He remained calm, did not refuse, nor told to do anything. Not long after, the wild forest cluster changed into a massive "Amitabha Temple" scene.

As for him, he is still in the same condition as raw rice. If anyone gives extra alms, they should give it to help the poor, hungry, and disabled.

In the 18th year of Trinh Nguon, Tang Dynasty, on the 19th day of the 7th month, he passed away at Amitabha Pagoda, at the age of 91.

Previously, there was Mr. Thich Phap Chieu in Lo Son. One day, he entered meditation and traveled to the Pure Land. Seeing a monk wearing torn robes standing next to the Buddha. The Buddha pointed to that monk and told Mr. Phap Chieu: "This is Mr. Thua Vien from Hoanh Son!".

After coming out of samadhi, Mr. Phap Chieu went to Hoanh Son to look for him. When he met him, it was clear that the monk with torn robes had seen him in samadhi, so he asked to follow him.

After his death, Mr. Phap Chieu went to preach in various places, and was appointed National Teacher by King Dai Tong of the Tang Dynasty. Phap Reflects on his teacher's virtue to the king. The king immediately turned towards Hoanh Son and bowed. Then the king ordered that his residence be called "Uncle Chu Dao Trang", and ordered Mr. Lieu Ton Nguon to compose a memorial essay engraved on a stone stele erected next to Di Da pagoda.

---o0o---

tieu_de: IV. GREAT MASTER OF THE FOUR FRACTIONS
tom_tat: Master Phap Chieu initially lived at Van Phong Pagoda in Hoanh Chau diligently cultivating
noi_dung:
IV. GREAT MASTER OF THE FOUR FRACTIONS

Excerpted from the series: “Tong Cao Tang Truyen”,

“Lac Ban Van Loai”

Master Phap Chieu initially lived at Van Phong Pagoda in Hoanh Chau diligently practicing.

In the fourth year of the Tang Dynasty, he opened a Buddhist chanting hall at Ho Dong Pagoda. On the opening day of the festival, feeling the auspicious clouds spread over, in the clouds appeared the palace, Amitabha Buddha and Avalokiteśvara, Mahasthamaprapta appeared in golden incarnations shining throughout the entire void. Throughout Hoanh Chau city, men and women, young and old, set up tables to burn incense and pay their respects.

Because Buddha and Bodhisattva manifested themselves like that, everyone developed the mind to diligently practice the Dharma. In this ashram, he opened five meetings.

In the fifth year of the Great Calendar, he met Manjushri and Samantabhadra, two great Bodhisattvas, at the "Great Saint Truc Lam Temple" in Ngu Dai Mountain. The two Bodhisattvas advised him to concentrate on the Buddha's name Dharma to educate everyone. They also predicted that he would be reborn in the Pure Land and quickly attain Supreme Bodhi.

During the reign of King Duc Tong, he opened a Buddhist recitation center in Tinh Chau and had five meetings.

Every late night, the king and people in the palace often heard the very clear sound of Buddha's name chanting. The king then sent people to follow the sound to find it and after realizing it was the sound of reciting Buddha's name at the ashram in Tinh Chau. The king then sent a messenger to bring him a ceremony to invite him to the court.

He opened a Buddhist recitation center at the royal palace and had five meetings. That's why people call it "The Five Associations of Mages".

One day, while he was concentrating on reciting Buddha's name, suddenly a Holy Monk appeared to him and told him: "The Dharma Master's precious lotus has been completed. Three years later it will bloom." Having finished speaking, the Saint immediately hid.

Exactly three years later, he gathered the assembly and said: "I am returning to Pure Land, everyone must strive to practice diligently."

Having finished his instructions, he immediately sat down and passed away.

---o0o---

tieu_de: V. GREAT MASTER THIEN KHUONG, FIVE ANCESTORS
tom_tat: Young Master Khuong, surnamed Chau, from Tien Do. As a child, mute from birth. At the age of seven, he followed his mother to Linh Son Pagoda to worship Buddha. Mother pointed at Buddha and jokingly asked: “You know someone
noi_dung:
V. GREAT MASTER THIEN KHUONG, FIVE ANCESTORS

Excerpted from the series: “Tong Cao Tang Truyen”

“Lac Ban Van Loai”

Young Master Khuong, surnamed Chau, from Tien Do. As a child, mute from birth. At the age of seven, he followed his mother to Linh Son Pagoda to worship Buddha. Mother pointed at Buddha and jokingly asked: "Do you know someone?".

He suddenly replied: "Shakyamuni Buddha".

Knowing that he had a good relationship with Buddhism, his parents allowed him to become a monk.

At the age of 15, he mastered five sets of Sutras.

During the Tang Dynasty, in the first year of Trinh Nguyen, he visited Bach Ma Pagoda in Luoyang. Seeing a light shining out of the place where the scriptures were stored in the hall, he looked to see, and the light came from the collection of writings "The Western Way of Transformation" by the Second Patriarch Thien Dao. He bowed and said, “If I have an affinity with the Pure Land, may this collection of writings once again radiate light.” As soon as he finished his vow, that collection of writings immediately illuminated; In the bold light there is the Bodhisattva. He said: "The stones of life may wear out, but if you wish, I will never change."

Then he went to Truong An to worship the statue of the Second Patriarch Thien Dao Great Master. During the ceremony, the Patriarch's statue suddenly flew up into the sky and a voice told him: "If you follow my teachings, save all sentient beings, the day after your achievements, you will be born in the Pure Land."

He went to Giang Lang and met a monk who said: "If you want to preach, you should go to Tan Dinh, the opportunity is there." Having finished speaking, the monk suddenly disappeared.

When he arrived at Tan Dinh, he found that no one in that country knew what reciting Buddha's name was. He collected money and then persuaded children to recite Buddha's name. At first, the children recited a Buddha verse and he rewarded them with money. After ten times, you'll be rewarded with one coin. After a while, even without a reward, they recite it. Before he was present, they recited. After that, wherever and whenever they are, they still recite. They recite Buddha's name on the street, they recite Buddha's name at home. More than a year later, everyone in Tan Dinh knew how to recite Buddha's name, and men and women, old and young, whenever they saw him, immediately recited "Amitabha Buddha". People moved their hands to their mouths and mumbled, the sound of reciting Buddha's name echoed everywhere.

He then established the Pure Land ashram in O Long Son, building a three-step altar. Every New Year's Day, good men and women gather there to recite Buddha's name and listen to the Dharma. Usually the number of people meeting is over three thousand. He sat on a high throne, loudly chanting Buddha's name and the crowd joined in. He recited a sentence, the people of the time saw a small Buddha coming out of his mouth, ten sentences were ten Buddhas, connected together like a string. He told the crowd: "You have seen the Buddha, you will surely be reborn." Everyone was very happy.

In the 21st year of Trinh Nguyen, October, he gathered all the monks and laity together and advised: “With this evil and impure world, everyone should be bored; with that Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, they should wholeheartedly increase their efforts. Whoever can see my light at this time is truly my disciple.”

Having finished speaking, he opened his hands and released a few long rays of light, then sat still and passed away.

The masses built his tower in Taiyan, named Dharma Master Tainan.

---o0o---

tieu_de: VI. GREAT MASTER DIEN THO OF THE SIX Ancestral Patriarch
tom_tat: Great Master Dien Tho, from Tien Duong, surnamed Vuong, surnamed Chong Huyen. When I was young, I often recited the Lotus Sutra and felt the goats kneel down to listen
noi_dung:
VI. GREAT MASTER DIEN THO OF THE SIX Ancestral Patriarch

Excerpted from the series: “Lac Ban Van Loai”

“All Good Things Come Together”

Great Master Dien Tho, from Tien Duong, surnamed Vuong, surnamed Chong Huyen. When I was a teenager, I often recited the Lotus Sutra and felt the goats kneeling down to listen to the Sutra.

When he grew up, he became a tax official for Van Muc Vuong. Many times he used his salary to go to Tay Ho to buy fish to release. The taking of public money was discovered. The judge assessed his crime as worthy of death.

When leading him to be beheaded, Van Muc Vuong secretly sent someone to follow him to watch his face. If he looked sad or scared, he should be beheaded, but if he was still happy and calm, he should be brought back to report. From the moment he was led away until the moment he was about to be beheaded, his face still showed no signs of fear or sadness, but rather a look of joy. The messenger immediately transmitted Van Muc Vuong's order to the eunuch to behead him and then bring him back to present to the Vuong.

Vuong asked: "Aren't you afraid of being cut to death?"

He replied: "I used a large amount of money from the public treasury, a crime worthy of death, but I used all that money to buy back the lives of millions of lives. I believe that due to that merit of liberating sentient beings, even if this body dies, I will be reborn in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Therefore, I have no fear."

Van Muc Vuong was moved and ordered an acquittal. He asked to become a monk, Vuong agreed.

He came to Tu Minh to receive Dharma teachings from Zen Master Druid Nham. Afterwards, he studied with Master Thieu Quoc in Thien Thai to invent the heart essence, and was approved by Master Thieu Quoc.

He once practiced "Phap Hoa Repentance" at Quoc Thanh Pagoda. While meditating, he saw Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva pouring orange juice into his mouth, from which he gained unhindered eloquence.

Even though he practiced "Zen", his heart was devoted to "Purity". Because he wanted a place to focus, he went to the Zen monastery of Great Master Tri Gia and made two lottery cards, one with the title "One-pointed meditation" and the other with "Dignified Pure Land". Then he sincerely turned to the Three Jewels and drew lots. Always draw the card "Dignified Pure Land" seven times. From now on, he single-mindedly cultivated pure karma.

In the second year of Kien Long, Song Dynasty, King Trung Y invited him to become the abbot of Vinh Minh Pagoda, his title being Tri Giac Zen Master. He stayed in Vinh Minh for 15 years and saved 1,700 monks.

Every day and night, the Great Master performed 108 exercises. The Great Master often transmitted the Bodhisattva precepts, bought and released lives, gave food to ghosts and gods, and all merits were dedicated to the Pure Land. At night, he went to another mountain to recite Buddha's name, counting the number of ten thousand verses as approximately. People near the place where he recited Buddha's name sometimes heard the melodious sound of loudspeakers. As for the Lotus Sutra, during his lifetime he recited one hundred and three thousand volumes. He has a collection of 100 volumes of "Zong Canh Luc", which contains the same teachings of three sects: Hoa Nghiem, Phap Hoa, and Only Consciousness.

He wrote the volume "Van Thien Cong Quy", in this volume, about the passage about returning to the Pure Land, the essential words and outline are as follows.

Question: Mind-only Pure Land and all ten directions, why do you base your mind on equanimity, but pray to be reborn on the platform, sending your body to Ultimate Bliss? So where is the door of non-birth, and if you have a mind that is impure and likes to be pure, where will you become equal?

Answer: Being born in the Pure Land of idealism is the part of one who attains self-centeredness. The Sutra "The Tathagata Is Not Thoughtful Realm" says: "All Buddhas of the three worlds are only mind-centered, so that depending on patience, they can either enter the first ground, surrender their body according to patience, or enter the first ground, surrender their body and quickly be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss." Because of this, we know that only those who attain self-centeredness will be born in the Pure Land, while those who are attached to the world will only end up in the predestined scene. Once there is cause and effect that is not wrong, it is clear that outside the mind there is no real dharma.

Again, the equanimity gate also refers to the realm of non-birth, even if one believes in the Buddha's words, but strictly because one's strength is not enough, the mind is shallow, the mind is coarse, the world is strong, the habit is heavy, one needs to be born in the Pure Land, to be able to rely on superior conditions and patience to easily achieve and quickly complete the Bodhisattva path.

The Ten Thoughts say: Even though a wise person strongly seeks rebirth in the Pure Land, the truth of birth cannot be attained, that is, true non-birth. This is the meaning "because the mind is pure, Buddha's land is pure". Stupid people are bound by "birth": when they hear "birth" they immediately think it is "birth", when they hear "no birth" they immediately think it is "no birth" without understanding the reason: "Birth is non-birth, non-birth is birth" so they argue with each other. This is a person with wrong views and blasphemy.

Question: Besides the mind without dharma and the Buddha without return, why do we see the Buddha and the Buddha comes to receive us?

Answer: Mind-only recites the Buddha's name, uses mind-only to contemplate all ten thousand dharmas. Having clearly understood that the scene is the mind, knowing that the mind is Buddha, so wherever one recites it is Buddha.

The Eightfold Samadhi Sutra says: "Like a person in a dream sees seven treasures, and his relatives are happy. When he wakes up, he remembers and thinks back, not knowing where the rich scene he just saw is. Reciting the Buddha's name is the same."

This is an example of the "scene" created by the "mind", which exists but does not exist, so there is no Buddha, neither future nor past. Again, "like an illusion that is not real, then the mind and the Buddha will both disappear." But "it is not that there are no illusions, then the mind and the Buddha are clear". "No" and "yes" are already unobstructed, so even though there is no past or future, there is no fear of seeing the Buddha coming. Seeing is not seeing, usually in line with the middle path. That's why the real Buddha does not come, nor does the mind go, but touches the path and communicates with the mind and sees for itself. Like someone who commits a serious crime, feels like hell. Duy Thuc Luan says:

"All are like people from hell who see good hell, etc., doing things that are painful for themselves." For that reason, it is all due to the evil karma of the perpetrator that appears, there is no real bronze dog or iron snake outside the mind. All things and all dharmas in life are like that.

Question: The Contemplation Sutra teaches 16 methods of contemplation, all of which involve cultivating the mind and cultivating concentration. Contemplating the Buddha's good form to see clearly is enough to reach the pure realm. How can a person with a scattered mind be reborn?

Answer: The nine levels of Ultimate Bliss have high and low levels, including the upper, middle and lower levels, but not beyond these two minds:

A.- “Concentrate the mind”, practice concentration at the time of High-class rebirth.

B.- “Concentrate”, only focus on reciting the name and practicing good deeds, then dedicate the vow to achieve the following results. But it takes a lifetime of diligence. When sitting or lying down, you must face west. During times of religious practice, respect, dedication, and vows, one must fervently pray without distraction. As if being imprisoned, as if being captured by the enemy, as if being drifted or burned, with one heart I pray to Buddha for help, vowing to escape the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death and return to the Pure Land, quickly attain non-birth and save all living beings, to ascend to the throne of the Three Jewels, and repay the four graces. If anyone is willing to do so, it will definitely bring results.

Such as unworthy speech, weak faith and vows, unfocused mind, not always connected but often distracted. Relaxing like that, when the time comes to seek rebirth, I'm afraid that karma will prevent you from meeting good friends. The body is stressed and suffering, making it difficult to maintain mindfulness. Because now this is the "cause", at the time of death it is the "effect". If you worry about “cause and effect” then “you will definitely not be in vain”. Like a gentle voice that resonates gently. Just like the picture, the shadow is straight.

If you want to achieve the ten recitations at the time of your death, in the present time, you must prepare in advance to concentrate on reciting the Buddha's name, contain the group of merits, dedicate it to pray for rebirth, reciting the Buddha's name without forgetting the Buddha, without leaving the Pure Land. Only then will you be certain and not worry.

Furthermore, the two paths "good" and "evil", the two consequences "suffering" and "joy" are all caused by three karma (body, speech, mind).

If the mind is angry or sexually immoral: that is the karma of Hell.

Being stingy and greedy without giving alms: that is the karma of hungry ghosts.

Stupid and stupid: is the karma of Animal birth.

Being arrogant and paying high tribute: is the karma of Asura.

Persistence in the five precepts: is human karma.

Cultivating the ten good deeds: is the karma of God.

Realizing the cause of emptiness: is the karma of Shravaka.

Understanding clearly the condition of birth without nature: is the karma of Pratyekabuddha.

Cultivating the six levels: is the Bodhisattva's karma.

True compassion and equality: is Buddha's karma.

If the mind is pure, then the golden pedestal and precious flowers will be born in the Pure Land. As for the filthy thoughts, the time will be filled with mounds and pits, and birth will be in the impure realm. These are all "parametic results", feeling the "higher fate". Therefore, cause and effect, apart from the mind, have no other separate self. If you want to receive pure retribution, you must practice pure virtue. Just as water flows down and fire rises up, of course it is like that, there is no doubt.

Because people studying Buddhism at that time were confused about "Zen" and "Pureness", not knowing which one to practice was better and more certain, so he had four verses to compare the benefits and harms of the two subjects:

I. There is Zen but no Pure Land

Ten people practice, nine people gradually

Warm scene if present money

At first, follow it.

II. Without Zen, there is Pure Land

Ten people practice, ten are reborn

Dang near Amitabha Buddha

Why worry about not being enlightened?

III. There is Zen and there is Pure Land

Like a strong tiger with horns

Currently living as a teacher

In the next life, I will become a Buddha or Patriarch.

IV. Neither Zen nor Pure Land

An iron bed with copper pillars awaits

Forever and thousands of lives

There is no place to rely on.

Song Dynasty, the eighth year of Khai Buu, on February 26, waking up early in the morning, he lit incense to worship Buddha. After the ceremony, he gathered the assembly to give instructions and instructions, then sat cross-legged on the dharma seat and passed away at the age of 72.

A little while later, a monk from Lam Xuyen came to the temple and paid homage to the Great Master's stupa for a full year. The decanter asked. The monk replied: "Last year, I was sick, my consciousness entered darkness, and I saw a statue of a Venerable on the side of the temple. Minh Vuong respectfully bowed. I asked the reason, and then I learned that it was the statue of Zen Master Dien Tho at Vinh Minh Pagoda in Hangzhou. He was reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss as a high-ranking monk. Minh Vuong values ​​his virtue and should worship him."

---o0o---

tieu_de: VII. That Patriarch of Provincial Thuong Thuong Grand Master
tom_tat: Master Tinh Thuong, from Tien Duong, surnamed Nhan, surname Thuu Vi, became a monk when he was young
noi_dung:
VII. That Patriarch of Provincial Thuong Thuong Grand Master

Excerpted from the series "Buddhist Records"

Master Tinh Thuong, from Tien Duong, surnamed Nhan, surname Thuu Vi, became a monk when he was only seven years old.

During the era of Thuan Hoa of the Song Dynasty, he lived at Nam Chieu Khanh pagoda. For the Pure Land ashram's tomb in Lo Son, he established Lien Xa and carved a statue of Amitabha Buddha. He injected himself with blood and copied the chapter "Pure Conduct" in the Avatamsaka Sutra. That's why Lien Xa was renamed Tinh Hanh Xa. At that time, 120 people attended the meeting. General Vuong Van Dan became a leader. Everyone calls themselves Tinh Hanh disciples. As for the Bhikkhu Sangha, the Great Master saved over a thousand people.
