In the 4th year of Thien Hy, on the twelfth day of the first lunar month, the Great Master was reciting Buddha's name and suddenly said loudly: "Buddha has come!". Then he quietly passed away at the age of 62.

Now that he passed away, the whole assembly saw the ground turn into a golden color, and it took a long time to return to its old color.

ADDITIONAL WORDS.- The sutra teaches: “Everything is created by the mind”. "If the mind is pure, Buddha's land is pure." The treatise says “All dharmas change only in consciousness”. Master Vinh Minh said: “If the mind is pure, then a golden dais and flowers will appear.” Great Master Tinh Hanh's mind is pure, this is "Pure Nhon". Tat attains pure Buddhaland, this is "Pure Fruition". Because the "Pure Fruit" was so strong, this impure soil was affected and temporarily turned into a golden color. The entire assembly was also infected and saw the golden soil appear.

The status of the Great Master is at the highest level.

---o0o---

tieu_de: VIII . EIGHT Patriarch Chau Hoang Grand Master
tom_tat: Master Chau Hoang, from Hangzhou, surname Tram, alias Phat Hue, alias Lien Tri. At the age of 17, he was appointed as a Dharma Teacher and was famous for being a well-educated person. Next to the house, there is an old woman who recites the Buddha's name a few thousand times every night.…
noi_dung:
VIII . EIGHT Patriarch Chau Hoang Grand Master

Excerpted from the series “Van The Phap Vi”

Master Chau Hoang, from Hangzhou, surname Tram, alias Phat Hue, alias Lien Tri. At the age of 17, he was appointed as a Dharma Teacher and was famous for being a well-educated person. Next to the house, there is an old woman who recites the Buddha's name a few thousand times every night. The master asked. She replied: "When he was born, my husband specialized in reciting the Buddha's name. On the day of his death, he was not sick, happily hugged everyone and walked away. Therefore, I know that the merit of reciting the Buddha's name is inconceivable."

Since hearing what the old woman from the neighborhood said, the Great Master focused on the Pure Land method. He wrote four big words, “Life and death are great” hanging them in front of the table to remind himself.

When he became a monk at the age of 32, he went to study with Bien Dung Zen Master and Tieu Nham Zen Master, researching the question "Who is that Buddha's name?" be awakened.

In the fifth year of Long Khanh, Ming Dynasty, the Great Master was begging for alms in Van The. Seeing the beautiful mountain scenery, he built a hut to live in. There were many fierce tigers in the mountain. Great Master practices Yogācāra Diem Khau, tigers do not cause harm to people.

That year was dry. The people of that country prayed to the Great Master to learn martial arts. He said: "I only know how to recite Buddha's name, I have no other talent." Everyone tried to appeal, but the Great Master felt the sincerity of the people, so he held the firecracker in his hand and walked along the field's edge, reciting Buddha's name. Heavy rain poured down immediately. The people rejoiced and respected the virtue, working together to build a pagoda and a palace. The monks gathered, and in no time it became a large gathering.

The great master advocated the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss and rejected crazy meditation. He authored the collection "Amitabha Sutra of Buddha's Teachings", which integrates both truth and reason, benefiting all three senses very wisely.

On the one hand, the Great Master specializes in cultivating the Pure Land and educating people. On the other hand, he often practices good deeds to help purify karma: evaluating the "Water Luc" ritual and writing "Yoga Diem Khau" to save suffering and darkness, opening ponds to release living beings, and writing precepts of killing. In the 40th year of Van Lich, at the end of June, the Great Master went into the city to say goodbye to his disciples and old people, saying: "I am going to another place." Then he returned and served tea to say goodbye to the crowd. People don't understand why.

On the afternoon of the first day of the seventh month, the Great Master entered the Sangha's house and said: "I leave tomorrow."

The next afternoon, the Great Master complained of fatigue and went into his private room to sit down and close his eyes. The monks, disciples, and old people in the city all gathered. The great master opened his eyes and said: "Everyone must recite the Buddha's name maturely, do not doubt or destroy my rules." Having finished his instructions, the Great Master clasped his hands towards the West, recited the Buddha's name, and passed away at the age of 81.

---o0o---

SUPPORT AND ANSWER

Excerpt from “Van The Phap Vi”

Mr. Cao Lu Xuyen sent letters to Van The twice to ask questions, and the Great Master responded twice. Here are some excerpts related to the Pure Land Edict:

Lu Xuyen.- The Avatamsaka Sutra belongs to the Supreme One Vehicle Complete Teaching, he put the Amitabha Sutra in the same category, but the printing seems to be incorrect. And because of this, someone wrote a treatise and guarded the Pure Land on Avatamsaka. Please, with the Pure Land facility, teach the Pure Land and with the Hoa Nghiem facility, teach Hoa Nghiem. Only then can the Buddha Dharma circulate, transmitting all five teachings to all three senses.

Great Master. - Hoa Nghiem has enough countless doors, praying for birth in the Pure Land is one of the countless doors, in the list of stars, I think that "Hoa Nghiem is extremely complete, Amitabha Sutra is less complete", that is, I said Amitabha Sutra is a relative of Hoa Nghiem, Hoa Nghiem is like a king, who dares to put the Minister of Poetry above the King? Who made that argument? He told me to take advantage of the opportunity, which is a very good idea, but it has two meanings:

A.- Thousands of organs are willing to teach, that is the work of the Tathagata in the world, I cannot do it in my strength. That's why Patriarch Cao Khe only specialized in transmitting Truc chi meditation, perhaps he didn't know other teachings. Coming to Van Mon, Cao Dong, etc., the Patriarchs all set up their own temples and separate places to teach people. The Patriarchs are still like that, let alone I am an ordinary person! If we falsely imitate Buddha, we are afraid that wanting to benefit others will end up harming others. Only Buddha is the Dharma King, with all dharmas being free. If ordinary people want to pretend to be the King, it will be difficult to avoid disaster.

B.- Preaching Avatamsaka includes the Pure Land. Teaching the Pure Land is also through Avatamsaka. Therefore, those who preach Hoa Nghiem at that time still preach Hoa Nghiem themselves, and those who preach Pure Land at that time also continue to preach Pure Land, there is still nothing against each other. Furthermore, the Avatamsaka Sutra was written by Nagarjuna Bodhisattva and he was born in the Pure Land. Manjushri and Samantabhadra are two Great Saints in the Avatamsaka Dharma Assembly, both of whom have made a vow for the Pure Land and also advised the whole Dharma assembly to pray together. You worship Hoa Nghiem but criticize the Pure Land, isn't that contrary to the vows of those three great Bodhisattvas of Hoa Nghiem? I honestly don't understand...

Lu Xuyen.- Qi Ky Zen Master said: "The person who wants to return to the West is leaving his father and running away, using the East to touch the West, wandering in a foreign land, suffering for Amitabha Buddha!". Does that word have no meaning?

Great Master.- You should respond to the Zen Master like this: "It is now like I miss my mother and return to my hometown, leaving the East for the West. How happy Amitabha Buddha is!".

Lu Xuyen.- The man of great enlightenment said: "Many lifetimes of miserable practice are not as good as one thought of attaining the Dharma of non-birth. One thought of dependent origination of no-birth is superior to the level of learning in the Three Vehicles." Moreover, regardless of the Three Vehicles or the One Vehicle, they are both selfless and selfless. Now when people are born in the Pure Land, they are the power of birth, salvation is the cause of birth, the power of existence clearly must be destroyed. If you wait for "Flowers to reveal the Buddha's enlightenment without birth" it will take a long time.

Great Master.- Have you attained the Dharma of Forbearance of No Birth? If you have realized it, you should not think that you are the source of birth, the Pure Land is the place of birth. Because the mind is saving, who can be born? And salvation is the mind, then what is the basis of birth? Being reborn but not seeing the source of birth, despite being born but still not being born, this is true non-birth. If you give up birth and say there is no birth, then it is the cessation of emptiness, not the correct principle of no birth. If you have mastered Zen Buddhism, don't you understand that: "From delusion to enlightenment, like lying in a daze and suddenly waking up, like a lotus flower blooming"? People who recite Buddha's name, there are people in this life who see Buddha's enlightenment, that is the flower that blooms in the present. Some people, after being born in Pure Land, see the Buddha's enlightenment, which is a flower that blooms later. Because the practice is both diligent and late, the foundation is beneficial and slow, so flowers bloom early and late. You shouldn't think it's too late.

Lu Xuyen.- Recently, one of your disciples came from Van The to Suzhou. I discussed the teachings of the upper vehicle, and he was shocked, surprised, and laughed in disbelief. Is it the student's fault or is it the teacher's fault? All men use their weapons to attack the heavens, taking salvation as their urgent duty. He appeared in the world and opened the way, and was the husband, but did not have the power of a great man, only the gestures of an old man and an old woman who was a vegetarian. One day, being questioned by an intelligent person, or being contradicted by an intellectual, will you then try to escape to the clouds and hide in the mountains?...

Great Master.- Before, you taught me that with the Hoa Nghiem body, the Hoa Nghiem tradition was transmitted, and with the Pure Land foundation, the Pure Land tradition was transmitted. Now why, to a monk in a certain deserted mountain, who is in the class of ignorant people who are compatible with the Pure Land sect, do you use the superior Zen technique to deceive him, making him startled and laugh at you? Is that because you made the mistake of "giving medicine that doesn't cure the disease"?

This old monk never dared to claim to be the world's most powerful person, but of course he did not have the power of a great man. He criticized Pure Land practitioners as "vegetarians". The ancients once said: that is not criticizing stupid husbands and stupid women, but rather criticizing the great Bodhisattvas: Manjushri, Pho Hien, Ma Minh, Nagarjuna, even Thien Thai, Vien Cong, Thien Dao, Vinh Minh, etc., the great Patriarchs. Are those people the vegetarian old man and the vegetarian old woman? Mr. Liu Di Dan, Bach Thieu Pho, Lieu Liu Chau, To Truong Cong, etc., those great lay people are vegetarians?

Even though he is an old man or an old woman who is a vegetarian, if he recites the Buddha's name and is reborn, he will immediately be able to live in a state of non-regression, and will immediately be able to sit on a lotus throne and join the ranks of the Saints. What should be despised! Besides, an old man and an old woman who only knows how to eat vegetarian food, recite Buddha's name, and maintain good moral conduct can be considered stupid. As for an intelligent and intellectual person who talks about Prajna, eats fish and meat to fill his stomach, then goes to the monks to talk about meditation and reason, that is a ghost. Stupid people are precious in their stupid destiny. We would rather be an old man who eats a vegetarian chanting Buddha's name or an old woman who eats a vegetarian meal and recites Buddha's name, and should not be a demonic person or a demonic woman.

So if there is a smart person or intellectual who comes to dissuade him, there is no need to go to the clouds and go to the mountains, that old man and woman can just lay his bed right at the intelligent person's throat, and spread the mat over the intellectual's eyes and that's it. Why? To protect and temporarily stop talking about Zen theory and reflect on the truth and practice it.

ADDITIONAL NOTES.- Before the Eight Patriarchs, although the Patriarchs propagated the Pure Land, on the one hand they still did not abandon Zen Buddhism. Only the Eight Patriarchs were a Zen master who was officially recognized by Tieu Nham Zen Master, the main Patriarch of the Lam Te sect, who returned to the Pure Land policy and strongly opposed crazy Zen. That's why contemporary Zen scholars are very dissatisfied with having such debates.

---o0o---

tieu_de: IX. FORMER TRI HUC GREAT MASTER
tom_tat: His father received and recited the Great Compassion Mantra and dreamed of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva giving birth to a boy.
noi_dung:
IX. FORMER TRI HUC GREAT MASTER

Excerpted from the series “Linh Phong Tong Luan”

Great Master Tri Huc, a native of Ngo Huyen, surname Chung, surname Nguoi Ich.

His father received and recited the Great Compassion Mantra and dreamed of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva giving birth to a boy.

When he was young, he studied Confucianism and wrote books about Buddhism. After reading the book "Bamboo Song Sui But" by Great Master Lien Tri, he immediately burned the book that criticized Buddha. At the age of 20, he read the Ksitigarbha Buddha Sutra, developed the intention to leave the world, and recited Buddha's name every day.

In the first year of Thien Khai, at the age of twenty-four, after listening to a Dharma Master preach the Sutra, he had doubts and then applied his mind to research. A little later, when he was enlightened, he closed his retreat in Ngo Giang. When he fell ill, he single-mindedly prayed to be born in the Pure Land. When his illness subsided, he gathered an altar and recited the rebirth mantra.

He recited a vow verse:

Bow down to Amitabha

Mantra to end karma

With Quan Am and The Chi

Bodhisattva Sangha

I love the light of the original wisdom

The hope of suffering in the cycle of reincarnation

Many lifetimes without pause

She cannot be saved

Now I have a human body

Still living a chaotic life

Dau attended Sangha again

But have not yet received the Dharma stream

Looking at the true Dharma

If you want to resist, your strength is not enough

Just because from a previous life

Not cultivating good roots

Now my mind decides

Praying for birth in the Pure Land

Then sit on the boat and pray

If you are not reborn

It is difficult to satisfy this wish

So with Saha

Decided to leave

Just like people drifting away

Before the bridge, quickly reach the shore

Then find a way

Picking people up in the middle of the stream

Now I am sincere

Introspect, dedicate your mind

Three doses of arm burn

The one-room altar is pure

Specialize in reciting the rebirth mantra

Except for eating and sleeping hours

Bring this merit and practice

Pray to be born in Ultimate Bliss

If you renounce your vow

Forget about the West

Then immediately fall into hell

To quickly repent

I swear I will not be attached to humanity or heaven

Together with non-action Nirvana

Praying to Buddha's majesty

Strength, fearlessness, no plus

The Three Jewels of Boundless Virtue

Gia has this Tri Huc

Conquering makes it impossible to retreat

Photography for growth.

Later, the Great Master widely spread the Thien Thai dharma in places: On Lang, Chuong Chau, Thach Thanh, Thanh Khe, Truong Thuy and Tan An, then returned to retire in Linh Phong.

At that time, Zen practitioners from all over the world considered the Pure Land dharma to be a teaching. Whenever they met people reciting Buddha's name, they would tell them to look up the word "Thuy (who)?". The Great Master himself believes that: Maintaining the name is the "perfect mind".

Mr. Trac Ta Xa, a Zen practitioner, commented: “What is the “single path” of the Buddhist recitation? What is the separation from the four strokes, the hundred concubines? What is the ultimate principle of the person reciting the Buddha? What is a stick in the back of the pompous and hypocritical person?

Looking forward to the Venerable putting aside Pure Land idealism and Amitabha self-nature. If you see the Tathagata's realm, say it quickly, to shake up the Great Thousand World."

The great master replied: "The highest direction first" is neither Zen nor Purity. As soon as we talk about seeking help, it is already a temporary right for people of low ability. If it is true, a great man should firmly believe that "the mind makes the Buddha, the mind makes the Buddha". If there is a way of reciting the Buddha's name, then it cannot be called "reciting the Buddha's Samadhi". If reciting does not hinder Buddha, then there is no need to ask "who?".

The Ultimate Principle of the Pure Land is: there is no Buddha other than mindfulness as the basis of mindfulness, nor is there mindfulness outside Buddha or mindfulness in Buddha. Right at the moment of launching, the whole body is pressed into the four strokes of absolute flying.

Only seeing the light of Amitabha Buddha is to see the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions. Only to be born in the Western Pure Land is to be born throughout the immeasurable Pure Lands, this is the “single highest direction” of the Buddha's name.

If you leave the current Amitabha and talk about Amitabha's self-nature, if you leave the Western Pure Land and talk about the idealistic Pure Land, that is "false pompousness".

The sutra teaches: "The Three Sages, the Ten Saints are still in retribution, only the Buddha is true in the Pure Land", this statement is "a stick in the back of the head".

Only by firmly believing in this method of reciting the Buddha's name, then relying on faith to make a wish, depending on the vow to start a virtue, when reciting, countless Tathagatas flow out, sitting throughout countless worlds in the ten directions and turning the great wheel of Dharma, illuminating the past and present, isn't that something outside of one's own responsibility, is it just shaking up the Great Thousand Worlds?

The great master once taught: “There is nothing strange about the method of reciting Buddha's name, just believe it and try your best to practice it.”

Buddha taught: “If someone recites an Amitabha Buddha, this is called “Supreme and Profound Meditation”. Patriarch Thien Thai said: “The four Samadhis chant Buddha by the same name. Samadhi of Buddha's Recitation is the king of Samadhi."

Patriarch Van The said: “One sentence of Amitabha Buddha includes all eight teachings, capturing all five sects.”

It's a pity that people today consider reciting Buddha's name to be a trivial matter and think it is the effort of foolish women. That's why your faith is not sure, you don't try hard to practice, you're lazy all day, so your pure karma doesn't succeed.

You must know that this one thought that is present is inherently free from four phrases and hundreds of steps, without the need for any intention to separate it. Right now, a Buddha's sentence is inherently transcendent, so there's no need to talk about magic or mystery. The only important thing is to believe firmly, hold firmly, and then recite. Or 100,000 sentences day and night, 70,000 sentences, or 50,000, 30,000 sentences, you must decide not to miss, vowing to never change for the rest of your life. That's right, not being reborn in the Pure Land of the three times the Buddhas are lying is false. After being reborn, one can abide without retreat, and all dharmas will appear one after another.

It's very taboo to do this or that. When you meet a person who studies morality, you want to study literature, when you meet a Zen practitioner, you want to be greedy and seek salvation. When you meet a person who upholds the law, you beg for alms and alms bowls... If that's the case, then nothing will happen, your mind will be busy with all kinds of things.

Unexpectedly: when reciting Amitabha Buddha to become mature, the Tripitaka teachings are included in it; One thousand seven hundred koans of the ascending organ are also in there; Three thousand majestic postures, eighty thousand virtuous actions, three collections of pure precepts do not go beyond the Buddha's words.

A true person recites the Buddha's name: internally he forgets the body, externally he forgets the environment, that is "great almsgiving"; Not giving rise to greed, anger, and ignorance is "great practice of precepts"; Not accepting neither human nor self is "great patience"; Reciting the Buddha's name without interruption is "great diligence"; The arising of false thoughts without foundation is "great meditation"; Not being confused by other things and other dharmas is "great wisdom".

Try examining yourself, if you have not forgotten the body and mind of the world, are still greedy, angry, ignorant, still have thoughts and non-self, are still interrupted, still have false thoughts, are still being dragged by other things, then you are not "truly reciting Buddha's name".

There is no special way to reach the state of one mind and no chaos. When you first practice reciting, you must use a string to write down the numbers clearly to make sure there are no shortages of decisive times.

From time to time, when you become proficient, without reciting but still reciting yourself, then whether you write down the number or not write down the number, it's okay. If at first you want to be completely free and formless, then the power of mindfulness will be difficult to achieve; This is because the belief is not certain so the practice does not try.

Anyone who is free to preach all twelve parts of the teachings, the Tripitaka, and understand thousands of koans is just a matter of being on the brink of life and death. At the moment of death, I decided I couldn't use it anymore.

In the 11th year of Shun Tri, Qing Dynasty, in the winter, the Great Master fell ill. He instructed his disciples: after the cremation, ground the bones and mixed with powder and give alms to the pomfret to make Pure Land karma with them.

Next year, on January 21, the Great Master woke up early in the morning, healthy and fresh as if he was not sick. At noon, the Great Master sat cross-legged on the bed, faced the West, clasped his hands and passed away, at the age of 57.

Three years after the Great Master passed away, the disciples gathered again to decide on the cremation method. When he opened the lid, he saw that the Great Master's entire body was still intact, his hair was long and covered the edges of his ears, and his face seemed alive.

The crowd could not bear to obey the Great Master's instructions, so they built a worship tower in Linh Phong.

Below is a modern monk who fell into harm's way as taught by the Patriarchs, quoted in “An Quang Van Sao”

---o0o---

MASTER NGO KHAI

Master Ngo Khai, a Dharma friend of Master An Quang, was originally a wise man, but his nature was high and ambitious. Initially, the Master studied Zen Buddhism and despised the Pure Land. A little while later, thanks to Dharma Master Thong Tri's guidance, he once again set his mind on the Pure Land. Even though the Master had faith in the Pure Land Dharma, but did not practice it diligently, his high thoughts did not lessen, Great Master An Quang once advised: you should humble yourself and practice diligently. But still could not restore the Master's fixed mind.

After a period of lecturing here and there, the Master fell ill and returned to Putuo. As soon as he returned to the mountain, he and his brother, Master Nguyen Thong, chatted and visited. Before the conversation ended, the Master was too tired to say a word. After noon the next day, the Master passed away. There is no good omen at all, nor is there a single good point that is enough to prove rebirth or liberation.

Oh! The sentence: "It is difficult for a thousand people to have one liberation", the words of the Second Patriarch and the sentence: "It is just a matter of birth and death, it cannot be used completely at the time of death", the words of the Nine Patriarchs, are they hammer blows for miscellaneous people, are they thunder in the ears of wise men!

Great Master Mac Am, a great Zen master and also a great Lecturer of the Qing Dynasty, at his deathbed asked the crowd: “What is liberation?”. No one could answer, the Great Master smiled and said: "There is nothing better than imitating the old man and the old woman who eats vegetarian and chants the Buddha's name."

---o0o---

tom_tat: Since childhood, the Great Master has not eaten meat. After becoming a monk, he researched the question: "Who is that Buddha recitation?" awakened, he said: “I have awakened
noi_dung:
X. THẬP TỔ THIỆT HIỀN ĐẠI SƯ

Excerpts from the series: “Tu Qi Great Master Di Cao”

“Seng Patriarch Wind Technique”

Great Master Thiet Hien, from Thuong Thuc, Qing Dynasty, Tu Te, title of Am Province.

Since childhood, the Great Master has not eaten meat. After ordaining, he researched the question: “Who is that Buddha recitation?” awakened, he said: "I have awakened from the dream!".

He closed his retreat for three years at Chon Tich Pagoda, reading Sutras during the day and reciting Buddha's name at night.

Later, the Great Master went to Mau Son to worship the Buddha's relics. On the anniversary of the Buddha's Nirvana, the Great Master gathered together the Sangha to prepare offerings and then, before the Buddha, he burned his fingers and made 48 great vows. When the Great Master made his vow, he felt the relic release light.

The Great Master composed the text "Developing the Bodhi Mind" to encourage the four groups. Many people recite this verse and shed tears.

Van says:

In the Sutras it is taught: "The main thing to do is to enter the path, develop the mind first. The main thing to practice is to make vows first."

When you develop your mind, the Buddha way can be achieved. When you make a wish, living beings can be saved. If you do not develop a broad mind and do not make solid vows, then even if you go through countless lives, you will still remain in the cycle of reincarnation. Even if you practice, you will still be miserable.

The Avatamsaka Sutra says: “Forgetting the Bodhi mind and cultivating good dharmas is called demonic karma.”

Forgetting is still demon karma, let alone having never committed it! Therefore, we know that: Everyone who wants to study Buddhism must develop Bodhi mind and must not delay.

But the wish has many different natures, now I summarize eight ways for the teachings of the community: “Evil, right, true, false, big, small, heavenly, perfect.”

1.- In life, there are people who practice and do not seek self-study, only care about external things, or seek wealth or fame, or are greedy for happiness in this life, or look forward to future retribution. Developing such a mind is called “evil”.

2.- As for those who practice but do not seek fame and profit, are not greedy for happiness, do not look for retribution, just to escape birth and death, only to achieve Bodhi, this is called "righteousness".

3.- Reciting and praying for the Buddha way, the heart and mind are to help sentient beings. Seeing the Buddha's path is long and long but not afraid, seeing sentient beings is difficult to save but the will is not weakened, like climbing a mountain determined to reach the top, like climbing a tower determined to reach the bottom. Developing the mind like this is called “truth”.

4.- There are sins that do not repent, there are faults that are not willing to admit it, on the outside it seems pure but on the inside the mind is dirty, first diligently and then lazy, even though there is a good mind, but mixing fame and profit, even though there is good dharma but contaminated by sin, that is called "false" (lies).

5.- When the world of sentient beings ends, my wish will end. The Bodhi path will be achieved and my wish will come true. Developing such a mind is called “great”.

6.- Viewing the three realms as a prison, viewing birth and death as an injustice, only wishing for your own quick liberation without wanting to save others, this is called “smallness”.

7.- If you have the notion that sentient beings and the Buddha path are outside your own mind, then make a wish to save your life, do not forget your merits, and do not stop your knowledge. Developing a mind like that is called “heaven” (deviation).

8.- Knowing that one's self-nature is a sentient being, one should vow to save it; knowing one's self-nature is the Buddha path, one should vow to achieve it. Not seeing any dharma outside the self-mind, then using an empty mind to make an empty vow, practicing empty conduct to realize the empty fruit, also no longer seeing the empty appearance, this is called "perfection".

The eight ways to develop the mind are clear, so we should carefully examine ourselves to see what kind of character we have to develop the mind: is it evil or false? Is truth truth? Is big or small? Is heaven a pill?

If you realize that it is evil, false, small, or heavenly, immediately correct it. If you consider yourself to be true, true, great, and perfect, then your strength will increase. To do so is to "genuinely develop the Bodhi mind".

This Bodhi mind is the king of all good dharmas, it arises thanks to ten causes and conditions.

1.- Because of thinking of the Buddha's grace.- My Original Master Shakyamuni Buddha, from the earliest moment of awakening his mind, practiced the Bodhisattva path for us, for countless eons he endured all kinds of suffering. As the Lotus Sutra says: "In all the Great Thousand Realms, there is no place the size of a mustard seed that is not the place where the Buddha sacrificed his life for sentient beings."

When we create karma, Buddha mercifully teaches us, but only because we are too stupid to listen. Then I fell into an evil state, and the Buddha felt even more pity and wanted to suffer for me, but my karma was too heavy and I could not be saved.

When I was born as a human, Buddha sought to help me plant good roots. In life after life, Buddha's heart followed me and never left my side.

When the Buddha appeared in this world, I was still in the world, but now I want to become a Buddha who has passed away.

What crime is it to be born in the Dharma Ending Age! What a blessing it is to attend the Sangha! What is the obstacle that cannot see the golden body? How lucky was it to meet the statue!

Then think to yourself like this: If in my previous life I had not planted good roots, how could I have heard the Buddha's Dharma now? I would never have known that I would always be grateful to the Buddha. Thanks to that virtue, mountains are incomparably high. If we do not develop the mind to practice the Bodhisattva path, uphold the Buddha Dharma, and save sentient beings, then even if our bones and flesh are broken, we will not be able to make up for it.

2.- Because I am grateful to my parents.- Alas, my parents gave birth to me with difficulty! Ten months of carrying heavy weight, three years of breastfeeding, we become human. I thought I was continuing the family line, inheriting my ancestors' inheritance. No wonder I became a monk and took the name Thich Tu. Don't offer food or water, don't support your limbs.

If my parents are still there, I don't take care of my human body. When my parents died, I did not guide my consciousness. Thus, for life it is a great loss, but for religion, it is not beneficial. Is that a serious crime!

Then think to yourself like this: From now on, for hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, I must practice the Buddha way. In the ten directions and three worlds, I always save all sentient beings. In this world, not only our own parents in this present life, but also our parents and everyone else's parents will be promoted to the next level. Only then can we repay the kindness of birth and upbringing.

3.- Out of gratitude to the Master.- Without the worldly Master, I would not know how to be polite. If I had not been born as a Master, I would not have understood Buddhism. Not knowing how to be polite is no different from being an animal. I don't understand how Buddhism differs from secular people. Now I know a little bit of etiquette, understand a bit of the Buddha Dharma, how to wear clothes, and how to be precepts and improve my body. This is all thanks to the Master.

Then think to yourself: Now I practice Mahayana, vowing to bring great benefits to all, following the Master's will, but also increasing the Master's merit. That's what we call gratitude to the Master.

4.- Out of gratitude to the donors.- Everyday items are not mine: two meals of rice porridge, clothes for four seasons, medicine when sick, beds and chairs when tired... are all bought for me.

People who work hard at plowing and harrowing still find it difficult to have enough to eat, but when we sit and enjoy food, we are still not satisfied! People in the textile and garment era constantly had to wear and tear, while we had extra clothes but didn't know how to take care of them! People back then had houses with thatched walls and wattle walls and were busy all their lives. In our time, people had wide temples with high roofs and leisurely all year round. Using other people's hardships to provide comfort for us, can we have peace in our hearts? Is it reasonable to use other people's wealth to support yourself?

Then think to yourself: If we don't worry about the two paths of compassion and wisdom, including cultivating blessings and wisdom, so that faith can be relied upon, sentient beings can be saved, the inch of cloth and grain of rice will one day have to be returned, and the hungry ghost hell will have to fall. We must solidify our Bodhi mind.

5.- Because of gratitude to sentient beings. - From beginningless time to the present, I and sentient beings have been related to each other, here and there we all have gratitude towards each other. Even though this life has changed and I'm in a coma, I don't remember, but if we consider the time, we can't help but repay it.

Now that furry animal wearing horns, who knows, I was once its child. Who knows, those worms, crickets, butterflies, and bees are our previous incarnations. To those who groan in hell and cry out among hungry ghosts. Even though we don't see or hear them, they still ask for help. Outside of the Sutras, there is no one else who can clearly explain this matter. Besides Buddha, no one can clearly explain it. Therefore, Bodhisattvas consider ants and lice to be their past parents, and animals and birds to be future Buddhas, so they often worry about salvation and always think of repaying gratitude.

6.- Because of thinking about the suffering of birth and death.- I and everyone else from many lifetimes until now have always been in the sea of ​​birth and death: sometimes as a heaven, sometimes as a human, or in this world or another world, dying here and being born there, sometimes up and down. Hungry ghosts leave early in the morning and return in the afternoon, hell comes out tomorrow. The blade of the mountain sword breaks its body; The boiling copper and iron burn the heart and soul; cry in fire, groan in ice. Countless lives and deaths within days and nights, moments of suffering equal to centuries. At that time, even though I knew I was suffering, I couldn't repent in time. After escaping, I immediately forgot and committed the same sin as usual. The mind is not constant, like a traveler wandering around, the body is not stable, like the door of the house changes. The dust and sand cannot count the number of bodies that have lived, and the sea water is still not as numerous as the tears of separation. Without Buddha's words, no one would see or hear this. If you don't read the Sutras, you won't know that reason. If in this life we ​​continue to be as greedy as before, still as ignorant as before, I am afraid that I will be forever lost in the past for thousands of lifetimes. The human body is difficult to obtain but easy to die. Good times are easy to pass but difficult to return. Unfortunately, later on, one must fall into evil paths and bring suffering, then who will be able to do that? Therefore, we must put an end to the desire for life and death, destroy the sea of ​​lust, save ourselves and others to reach enlightenment, relationships in this life cannot be neglected.

7.- Because of respect for the spiritual nature.- My nature and that of Shakyamuni Tathagata are no different. Why has the Master become a clear-minded and free Buddha, but we are still ordinary people who are in a coma and crazy? The Original Master has immeasurable magical powers and wisdom, immeasurable merits and solemn liberation, but I only have immeasurable karma of ignorance, immeasurable afflictions, impurities, and sufferings of birth and death!

The mind and nature are the same, but because of ignorance and enlightenment, they are as different as heaven and abyss. For example, priceless treasures buried in the mud are considered rocks. Now we must use countless good dharmas to treat afflictions. Only by cultivating virtue will our virtuous nature appear. Like a precious pearl that is washed and dried so that it immediately radiates light and shines on the high platform. Only then will the Buddha's teachings not be in vain and will not disappoint one's spiritual nature.

8.- Because of repenting of bad karma.- The sutra says: "If you commit a sin of kila, you will fall into hell with the lifespan of the Four Heavenly Kings."

Even small crimes are punished like that, let alone serious crimes?

Nowadays, every day, every move and action often violates the precepts. When I eat and drink, I always violate thi-la. Counting it carefully in one day is enough to commit many sins, let alone in a lifetime, even many lives in the past. Just looking at the Five Precepts is not necessarily complete, let alone the Ten Precepts, the Complete Precepts, the Bodhisattva's immeasurable precepts!

Now we must wholeheartedly pray for someone to repent, love ourselves and others, be passionate in our body and speech, and let our tears flow according to our words, hoping that our sins will be eliminated and suffering will be freed.

9.- For the sake of rebirth in the Pure Land.- In this evil and depraved realm, it is very difficult to practice. Being reborn in the Pure Land and becoming a Buddha is very easy. Because it is difficult, many lifetimes have not been achieved. Because it is easy, one lifetime has attained the fruition. For that reason, since ancient times, all the Saints and Sages have been inclined toward Ultimate Bliss, and all the Sutras and Treatises have all pointed to the Pure Land. In this life of practice, there is no method better than this method.

In the Amitabha Sutra, it is said: "With few good roots and few blessings, one cannot be reborn." Thus, many good roots and merits are born. Many blessings are nothing more than holding on to names, many good roots are nothing more than developing Bodhi mind. Reciting the Buddha's name for a moment is better than giving alms for a whole year; developing Bodhi mind is better than practicing for many lifetimes.

Besides, reciting Buddha's name is to hope to become a Buddha. If you don't develop the Bodhi mind, what is the point of reciting it? Still developing Bodhi mind to practice, but not being born in the Pure Land, it is easy to regress and lose. So in the Sutra there is an example:

"Bodhisattva's initial awakening of mind, with fish eggs and yem la flowers, is many causes but few fruits."

Sow the Bodhi seed, cultivate it with Buddha's name, then the path and fruit will naturally grow, then rely on the Buddha's great vow and surely be reborn in the Pure Land. To have reached the Pure Land means to abide and not retreat; From here, two-fold blessings and miraculous fortunes grow and reach perfection. Therefore, we must single-mindedly pray to be born in the Pure Land.

10.- For the sake of protecting the Dharma.- For my sake and for all, the Master has practiced the Bodhisattva path for countless eons, doing things that are difficult to do, and enduring things that are difficult to endure. After achieving Buddhahood, he devoted his life to guiding everyone and thoroughly teaching all kinds of things. When the opportunity for teaching was completed, the Buddha entered Nirvana!

The true Dharma has passed, the image of the Dharma has ended, now there is only the end of the Dharma: there is the Dharma but no one can attain the Dharma. Evil and right are not divided, right and wrong are mixed. Competing together for personal gain, not for profit, while seeking fame, the Three Jewels no longer have true meaning, decline and become so bad that they cannot bear to say anything. Thinking about this, it's hard to hold back the tears.

If we are Buddhists but cannot repay the Buddha's grace, we will not benefit ourselves at all times, and outside we will be of no use to others. Living has no benefit for the present, dying is still useless in the future. Thinking like that made me heartbroken and hastily raised my mind, together with my companions, I went to the ashram to recite repentance and form a dharma assembly. Make 48 vows, vow to save sentient beings, and vow to become Buddha. In this retribution body, I vow to return to the Pure Land, to reach the nine levels, to participate in the Holy Stream, to attain the attainment of No Birth, to be able to abide without retreat.

Then take the boat and make a vow to return to Saha, making Buddha's day shine brightly and the wheel of Dharma constantly turning...

The eight ways and ten conditions are known enough. When the mind develops the tendency, there is a path and a way. I hope that the public will be sensitive to my sincerity and earnestness, and join me in making a great vow and developing a great heart. If it hasn't developed yet, now develop it, if it has developed then now it will grow, if it has grown then continue it. Don't find it difficult to be afraid, don't find it easy to look down on it. Don't rush but don't endure, don't relax but don't get it. Don't let your ignorance stop you from developing your mind, and don't be cowardly and abandon yourself because your wisdom is shallow and thick. For example, if you plant a tree, if you plant it for a long time, the roots become shallower and deeper. It's like sharpening a knife, when you sharpen it, the blade gradually becomes sharper. It's probably because the roots are shallow that they leave them dry and don't plant them, so floods leave them like that, making them useless!

But if you let your practice be so hard, you won't know that laziness is even more miserable. Because of practice, even though you have to work hard in the present, you will have eternal peace and happiness in the future. Laziness and laziness steal comfort for a lifetime, but then many lifetimes of suffering.

What's more, if you use the Pure Land as a pearl, then there's no need to worry about regression. If you use the Unborn as a ring power, there's no fear of hardship.

Don't say that your thoughts are impermanent and don't arise, and don't say that your wishes are useless and don't make them.

We must know that when the mind is true, then the fruit is real, and when the vow is great, the virtue is deep. That emptiness is not as vast as the mind, and that diamond is not as durable as the power of vows.

If the masses do not reject my words, from now on we will be relatives of Bodhi and good friends in the Pure Land. May we together be reborn in the Pure Land and serve Amitabha together, helping all sentient beings to attain perfect enlightenment.

A little while later, the Great Master lived at Tien Lam Pagoda in Hangzhou.

In the 7th year of Ung Chinh, the Great Master established Lien Xa as an oath to keep the community, taking his entire life as an appointment. Divide day and night into 20 parts: 10 parts reciting names, 9 parts visualizing, 1 part repentance.

A Zen monk came to ask about the practice of reciting Buddha's name.

The great master explained: "A single sentence of Amitabha Buddha is the beginning of a koan, without any other discussion, the winner will immediately decide. Like a big fire, if you jump into it, it will immediately burn. Like a Thai A sword, when you get down, it will break. Eighty-four thousand dharmas, no more than six words. One thousand seven hundred koans, one sentence is enough to guess. No matter who doesn't like to listen to the Buddha, I recite the Buddha's name to myself. Please don't say too many words, just be single-minded and not confused."

The 11th year of Ung Chinh, the 8th day of the December month. The great master told the assembly: “I will leave in April next year.” Then the Great Master closed the door and recited Buddha's name ten thousand times a day.

Next year, on April 12, the Great Master told his disciples: "From the beginning of this month until now, I have seen the Three Saints of Ultimate Bliss twice. I will be reborn!". Then the Great Master wrote a poem to say goodbye to them.

The next day, the Great Master did not eat or drink, just closed his eyes and sat upright. At the fifth watch, the Great Master bathed and changed his clothes. The next day, the 14th, near noon, the Great Master turned his face to the West and closed his eyes in silence. Masses of monks and laypeople from all over gathered like a market. The Great Master suddenly opened his eyes, looked at everyone and said: "I will return soon to the Pure Land. Escaping life and death is a big thing, everyone should keep their hearts pure and diligently recite Buddha's name."

Having finished his instructions, the Great Master clasped his hands and loudly chanted the Buddha's name and passed away. Life expectancy is forty-nine years old.

---o0o---

tieu_de: XI. THE TENTH ANCESTOR OF THE PROVINCIAL MASTER
tom_tat: Master Ji Tinh, from Phong Nhuan, Qing Dynasty, surname Ma, surname Triet Ngo, alias Nap
noi_dung:
XI. THE TENTH ANCESTOR OF THE PROVINCIAL MASTER

Excerpted from the series "Enlightenment of Zen Master Yu Luc"

Master Ji Tinh, from Phong Nhuan, Qing Dynasty, surname Ma, surname Triet Ngu, alias Na Duong.

In his childhood, he studied history and scriptures. After becoming a monk, he went to study in many places, learning extensively about both the "Nature" and "General" sects, and the one he liked the most was "The Three Contemplations of Dharma Flowers". Next, he studied with Zen master Tuy Nhu Thuan at Quang Thong pagoda and discovered the essence of his mind. Later, Master Thuan Zen stayed at Van Tho pagoda, and the Great Master succeeded him in Quang Thong, teaching and promoting his followers. The tone is very clear.

The great master said: "Zen Master Vinh Minh Tho is a dragon statue of Zen, but he still surrenders to the Pure Land, let alone in the time of the end of the Dharma, even more so!".

The great master specializes in Pure Land cultivation and advocates Lien Tong. Every day, teach them to welcome guests with a stick of incense. In addition, we are determined to only pay homage to Buddha and recite Buddha's name.

Not long after, the Great Master went to live at Giac Sanh Pagoda, and soon returned to live at Tu Phuoc Pagoda in Hong Loa Son. The monks from all over loved the Great Master, so they gathered more and more in Tu Phuoc every day, and became a monk.

The Great Master, for the sake of Dharma and people, was not tired at all, and everyone used the Pure Land as their refuge. Whenever I preach about the Tathagata's grace to save suffering and bring joy, tears often follow his words. The audience was moved, most of them had tears, snot, and noses that wet their shirts.

The great master once taught: "At the beginning of our relationship in the cycle of birth and death, there are two abilities: A.- "The mind is full of dignity and strength in the land of heaven and earth", this is the power of the mind. B.- "Like a human being, the fruit is strong and the shield is strong(1)", this is the force of karma.

Karma is great, but mind power is greater. Because karma has no self-nature and depends entirely on the mind, focusing on the mind makes karma strong.

If you use a focused mind to cultivate pure karma, then the pure karma will be strong. The next day, you will receive your final death, and will be determined to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, not to be born in any other realm. Like a big tree with high walls slanting towards the West, when it lifts its roots and loosens its legs, it decides to fall face down towards the West.

What is a focused mind?

We cultivate pure karma: our faith must be deep and firm, our aspirations must be earnest. Due to deep faith and strong aspirations, all false teachings cannot be shaken, all conditions cannot be attracted.

Suppose that while we are cultivating pure karma, Patriarch Bodhidharma appears and tells us that if we give up pure karma and practice Zen, we can immediately become a Buddha, then we would also thank the Patriarch but would not dare to obey. Even though Shakyamuni Tathagata suddenly appeared and told me that there was a method other than the Pure Land, and then told me to leave the Pure Land to practice that method, I still bowed to the Buddha and said yes. Being steadfast like that is called deep faith.

Even if the red ring of fire were to fall on my head, I would not forget my wish to be reborn because of this suffering. Even if the greatest wealth and joy in life, such as the throne of Luan, comes to us, we will not forget our wish to be reborn because of that happiness. Encountering such extremely adverse circumstances and still not changing your heart, this is called a fervent wish.

Firm belief, strong aspiration, that is the focused mind. Use this mind to cultivate pure karma, then pure karma will be strong, strong karma will quickly mature. When the pure karma of Ultimate Bliss is mature, the Saha fate will cease. Thus, at the time of death, even if you want the realm of reincarnation to appear, it is impossible, even if you want to leave Amitabha and the Pure Land realm and not appear, it is also impossible.

But that firm belief and earnest aspiration must be trained in times of trouble, so that at the time of death, one will not stray into another path. Like the Ancient One at his deathbed, the gods played music and phan to procession at the Tusita Heavenly King throne that they had tried to renounce, focusing on reciting the Buddha's name until the Buddha and the Saints arrived before they followed. And when you are about to die, the four great elements divide, and the gods come to pick you up, which is the ultimate scene. If in normal times your faith and aspirations are not completely firm, when you encounter that scene at the time of death, it will be difficult to control yourself.

There is a Zen practitioner who comes to clarify: "All dharmas are illusory dreams, Saha is inherently an illusory dream, Ultimate Bliss is also an illusory dream. Simultaneity is an illusory dream, what is the use of practicing?".

The Great Master said: "It's not like that! From the Seven Bodhisattva Levels down, they all practice in illusory dreams. Up to the level of Enlightenment, they are still sleeping because of ignorance. Only the Buddha is Great Enlightenment.

While in a dream, suffering and joy are clear. The dream of suffering in Saha is not as good as the dream of peace and happiness in the Pure Land. Moreover, the Saha dream scene is from dream to dream, going deeper and deeper into a place of ecstasy. The dream scene of Ultimate Bliss is to emerge from the dream and become a Great Enlightenment. Although the impure world and the pure world are the same illusory scene, the effects and results are very different, so it is necessary to practice the Pure Land as soon as possible.

The 15th year of Gia Khanh, February. The Great Master knew in advance the day of rebirth, so he went to say goodbye to different places and advised: "This illusory body will not last long. Everyone should make an effort to recite the Buddha's name. We will meet each other in the Pure Land."

In December, on the 2nd day, at first glance, I saw countless phan buu fields coming from the West. The great master told the crowd: “The Pure Land has appeared, I am about to return to the Pure Land!”. Then the Great Master told the crowd to take turns reciting Buddha's name. On the 17th day, Monkey hour, the Great Master told the crowd: "Yesterday I saw Manjushri, Guan Yin and The Three Bodhisattvas, and now the Buddha himself has come to receive me. I'm going!" Having finished speaking, the Great Master turned to face the West and said: "If you say a good name, you will see a good appearance!". Having finished speaking, the Great Master crossed the seal and passed away. Life was 70 years old, Sangha was 49 years old. At the moment the Great Master passed away, the whole assembly smelled a strange, sweet scent. Left exposed for 7 days, the Grand Master's body looked as fresh as life, and his white hair turned black. At the time of cremation, he received more than a hundred relics.

ADDITIONAL NOTES.- Among the Mahayana sects, Zen Buddhism calls itself "Directly pointing to the true mind, realizing one's nature and becoming a Buddha" and also calls itself "a special external teaching". Of the 11 Patriarchs of the Pure Land Sect, all 6 are former original Zen masters: Third Patriarch Vien Vien Zen Master, Sixth Patriarch Vinh Minh Tho Zen Master, Eight Patriarchs Buddha Hue Zen Master, Nine Patriarchs Random Ich Zen Master, Ten Patriarchs of Province Am Zen Master, and Ten Patriarchs Triet Ngu Zen Master. They went from Zen to Pure Land practice and propagated the Pure Land dharma. Why did they not propagate meditation but return to propagate purity? There are two reasons:

1.- Direct Samatha meditation is only beneficial for the Upper level and the upper level, but the Middle and Lower levels find it difficult to achieve complete enlightenment. It is not as good as the Dharma method of reciting the Buddha's name that benefits all the three spiritual capacities (superior, medium, inferior): the person with the highest ability can realize the supreme, one-pointed mind, and the person with the lowest level of ability who specializes in reciting the Buddha's name can also be reborn in karma. Once reborn, he immediately attended the Holy Assembly, immediately saw Amitabha, immediately approached the Bodhisattva, why worry about not achieving great enlightenment? Because of such narrow (meditation) and broad (purity) benefits, they strongly teach and advise fellow Pure Land practitioners, so that everyone can benefit reliably.

2.- Having clear mind and seeing one's nature must be a person with great wisdom. Even though you have been thoroughly enlightened, the ignorance, afflictions and karma that have been accumulated for countless lifetimes up to now cannot be cleansed in one go. If one's karma is still intact, it is still stuck in the cycle of birth and death, and one day it is difficult to guarantee that one will not be confused. If you are fully enlightened and are reborn, you will be on the right path to becoming a Buddha. Because they wanted to ensure enlightenment, they realized meditation, which included cultivating purity and praying to be born in Ultimate Bliss.

Not only the Zen masters above, there are many other Zen masters, and many Patriarchs in other sects: Hoa Nghiem, Phap Hoa, Duy Thuc, etc. who dedicate themselves to the Pure Land and lead people to the Pure Land, but we will see their brief history in the next volume.

Oh! The Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss is like the ocean: thousands of rivers and creeks all flow together, the Saints above and the mortals are inclined towards it.

We, those who have the will to "improve ourselves and others", must soon use "deep faith", "strong vows", "specially upholding the Buddha's name" to be reborn, to participate in the Holy Seed, to abide without retreat, to achieve Bodhi, to save sentient beings, and to attain Buddhahood.

May I bring this merit

Solemn pure Buddha land

Together with the Dharma world of sentient beings

Born together in the Pure Land

DEAR THANH
