noi_dung:
A 2 - MONKS

I - HUE TRIEN

Master Hui Trien, surnamed Dong, became a monk in Tuong Chau when he was young. During the time of Zhou Wu De's destruction of Buddhism, he fled to Mao Mountain and then to The Ha, going to An Chau to listen to the teachings of the Sutras. Whenever he heard any Sutra, he immediately realized its profound meaning. At an old age, he returned to Tuong Chau to live at Quang Phuoc pagoda. The pagoda is at the top of the mountain, so we have to go down the slope to carry water. The Sangha is large and the water is not enough. He is about to move to another place. At night, there was a God, taller than a staff, wearing a purple robe, who came to pay homage to him and said: "The Dharma Master is requested to stay here to regularly preach the Mahayana Dharma. Please do not pay attention to the Hinayana Dharma. The Hinayana Dharma is like a high mountain without water and cannot benefit people. The Mahayana Sutra is like the ocean, if there is one person who preaches it, he can make that place precious and dignified, the Dharma community flourishes, and the goods are abundant. If you desire the Hinayana Sutra, then those benefits will all be there." I hope that you will stay and promote Mahayana and not disappoint the expectations of this little god. The magician needs water, I will personally go to Tu Mau stream in Kiem Nam to ask for water from the Dragon King. The white god finished speaking and suddenly disappeared.

On the night of the 7th of the following month, a strong wind blew from the southwest, thunder and rain poured down all night, and by morning the sky stopped. The crowd went out to look around and saw that the low land north of the pagoda had a cool and sweet stream. The whole temple was happy.

The magician has a gentle personality, always smiles happily, and teaches diligently. After staying in the mountains for a while, the monks all respected him.

In the 23rd year of Trinh Quan, on the night of April 8, the Mountain God appeared again and said: "Soon the Dharma Master will be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss."

On July 14, after the assembly finished preaching the Vu Lan Sutra, the Dharma Master clasped his hands and said: "The longevity of the donation must now be divided equally. All of my possessions, please donate to the Sangha of the ten directions and the poor and disabled, even to the animals." Having finished speaking, the Dharma Master sat still and passed away on the Dharma chair.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

II - DAO TRAN

Dharma Master Dao Tran, at the beginning of the Liang Dynasty, meditated on Amitabha Buddha on Lo Son Mountain, but about rebirth, he was still hesitant in his mind. One night, the Dharma Master dreamed of someone sitting in a large treasure boat going through the sea, saying he was going through Amitabha Buddha's country. The Dharma Master asked to follow. The person sitting in the boat said: "You haven't built a bathhouse to worship the Sangha, haven't recited the Amitabha Sutra, your pure karma hasn't been achieved yet, you can't go yet!". After waking up, the Dharma Master built a hot bath to offer to the Sangha and recited the Amitabha Sutra for many years diligently practicing without delay.

Later, while sitting in the contemplation room, the Dharma Master saw someone carrying a silver lotus and said: "After death, the Dharma Master will sit on this silver throne. The Dharma Master's deeds should have earned him a golden throne. But because in the beginning, his mind was hesitant, he only got this level!". The magician was very happy, so he copied the above matter on paper and put it in the sutra box.

The night the Dharma Master was reborn, from half of Mount Lo Son to the top, it was as bright as several thousand red-burning torches lined up. People in the villages near the mountains thought they were kings holding a congress. When we inquired in the morning, we learned that Dharma Master Dao Tran had passed away.

The monks reviewed the belongings in the Dharma Master's private room. When they opened the sutra box, they saw a page recording the sighting of a silver pedestal and realized that the Dharma Master had passed away.

Excerpted from the series: The Story of Cao Tang

Lac Ban Van Loai

---o0o---

III - DAO NGAN

Master Dao Ngan, from Wei County, became a monk under Linh Du Dharma Master, learned the Buddhist teachings, and preached without hindrance.

One time, the Great Master preached the Avatamsaka Sutra and the Ten Grounds at Hang Lang Son pagoda. It was a dark night without lights. The Great Master raised his hand and pointed, and immediately emitted a golden light, illuminating the entire lecture hall. The audience was surprised. The great master said: "That light is always in your hand, what's so strange about it?". In his life of preaching, the Great Master always only returned to the Pure Land, vowing to be born in the Pure Land.

Later, while at Bao Ung pagoda, the Great Master knew the date and time in advance, and told the monks and laymen to come together on the 1st of the eighth month to say goodbye. When the time comes, the masses gather together. The master asked if it was almost time for dinner? Then the Great Master sat down, and a strange fragrance suddenly emitted from the incense burner on the bench. The great master preached the Bodhisattva precepts, the words were very essential, the listeners' minds were pure.

Having just finished preaching the precepts, the Great Master raised his face and looked up, seeing the Heavenly beings milling about and heavenly music rising. The great master told the crowd: "The gods of Tusita heaven came to welcome me. But heaven is the basis of birth and death, not the place of my desire. All my life I have only prayed for the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, why have I not been able to achieve such a wish?"

The master finished speaking, the music became softer and then stopped. Immediately I saw from the West, the scent of flowers, techniques, music, phan phan, and treasures, filling the sky like big clouds, flying in, then spinning and stopping right at the Great Master's head. They all saw it and exclaimed that it was strange and rare. The great master said loudly: "Everyone who stays here should try to practice diligently. Now the Holy Sangha of Ultimate Bliss has come to pick you up. I will go!". Having finished speaking, the Great Master still sat upright on the throne and passed away, at the age of 69. That year was the 7th year of Trinh Quan.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

IV - HUE QUANG

Master Hue Quang, in Luoyang. He narrated commentaries such as the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Ten Grounds, Nirvana, etc., which discussed the "real power of shaming" very clearly.

One day, when he was sick and saw the gods coming to pick him up, the Dharma Master said: "In my life, I only wish to be reborn in the Pure Land!". In a moment, Buddhas crowded the entire space. The shaman bowed and said: "I hope that His Holiness the Father will take care of you and grant you your wish." Then the Dharma Master picked his fingernails and passed away.

Excerpted from the series Buddhist Records

ADDITIONAL WORDS.- The moment of death is when the four great elements disperse. The Devas coming to receive them is a scene of great joy, but still try to be kind and determined to be reborn. The steadfast vows of Great Master Dao Ngan and Dharma Master Hue Quang are worthy of being an example for all generations.

---o0o---

V - MISCELLANEOUS

Zen Master Phi Tich, when he first became a monk, specialized in studying the Law of Rituals. Later, he and Master So Kim Phap researched and practiced the Thien Thai teachings.

In the year of Thien Buu, he went to the Buddhist monks, lived in Zhong Nam Son, and composed the set of "Reciting the Buddha's Precious Vuong Luan", three volumes, handed down in the present life. In that collection, regarding the passage that teaches focusing on reciting the Buddha's name, the summary is as follows: The Compassion Flower Sutra says: "From the moment Prince Mat Su developed the Bodhi mind, while walking, with every step he concentrated single-mindedly on the Buddha's thought, thanks to that, the present prince has become a Buddha, in the world of Wonderful Joy, he is the Buddha Akshobhya."

I believe that when walking on a wide road, when walking in a garden or a forest, one must practice the Dharma like Prince Mat To. When patience comes, whether it is when taking the throne or entering court with jade, horses and chariots are rumbling, flags and drums are majestic, there is no way not to use the effort to meditate at that time instead!

As a person, there is no one who does not breathe in and out. Most other people use pearls, jade, tree seeds, etc. as a chain of recitation, while I use breath as a chain of recitation. Reciting the Buddha's name with the breath has a very strong reliance. Don't be afraid that if a breath doesn't come back, it will belong to the next life! When I walk, stand, lie down, or sit, I always use that rosary. Even when I'm too tired, I sleep with the Buddha in my mouth, and when I suddenly wake up, I connect it again. Then in my sleep I saw Amitabha Buddha, like rubbing a tree and giving off smoke, that was the starting point of fire. If you dream of seeing the Buddha forever, you will achieve right concentration. When you see the Buddha face to face, you will receive the Buddha's prediction, and you will definitely be reborn forever without missing a single one.

Question: So we can only think silently without having to recite it out loud?

Answer: There are five meanings that require chanting the Buddha's name out loud. 1. Uprooting a tree by its roots requires the urging of a voice. A lifetime of diligence will eliminate hundreds of worries and sorrows; 2- Wherever the Buddha's voice reaches, all disasters will disappear, and the merit and virtue of those who follow the forest and mountains will prosper thanks to the sound;

3- The holy scene appears and the flowers from the sky are showered because of the sound; 4- It's like pulling a stone that's too heavy, making a loud noise and then walking lightly to the ground; 5- Like an army marching into battle thanks to the sound of drums and horns, soldiers move back and forth based on the place where orders are issued.

According to the above meanings, thinking and reciting the same language, just contemplation of two fortunes, very consistent with the Buddha's intention, there is no problem! Hua Yan said: “It is better to endure immeasurable sufferings and hear the Buddha's voice, than to enjoy joys without hearing the Buddha's name.” So in time, Buddha's voice resonated far and wide, spreading good roots to all living beings. It seems that the thunder of Spring animates the vitality of plants and trees, which should not be underestimated"...

Regarding the teaching: "The reason for dual practice is that of birth and non-birth", he said: "Many people say that reciting the Buddha's name is a conscious thought, but I think that reciting the Buddha's name is non-thought. Reciting is "emptiness", it is not considered "existence". "Buddha" that is "the birth of the mind". Again, that is "the baseless part", that "cultivation of the Buddha's name" that is "the one and only dharma". Again, "the mind with no thought" that is "mindfulness is emptiness", but that is "emptiness is the thought". This is the meaning of "two states of mind, two reflections". The light that is always calm is "reciting the mind without mind", the light that is always clear is "that of cultivating the Buddha's name". The Tathagata's right concentration and light is Therefore, reciting the Buddha's Samadhi can give birth to Shurangama Samadhi.

The verse of breaking the form in the Sutra "Bodhisattva Reciting the Buddha's Samadhi" says: Reciting the Buddha's pure golden body, calm the mind without attachment. Meditating on what dharma is called Buddha? The mind always observes. The yellow color is not the Tathagata, nor are the following four aggregates. Leaving form and space, Tathagata, one who contemplates form should understand. That is the pure, most sublime place of the Tathagata. Can skillfully destroy all the wrong views of pagans. Like the Dragon King sending heavy rain, all species benefit.

In this Sutra, it clearly points out the Six Paramitas and Ten Thousand Practices, there is no dharma that is not "reciting the Buddha's Samadhi". In the Mahaprajna Prajnaparamita, the Buddha said that all dharmas do not pass away to teach people with dull faculties, because this class gives rise to attachments. As for those with good faculties, the Buddha explained the Buddha's good appearance, because he knew that the lotus was not contaminated by the world. In the Sutra "Zazen Samadhi" it is said: "The Bodhisattva who meditates does not contemplate all other dharmas, but only recites one Buddha, like the golden Mount Meru in the middle of a wide, cool ocean. He also contemplates the merits of the Buddha's Dharma body in the same way."

Due to the above passages and reasons, we know that no thought should not be thought of as no thought. Contemplating the true Buddha's appearance is the same, contemplating the body, every scene encountered is the true nature, no mind is not a Buddha. Decide not to leave thought but maintain non-thought, to leave birth but also establish non-birth. If we separate thought and birth and establish no-thought and no-birth, it is because we do not understand the principle that "affliction is Bodhi, sentient beings are Buddha". It is impossible to separate, but when you have righteous thoughts, you are thoughtless; when you are reborn, you are truly not born. That meaning is very clear, like a quiet autumn night, the bright full moon emerging from the clouds!...

In the year Vinh Thoi of the Tang Dynasty, the Zen Master was invited by the court to hold the position of "Chief Witness" in the Sutra translation conferences. Such as Nhon Vuong Protecting the Nation, Prajnaparamita Sutra, Secret Nghiem Sutra, etc.

Excerpted from the series Tong Cao Tang Truyen

Precious Samadhi Treatise

---o0o---

VI - HOAI NGOC

Lawyer Hoai Ngoc, surnamed Cao, from Don Khuu, strictly maintained the precepts and dignity, practiced Dau Da conduct, ate one mid-day meal, always sat without lying down, used one set of robes all year round, allowing lice to live freely. Every day, the Lawyer plans to recite Buddha's name fifty thousand sentences. Throughout his life, he recited the Amitabha Sutra thirty thousand volumes, and always worshiped and repented.

In the year of Thien Buu of the Tang Dynasty, on the 9th day of the sixth month, in the sky, Buddha and Bodhisattva were seen as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. One of them carried a silver platform to process. He said: "I will recite Buddha's name all my life, and I will only sit on the golden dais!". The saints immediately hid. The lawyer became even more diligent. 21 days later, he heard a voice in the void saying: "A great light has appeared above your head. You should sit cross-legged and wait for the Buddha to come!".

Three days later, a strangely beautiful light shone throughout the temple. He told the crowd: "Whenever I hear a strange fragrance, that is when I will be reborn!". Then he composed a verse that said: "Pure, bright, clean without any stains. The golden throne of the highest grade is waiting. I have practiced virtue for ten lifetimes. Appearing in this world to suffer a state of suffering. One life of asceticism is more than ten lifetimes. Completely leaving Saha to return to the Pure Land." As soon as I finished writing the verse, a strange scent filled the entire temple. The holy congregation fills the whole of space. Amitabha Buddha and Avalokiteśvara and Mahasthamaprapta appeared in bright yellow, sitting on a diamond platform to receive the procession. The lawyer smiled and passed away.

Prefect Doan Hoai Nhien praised: "My teacher realized the Dharma body in one thought. The Buddha's realm's incense and music were carried out twice. In front of the alley, there was a tall and tall kneeling tree. The only branches left were golden pedestals."

Excerpted from Tong Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

VII - TE HOANG

Dharma Master Qi Hoang, surname Tram, surname Dang Chi, from Huzhou, became a monk at Vinh Dinh pagoda. Quiet in nature, he stayed away from fame and trouble, often staying in a quiet room as if there were no one around. He specializes in the commentaries on the Dharma Sect and is knowledgeable about the Lotus Sutra. He used to be the Dharma Master of the Dharma altar in To Ho.

In the 10th year of the Dai Lich, he attended the Buddhist chantry at Luu Thuy. Concentrating on reciting Buddha's name for a while, he suddenly saw the Pure Land realm, so he recited to himself: "The flowing water is rippling. The brilliant lotus radiates golden light. Sitting on the flower platform, going to the Pure Land. Who are you, go to heaven!".

Not long after that, one day the Dharma Master fell ill and told his disciples: "The white crane flew in front of me, did you see it?". The disciple asked: "The monk is about to be reborn, why is he sick?". The magician said: "The body of the four great elements is impermanent, even if it is a Saint, it still has not recovered." Having finished speaking, the Dharma Master turned his face to look at the Amitabha Buddha statue and passed away, at the age of 68 years old.

III - INCREASED TEST

Dharma Master Tang Te entered Lo Son to receive teachings from Great Master Hue Vien and demonstrated his understanding of the essential Dharma. When he was thirty years old, he went to the court to open the lecture and the scholars were impressed. Great Master Hue Vien praised: "If you are propagating the Dharma together with me, is this Sangha?"

Not long after, the Dharma Master became seriously ill, so he earnestly prayed to be born in the Pure Land soon, day and night commemorating Amitabha Buddha. Master Hue Vien gave him a large candle and said: "Try to reflect on the West!". The magician held a candle in both hands and sat leaning against the chair, single-mindedly thinking of Buddha without distraction. The magician again asked the monks to recite the Infinite Life Sutra. At the fifth watch, the Dharma Master gave the candle to his disciple, Mr. Nguon Bat, and told him to follow them and practice the Dharma. The shaman temporarily lay down to rest and then dreamed that he was holding a candle in his hand and flying in the sky, meeting Buddha Amitabha leading him to all ten directions. When he woke up, the Dharma Master was happy and said: "I pay attention to the memory of the night when the Buddha welcomed me." Examine yourself, your body is completely free from any illness or suffering, no different from someone who is not sick. The next night, the Dharma Master who was sitting reciting the Buddha's name suddenly stood up, looked up and told Nguon Bat: "The Buddha is coming to pick you up, let's go!". Having finished speaking, the Dharma Master turned his face to the West, clasped his hands and passed away. At that time, it was hot weather, three days later, the Dharma Master's corpse was like a living person, emitting a sweet scent. That year, the Wizard was 45 years old.

Excerpted from the series Tong Cao Tang Truyen

Dong Lam Truyen

IX - HUE CONG

Dharma Master Hue Cung, from Du Chuong, attended the Lien Xa meeting in Lo Son. He was a close friend of Tang Quang and Hue Lang. The two Dharma masters, Tang Quang and Hue Lang, were not as educated as him, but their aspirations and practice were more diligent. Two Dharma Masters once told him: "Senior brother, although you have learned a lot and understand a lot, do you not know that in the Avatamsaka Sutra there is a reminder: "Like a deaf person playing music, it pleases the ears of others but you yourself do not hear it at all." Listening to what the two of you said, he still did not think it was right.

Within seven years, Tang Quang and Hue Lang, two Dharma masters, passed away one after another. When the two Dharma Masters passed away, he saw many responses from the two reincarnated people. And five years later, he became seriously ill and complained to himself: "Revolving forever in the six paths, I don't know when it will end, where will I go after death?". The shaman forced himself to go to the statue of Amitabha Buddha, bowed his head, and shed tears like rain, vowing to return to the Pure Land, with his mind undistracted all day long. At first I saw Amitabha Buddha carrying a golden dais to receive him, and he saw himself sitting on that dais. He again saw Tang Quang and Hue Lang, two companions standing in the light of the golden platform, and said to him: "Elder has been reborn as a High Rank, we are very happy, we only regret that it has been delayed until today!". He quickly called the crowd to come and tell the story, then passed away happily. At that time, it was the 11th year of Yixi of the Jin Dynasty.

Excerpted from the series Dong Lam Truyen

X - HUE THANH

Great Master Hue Thanh's family name is Doan, from Le Duong. At this time, the Great Master studied at Thap Tru Pagoda. Hearing the voice of Master Hue Tu, the Great Master went to Nam Nhac to study. The great master practiced the Dharma very diligently and often meditated with his eyes open from early morning until morning. Zen Master Hui Tu told the Great Master to enter the Samadhi, Directional Samadhi, Guan Yin Samadhi, Phap Hoa Samadhi and Bat Chu Samadhi, to eliminate obstacles. The Great Master practiced these Samadhi subjects for three years, attaining the "Samadhi of understanding the speech of sentient beings".

Later, the Great Master went to Kinh Chau to establish a temple and stay there. Every day, the Great Master recited the Amitabha Sutra, visualized the Western Pure Land, and sat without lying down for thirty years. Every time the Great Master entered samadhi, he often saw the temple and the treasure. One day, the Great Master told his disciples to meet in the Tran Thiet Hall so that the Great Master could preach Nirvana. When the preparations were finished, Master Tri Gia arrived from Ngoc Tuyen. The two Great Masters sat together and discussed mystical principles. After a while, Great Master Hue Thanh passed away peacefully in his seat. At that time, people saw the Great Master sitting on a hidden platform flying towards the West.

B 2 - MONKS

I - HUE AN

Nun Hue An, from Minh Chau, lives in the Duong family monastery in Tieu Khe. Dedicated to cultivating the Pure Land all her life, reciting the Diamond Sutra, no matter Winter or Summer, she was never late. The Nun often saw the Buddha's light shining in her room.

One day when she was sick, the Nun sat upright and told everyone not to make a noise. A moment later the Nun said: "Buddha has come!". Then he told them to recite the Buddha's name in unison, while the Nun still sat upright, clasped her hands facing the West and passed away, at the age of 96.

Excerpted from the series Buddhist Records

II - CHAU CAM

Nun Chau Cam, family name Thang, surname Thai To. The Hangzhou native, who was Tram Giao Tho's wife, was Master Lien Tri. The day Tram Giao Tho became a monk, Chau Cam was only 19 years old. Someone urged her to stop her. She said: "Don't you listen and keep saying "life and death are great" every day? If you hinder it, it means harming you, and you will also damage your virtue. Don't!" At the age of 47, she became a monk and received full ordination. She keeps her precepts very strictly, diligently cultivates the Pure Land, specializes in reciting Buddha's name and performing repentance ceremonies.

In the 42nd year of Van Lich, she fell ill, and when she was about to die, she told her attendant: "The sutra says ten recitations of rebirth, help me up quickly!" Then the Nun sat upright, facing the West, clasped her hands and recited Buddha's name and walked away, at the age of 67.

Excerpted from the series Hieu Nghia Am Luc

III - ADVERTISING

Nun Quang Giac, surnamed Cung, from To Chau. While still living in the secular world, she became a vegetarian from the age of 12, recited Sutras every day, diligently worshiped Buddha, and vowed not to get married. At the age of 28, he became a monk and became a monk at Hieu Nghia hermitage in Hangzhou. She kept her precepts very strictly and diligently practiced without regard for hardship.

Later, when she fell ill, she refused medicine and was determined to die. While lying there gasping for breath, she suddenly stood up and sat cross-legged facing west. The Amitabha prepared the table and placed the statue of Amitabha in front of her. She opened her eyes to look at the Buddha statue and clasped her hands respectfully. Then she washed her hands, changed her clothes, held the string of Buddha objects and sat upright, quietly as if in meditation. The attendant was afraid that she would fall, so he used two big pillows to support her. She waved her hand and told her not to. The people in the hermitage came around to recite Buddha's name. She said: "Don't dare to trouble the masses, I have my own policy!". She sat cross-legged upright like that, chanting Buddha's name softly day and night without moving and chanting without stopping. It wasn't until she lost her voice that everyone came closer to see that she had passed away. On the 7th day of the second month, the 39th year of Wanli of the Ming Dynasty. She was 33 years old at that time.

Excerpted from the series Hieu Nghia Am Luc

IV - THANH TINH

Nun Thanh Tinh, surnamed Thiet Tu, from Guangzhou, has been a vegetarian and kept the precepts since childhood. After becoming a monk and receiving full ordination day and night, she recited Buddha's name non-stop. She once advised the public to work together to carve a statue of Thien Thu Thien Thien Nhan Dai Compassion out of Dandelion wood. It took almost a year for the statue to be carved, and she had just fallen ill. She knows the date and time in advance. When the time came, she told the crowd: "The Great Compassion Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva came to pick me up!". Having finished speaking, she closed her eyes and passed away.

V - TREASURE

Nun Trieu Am, Kim family, Thuong Thuc family, daughter-in-law of the Also family. Her husband died early, she remained a widow, and then together with her son, Doan Ngo, decided to become a monk. When Doan Ngo became a monk, she also went to To Chau to worship Nun Chon Nhu to pray for salvation. After receiving ordination as a nun, she returned to her village to rent a house to practice, reciting Buddha's name day and night six times a day.

One day, when she was slightly ill, she showered, put on her clothes and sat firmly in the middle of the house. In the afternoon, she said: "I'll go now!". Up to now, she still sits in the same place, puts her hands in her shirt and passes away, at the age of 73. At that time, it was the year of Thuan Tri of the Qing Dynasty.

C 2 - TRUSTEES

I - HOANG DAO MEMBER

Mr. Yuan Hongdao, alias Trung Lang, alias Shi Dau Layman, from Hubei. His older brother's name is Tong Dao and his name is Ba Tu, his younger brother's name is Trung Dao and his name is Tieu Tu. All three brothers passed the Ming Dynasty doctorate and all liked Zen Buddhism.

In the year of Van Lich, Mr. Hoang Dao became Tri of Ngo Giang district, then became Head of the Ministry of Rites, then promoted to the position of Huan Tu Lang Trung, then called home sick. At first, he studied meditation with Ly Trac Ngo, understood well and liked to argue. He judged to himself that it was just empty talk and not a true testimony that would be of any use in the matter. He then dedicated himself to praying for rebirth in the Pure Land, chanting morning and night, and keeping the precepts. He once took the teachings from the Sutras and created them into the "Western Association of Treatises", perfecting the whole nature and entering the non-dual world. In that volume, in the chapter on "The Five Kinds of Virtue" which is very essential, the summary is as follows:

One is “Belief in the heart”. The sutras teach that faith is the beginning of the path and the mother of merit. Faith in the mind is the main cause of all meritorious deeds, reaching the Supreme Bodhi is only the completion of this faith. Like a grain of rice falling to the ground, until it blooms, it remains the same, like a bamboo shoot until it becomes a tall bamboo, it is still the same tree. The Bodhisattva's initial mind depends on the power of faith to achieve success. Pure Land Buddhism uses faith as the basis: 1- Believe in the basic wisdom and immovable wisdom of Amitabha Buddha and ourselves are no different. Like vast space, when the sun is bright, sometimes it is bright, when the clouds are spread out, it is dark, space is still no different. Besides, the sky and clouds are not outside of nothingness, they are also nothingness. 2- Believe in Amitabha Buddha, through countless lifetimes, he has practiced countless outstanding meritorious deeds, making it difficult to endure difficult situations. I can practice like that too. Why ? Because from beginningless time until now, I have been immersed in the three paths and six paths, suffered countless times of life and death, until I wore feathers and horns, sat on a knife and lay on fire, I have been able to endure so much useless suffering, not to mention this Bodhisattva's work of saving sentient beings, how can I not be able to do it because I am afraid of hardship? 3- Believing in Amitabha Buddha to achieve immeasurable wisdom, immeasurable magical powers, immeasurable vows, etc., I will also be able to do the same. Because the Tathagata, from his pure self-nature, has all these immeasurable and immeasurable uses, I, along with the Tathagata, still have the same pure nature. 4- Believe in Amitabha Buddha, there is no past and no future, and we also have no past and no future. The West and Saha are only an inch apart, if you want to see it, you will see it. Because all Buddhas use the dharma nature as their body and realm. 5- Believing in Amitabha Buddha and practicing patiently until attaining fruition is not beyond a moment, nor is we beyond a moment, because we are on par with the Buddhas. Because time belongs to karma, in the nature of dharma there is no karma. Having all five articles of faith explained like this is the conduct of beginners who believe in the Pure Land of all Buddhas.

The second is “Mere contemplation of conduct”. The three contemplations of the Lotus Sect teach the teachings of single-mindedness and the essence of all dharmas. The sixteen dharma contemplations of the Pure Land, each contemplation covers all three subjects. In Dieu Tong Sao, it is said:

The body of the three virtues in nature is the three bodies of the Buddhas. It is these three virtues and three bodies INCLUDEPICTURE "http://www.quangduc.com/tinhdo/77duongvecuclac8-2_files/image001.gif" \* MERGEFORMATINET INCLUDEPICTURE "http://www.quangduc.com/tinhdo/77duongvecuclac8-2_files/image001.gif" \* MERGEFORMATINET is the one-pointed mind of three contemplations of oneself. If it were not like that, then there would be a Buddha outside of contemplation of wisdom, so that the scene does not include the mind, and it would not be wonderful. It is also possible that Amitabha Buddha's three bodies are Dharmakaya, his three contemplations are Prajnaparamita, and contemplation to see Buddha is Liberation. Hold one but have all three, like the words INCLUDEPICTURE "http://www.quangduc.com/tinhdo/77duongvecuclac8-2_files/image002.gif" \* MERGEFORMATINET . Contemplation of the Buddha is like that, so is the time of contemplation of other warnings and warnings. As it is clearly explained in the series of stars, this is not a complete translation. Understanding the above meaning, you will know that one recitation of the Buddha's name is enough for all three contemplations. It is clear that the mind that is capable of reciting is not the heart, not the cause, this is not contemplation. Understanding that the Buddha's thoughts are fully integrated throughout space and time, this is false contemplation. Absolute clarity and understanding, dual disappearance, dual illumination, this is the middle way. Again, constant recitation is one mind and three contemplations, and mindfulness is one state and three truths. Non-dual energy and facility are meant to contemplate non-duality together. The three truths are the Dharmakaya, the three contemplations are Prajnaparamita, the truth and contemplation are non-dual, and reciting the Buddha in conjunction is Liberation. Holding one means all three words INCLUDEPICTURE "http://www.quangduc.com/tinhdo/77duongvecuclac8-2_files/image002.gif" \* MERGEFORMATINET . So chanting the Buddha's name once can purify all four realms, like holding a grain of dust and turning the earth into sulfur metal. This is called the contemplation of "The Dharma Realm is perfect and indifferent".

Third is "The Six Virtues". The Commentary on the Origin of Faith says: Bodhisattvas deeply understand and present the basis of cultivating renunciation. Because they know the nature of the Dharma and leave greed, they accordingly practice the "paramita of giving". Because we know the immaculate nature of the Dharma, we abandon the five desires and practice the "paramita precepts" accordingly. Because you know the nature of the Dharma is not suffering, leave anger and anger and practice "Paramiti" in accordance with the practice. Because we know that the nature of the Dharma has no form, our body and mind let go of idleness and follow the "paramita of diligence". Because we know that the nature of the Dharma is permanent, we cannot be disturbed, but we can practice "paramita meditation" accordingly. Because we know that the nature of the Dharma is inherently clear, we leave ignorance and practice "Prajnaparamita" accordingly. Therefore, Pure Land practitioners have no more than one practice that fulfills all six meanings. While reciting the Buddha's name, reciting renunciation is the practice of "giving", reciting purity is the practice of "precepts", reciting the Buddha's name is the practice of "forbearance", reciting continuously is the practice of "diligence", reciting pure concentration is the practice of "concentration", reciting the Buddha's name is the practice of "wisdom". You should know that: "Separation from Tich Tich Tuc Nhut" must have appearances that arise depending on conditions, but from reciting the Buddha's name, it becomes true, supports non-duality, appearances are non-dual. Therefore, one practice of reciting Buddha's name includes all practices. Because reciting the Buddha's name is a single-minded method that inherently has no virtue in the mind. If you abandon your actions, you abandon your mind.

Fourth is the “Prayer of Compassion”, in the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the ocean of nature is endless, offerings are endless, precepts are endless, patience reaches endless benefits. Therefore, Bodhisattva Thien Than Bodhisattva recites the "Pure Land of Five Mindfulness Gates", using four subjects: "Presting, praising, praying, observing" to achieve the "entering merit" part, and using one subject "dedicating all afflictions to sentient beings throughout the world" to achieve the "exporting merit" part. Bodhisattvas who practice these five Pure Land disciplines will quickly attain Supreme Enlightenment. Complaining: “The Pure Name Sutra says: “Bodhisattvas observe sentient beings that are inherently empty. If I vow to save sentient beings, they are all like echoes, like shadows, like bubbles of water, etc...." Since sentient beings are inherently empty, if I vow to save sentient beings, is it like seeing flowers and spots with blind eyes? Explaining that: "In the Treatise on Wisdom, it is written: "Buddha said no Buddha is to destroy the concept of attachment to Buddha, not the intention of saying to accept the form of non-Buddha." You should understand that saying no to sentient beings is to destroy the concept of attachment to sentient beings, not to say to accept the form of non-living beings. Therefore, the Pure Name Sutra continues: "After observing like that, the Bodhisattva thought to himself that for the sake of sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma of non-living beings, that is compassion. "True". Therefore, to see that Bodhisattvas always save sentient beings is to clearly understand the meaning of no sentient beings. If you see that there are sentient beings, then there is a self. If there is a self-view, then the compassionate mind is weak, and it is not possible to practice great deeds to benefit sentient beings.

Fifth is “Worthy Dharma Conduct”. The Dharma realm is boundless and boundless, and the deeds of the Bodhisattva are also boundless and boundless, so all of the Bodhisattva's deeds are also worthy of the dharma nature: non-existence, non-existence, neither practiced nor non-practiced. Worthy of the Dharma's own nature: not the first mind, not the later mind. Now briefly explain that general practice: A-Bodhisattva saves sentient beings to the ultimate Nirvana without residue without the sentient beings' precepts decreasing. Like a mannequin playing the piano, smiling and speaking clearly, but it's just an empty piece of wood. B- Bodhisattvas either practice the five uninterrupted karma without any sadness, go to hell without sin, go to the animal world without all kinds of ignorance, arrogance... Like a divorced girl whose husband patiently gives birth to children, but her body remains pure and does not leave her biological mother's side. C- Bodhisattva himself enters concentration and then exits concentration in a human body, enters concentration in one body but exits concentration in many bodies. Entering concentration in a sentient body but coming out of concentration in an inanimate body... Like a fierce tiger rising up, kneeling and dancing, it's just the tiger's will, not the body, but still unconscious. D- Bodhisattva in the body of small sentient beings turns the Dharma wheel, lights the Dharma giant, shakes the Dharma lightning, the demon palace collapses, the great earth shakes, and saves limitless and boundless sentient beings, but the small sentient beings still do not know anything. It was like the Heavenly Emperor's Divine Music crawling into her nostrils to hide, but she still didn't know. E-Bodhisattva wanted to stay in this world for a long time, so he used the time of one thought to extend it into countless hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of nadotha eons. If you want to live a short life, the Bodhisattva will shorten countless countless hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of nadotha kalpas into the time of one thought. Like children watching horses run at the lights to draw soldiers, it is impossible to consider whether there is more or less.

If a person can attain the above non-thoughtful actions, in the space of a single thought, he will be able to capture the entire Pure Land of the Buddhas of the three times. This is called the solemn conduct of the Bodhisattva's Pure Land. If you use your impartial mind to look at it, you will see it, something that ordinary minds cannot measure. Because self-nature transcends all limitations.

When the "Western Agreement" was just finished being compiled, the Tong Dao and the Middle Dao simultaneously developed the intention to dedicate to the Pure Land.

A little while later, Mr. Hoang Dao came to live at a temple in Kinh Chau and passed away without getting sick.

Mr. Trung Dao was a mandarin, holding the position of Ministry of Rites Lang Trung. After resigning, he returned home and diligently worshiped Buddha and chanted sutras every day. In the 42nd year of Van Lich, on the full moon night of the first lunar month, after finishing the recitation, he suddenly entered meditation, got out of the house in a trance, lightly flew along the clouds, two disciples led him flying to the West, and momentarily lowered down and shouted: "Stop!". Trung Dao landed and saw the ground was flat, smooth and shining. On one side is a large pond, in the pond are lotus flowers of all five colors, with an unusual fragrance. Across the pond, bridged with sulfur, on the other side of the golden bridge, you can see the railings and the magnificent castle. Trung Dao clasped his hands together and asked: "What place is this, who are you?". Answer: "We are the attendants of Mr. Linh Hoa!". Question: "Who is Mr. Linh Hoa?". Answer: "It's your brother, Mr. Trung Lang! I'm waiting for you right now. Let's go quickly!". Then the pupil led him to a place with beautiful and tall trees, a pond with cool, clear water, and beside the pond there was a gateway made of white jade. A boy led him, past more than twenty layers of temples, to the bottom of a large building, there was a person coming down, his face shining like jade, his clothes fluttering like clouds, and he was over a foot tall. That person greeted: "You're there!". He looked closely and was now Mr. Hoang Dao. The two mediums went upstairs, and five other people came and sat at the table.

Hoang Dao told him: "This is the border of the world of Ultimate Bliss, also known as the Land of Lama. People who practice Pure Land but have not yet achieved faith and have not yet perfected their precepts and virtues are mostly born here. Up here is the temple of the Buddha of Transformation. In front of that temple there is a lotus pond about a hundred yojanas large, which is the place of rebirth for those who are reborn. After being born, they will separate into temples and reunite with predestined people. Because there is absolutely no defilement of love, it is easy to attain victory. "Sometimes it's time to be a human being in the Pure Land." Trung Dao asked: "Where were you born?". Hoang Dao replied: "When I was still a human being, my vows were deep, but my defilements had not yet been eliminated, so I was born here. Now I have been born in the Pure Land. Even though I was in the Pure Land, but because my precepts were not yet perfect in my previous life, I could only live on the ground and could not live with the Great Beings in the pavilion of space. I still need to practice more. Fortunately, thanks to my powerful wisdom in my previous life, I have the four collections of "Western Association of Treatises", praising the unconditional power to save sentient beings. of the Tathagata should feel the freedom to fly and be able to go to other worlds to listen to the teachings of the Buddhas.

Having finished speaking, Hoang Dao held Trung Dao's hand and flew up into the void, in the blink of an eye, he left the old place thousands of miles away, arriving in a land where everywhere was bright and clear, the land was lapis lazuli, the trees were seven jewels, all were auspicious sandalwood trees, on the trees countless beautiful flowers shone like rings of fire. There is a vast treasure pond, with natural ripples emitting countless wonderful sounds. In the pond there are countless lotus flowers made of gold and jade treasures... petals emitting light of five colors. On the shore of the pond are hidden towering castles, rows of long rows, wide and flat paths along the rows of buildings. Every castle has countless musical instruments that always perform magical teachings...

Hoang Dao said: "The realm you are looking at belongs to the abode of earthly beings in the Pure Land. Beyond this place is the abode of the Great Beings, which is infinitely better than here, with magical powers also tenfold better. Thanks to the power of wisdom, you can go there but cannot stay there. Past there, is the abode of the Ten Levels of Equal Enlightenment Bodhisattva, you cannot understand. Beyond that is the abode of Wonderful Enlightenment, only Buddha and Buddha can understand." After the lecture, Hoang Dao led Trung Dao and said: "I did not expect such limitless and beautiful joy. If I had strictly observed the precepts when I was still in Saha, then that would not be all! If people, precepts, and wisdom are all complete, then they will be reborn with very high dignity. Only pure moral conduct will also be reborn very well. But if you have wisdom but no virtue, then most of the time you will be drawn by karma into the eight groups of ghosts and gods. I have seen many people. In you, you have the spirit of Prajna. There are many, but the power of precepts is very weak. And the person who understands the principles but does not give birth to precepts is crazy, not true wisdom. After returning to Saha, you must try to truly understand, truly practice pure vows, diligently practice kindness to all. Soon you will reunite with me. If you stray from other paths, it will be terrifying. If you cannot practice pure precepts, then it is important to practice the precepts First, he sent a message to his monks in Saha: No one who cuts meat and fishes every day, and is greedy for delicious food, has been born in this pure and dignified world of Ultimate Bliss. Even if you are so talented in preaching the Dharma, what is the use? You and I have been brothers for countless lifetimes, even when we were in the evil path By the way, I came here to advise you. The pure world and the impure world are separate, we cannot keep you here for long!". Trung Dao asked about Tong Dao's birthplace, because Tong Dao had passed away. Hoang Dao said: "His birthplace is also very good, later you will know for yourself." Having finished speaking, Hoang Dao flew into thin air and disappeared. Trung Dao alone walked slowly on the shore of the precious pond to admire the scenery. Suddenly he lost his footing as if he had fallen into the water. He was startled and woke up, only to find that he was meditating at home. That's why he recorded the above things in the book.

Before Hoang Dao was reborn, Tong Dao had a son named Dang, 13 years old, with an intestinal disease. When he was about to die, he said to Hoang Dao: "I'm going to die! Is there any way to save him?" Hoang Dao said: "If you single-mindedly recite Buddha's name, you will be reborn in the Pure Land. This place is a life of evil and misery, not worth being attached to!" Dang immediately clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name. Relatives also recited Buddha's name in unison to help. Moments later, Dang smiled and said: "I see a pink lotus bud." After a while, Dang said again: "The lotus is so big and its color is so bright." A moment later, Dang said: "The Buddha has arrived. His appearance is very beautiful! His body radiates light throughout the whole house." Then he opened his mouth to proclaim Buddha! Buddha ! but stopped breathing. Dang's hands were still clasped upright on his chest.

II - NGUYEN HI

Mr. Ngu Thuan Hi, from Truong Nhu, from Tien Duong, was a lay disciple of the Great Master Bat Patriarch Lien Tri. When he was only three years old, he always chanted the Buddha's name and saw a lotus flower and a precious tree appear in his house. His grandmother, a female follower of the teachings, said: "That is the good scene of the Western Pure Land!". Only then did she teach me the method of meditation. From that day on, he often sat upright and closed his eyes to meditate. Mr. Thuan Trinh, his younger brother, together with him practiced Thien Thai meditation. When he worked as a monk in the neighborhood, he had free time to teach his children how to practice contemplation. After passing the bachelor's degree, teaching in Tuy Son, he promoted the establishment of a Buddhist association. At one time, together with the other associations, they recited Luong Hoang Sam's seven-fold prayer. On the second day, auspicious clouds shined light into the porch and walls dripping with nectar water. It rained golden-colored rice, jet-colored sticky rice, and agarwood-scented water. In the middle of icy winter, countless flowers bloom. Feeling that strange omen, Mr. Thuan Hi became more diligent in practicing meditation. Before long, he knew the past and the future, could foresee the sun and rain, good and bad things. When Master Lien Tri received the news, he sent a letter to reprimand him for being a demon, advising him not to be complacent.

In the 11th year of Van Lich, he passed his PhD. When his father died, he built a tent next to his father's grave for three years, then came to Van The to receive ordination from Great Master Lien Tri. His father's grave was on the mountain. Every day he gave rice and soup to cheetahs and rabbits. There were tigers and leopards that lingered until he chased them away.

At the end of the funeral, he took over the position of Phuong Ty, then resigned and went to Thien Muc mountain in front of Zen Master Cao Phong Dieu's coffin, meditating day and night. On the 21st day, he was so tired, he was about to go to bed, when suddenly he saw Zen Master Dieu appear and cut off his left arm. He immediately became enlightened, and when he arrived at Van The, he was certified by Great Master Lien Tri. The Great Master told him: "Anyone who wakes up from sleep, if they don't wash their face, comb their hair and put on a hat, but keeps lying on the pillow and blanket, will surely fall asleep again, but the person who is confused but will become enlightened, if they are not dignified and stay close to impure scenes, will surely fall asleep again. Lotus flowers near fire easily wilt, buds easily break, you must take care of yourself! Don't let a small ray of light hinder your path of practice. You should dedicate yourself to the Pure Land to ensure the path and fruition, which is also the cause. continue to be a good person". Obeying the Great Master's words, from then on he specialized in Pure Land cultivation.

There are people who do not believe in the Pure Land Dharma. He said: "Self-enlightenment, enlightenment of others, and perfect enlightenment are called Buddha. Therefore, reciting Buddha's name is enlightenment. Should reciting not always be enlightened but reciting often be deluded!".

Someone asked how to recite Buddha's name? He said: "In all times, always awakening to mindfulness is the key. Hundreds of thousands of means are just one word "knowledge". Mindfulness does not leave Infinite Light, then it is mindfulness straight into the Buddha's wisdom. People who study the path and practice diligently leave birth and death, now mindfulness does not leave Infinite Life, then there is no kind of birth and death that cannot escape!".

The court summoned him to hold the position of Tu Huan Lang Trung, but a short time later he resigned. At that time, Great Master Lien Tri was teaching the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra in Nam Binh Son. The Ransom Tomb of Ten Thousand Public Pond established an association to release living beings. The membership includes more than twenty thousand monks and laity. Among them, noble intellectuals make up a large number. The Kinh and French languages ​​shook the whole region. That freeing association also redeemed three large lagoons, built fences, put up guard posts, and made places to release birds and fish. All of the above great works were promoted by Mr. Thuan Hi.

Later, Mr. Thuan Hi always lived in Nam Binh Son, Mr. Thuan Trinh also hid in Linh Vuu mountain until old age.

If you can visualize, you will have no worries about not being reborn!". From then on, he specialized in contemplating Buddha. He went to Truong Can Pagoda in Nanjing, while worshiping the Buddha's name at the tower, at first he saw the top of the tower emitting white light, in the white light the Buddha appeared in yellow. One day, while sitting in the meditation hall looking out the window, I suddenly saw the vast ocean, in the middle of the sea there was a mountain, the Buddha sat on the top of the mountain, the Buddha's body radiated light in all four directions.

He was originally a talented writer, so he followed the literary style of life to express his principles. He authored the volumes: Lotus World Poetry, Tathagata Fragrance, Tan Gia Am, etc., published and propagated. He gave away a large part of his offerings to The Ha Pagoda.

Mr. Tran Toan, from Dinh Quan, from Giang Nam. Doctor of the Ming Dynasty, awarded the title of Hinh Khoa. Because of his outspokenness, he was dismissed from his position. He stayed at home early and late at night to concentrate on reciting Buddha's name.

One day, a guest came to his house and scolded him, saying: "Didn't you listen to Zen Master Dai Giam's idealistic treatise on the Pure Land? Why do you like to be pure when you're so boring?"

He replied: "Thought-only Pure Land came from Dai Giam's mouth, but it did not start from Dai Giam. "Your own mind creates Buddha, your own mind perceives Buddha", the Tathagata had already said a long time ago! Looking closely at Dai Giam's words, we are afraid that people use an impure mind to seek a pure realm, not to say that the world is free from impurity and purity. Discussing the joy in Ultimate Bliss, not only in golden land, precious trees, beautiful flowers, beautiful temples. Not only The birds singing, the dharma, the wind singing melodiously. But I can also gather with the great Bodhisattva Saints, live in the Buddha's limitless light, live for countless kalpas, attain the Endless Endurance, attain Supreme Bodhi, and save boundless sentient beings, that is truly worthy of joy.

Guests use their own meditation method, preferring impure realms. As for me, I use my meditation method, preferring the pure realm. A place of meditation, no guests, no me. A place that is neither impure nor pure. The customer has no reason to scold me!

In the year of Long Khanh, he was reinstated as Lai Khoa. In the year of Van Lich, he was promoted to the position of Hinh Bo Thi Lang.

In the 16th year of Van Li, in the seventh month, he lay sick, constantly reciting Buddha's name. At that time, there was a rule that during the sunny months, for officials of the third rank and above, the court provided ice water every day. That day, he left a block of ice next to his bed. Everyone saw a seven-storey tower appear in the block of ice, surrounded by a railing with a canopy, and the doors were hung with spirit jades. As the ice block melted, the tower also grew smaller. A moment later, when he died, the shadow of the tower also disappeared. People in the capital said it was a rare miracle.

V - STRICTLY

Mr. Nghiem Trung, nicknamed Dao Triet, from Giang Nam, worked as a governor in Thieu Vo. Retired in old age, staying at home to practice the Pure Land discipline of Great Master Lien Tri. His son Nghiem Phat is still a person who diligently recites Buddha's name and likes to do good. When he was 25 years old, he was sick and was about to die. He said: "Don't chant nonsense, just focus on reciting Buddha's name!". Phat replied: "Yes!". A moment later, he said again: "From now on, I will also single-mindedly recite Buddha's name." Phat happily said: "If that's the case then I won't have to worry anymore." Having finished speaking, Phat's face turned solemn and he clasped his hands and passed away.

He had Nghiem Phat's Pure Land Long Poetry printed out, then sent it to his relatives and friends near and far, along with a letter like this: "In the past, when I was sick and thought I was going to die, how could I expect to survive? Even if my life is still alive now, who knows what tomorrow will be! Thinking back to the many years in the battlefield and the time spent in business and family, it is as tasteless as chewing wax. This dirty skin will rot soon. What is the durability of Luc Tran's charm? Surely, there is nothing better than completely changing your mortal mind and praying to be born in the Pure Land, reciting a single Amitabha verse, and giving away this collection of Pure Land texts to show your sincerity.

At the age of 78, he was enlightened and mindful and passed away.

VI - THAI YUAN REALITY

Mr. Thai Thua Thuc, from Quy Dinh, from Ho Quang. When he was twenty years old, he became a man and served Buddha. He often recited the "Three Thousand Buddha Name Sutras", every day memorizing the three names of the Buddha. In the 11th year of Wanli, he passed the doctor's degree to hold the position of Crown Prince in Shaoxing. Every day he recited the Diamond Sutra. He guided farmers, hired workers, and fellow practitioners to recite Buddha's name. He wrote a poem to express gratitude to the guests: "The guest misses An Duong's house. A temporary pot of grapes in the Tuong River, not worrying about tomorrow's business, just waiting for Western paper, settling down on a small thatched roof. A couple of plates of soy sauce fit in his mouth. In his heart, he wipes away love and hate, leaving no one to scold or complain."

The year he was about to die, he called himself "Bat Cuu Dao Nhon". When he became sick, he went to the temple to invite the monks to shave their hair. When I returned home, I saw the Holy crowd bringing the silver stage to process. He always called Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva when he passed away. He has written works such as Pure Land Poetry and Nhon Qua Tho that were circulated during his lifetime.

VII - PHUNG TAP

Mr. Phung Tap, surnamed Te Xuyen, a native of Shu, passed a doctorate in the Song Dynasty. At first he came to study with Zen Master Buddha Nhan, then went to study with Dai Hue Zen Master, then went to the mountain to practice meditation and was very enlightened. After enlightening, he practiced Pure Land, composing the ritual "Amitabha Sam". In the year of Shaoxing, when he took charge of Lo Nam, he promoted the Sangha and established an association to recite the Buddha's name, together vowing to be reborn. At that time, most of the Buddhist scriptures were lost because of the enemy's chaos. He used his salary to create 48 collections of Mahayana Sutras and 48 collections of Hinayana Sutras to offer to the temples. At the same time, he wrote a vow: My donation of Sutras, an act that fulfills both. Using wealth to create Sutras is "donation of wealth". Using the Sutra to transmit the Dharma is a "dharma offering". Donating wealth will bring you blessings on earth and in heaven. Donating Dharma will give you intelligence and wisdom. Both of those treasures are the cause of birth and death, the root of samsara. Now I vow to dedicate those two treasures to adorn the Pure Land so that when I die, I will be reborn in the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, flowers will bloom, I will see the Buddha hear the miraculous Dharma, I will attain the patience of Non-birth, I will not retreat, and I will enter Bodhisattva status. Then I will return to the impure realm in the ten directions, appearing in countless bodies to do Buddha work. I pray that I will be like Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, full of great compassion, full of great divine power, manifesting myself throughout all living beings, appearing in different forms and preaching Dharma to all living beings to gain wisdom, guiding all living beings to completely escape samsara, so that all living beings can become Buddhas. That is my wish to give away the Sutra.

Later he appointed Mang Chau. In the fall of the 23rd year of Shaoxing, he submitted a request for retirement, and at the same time informed the officials and his friends of the Dharma, and promised to die on October 3rd. When the time came, he ordered a high throne to be installed in the back hall. That morning, the official guests arrived at the palace. He continued happily as usual. Near noon, he straightened his hat and robes and bowed towards the royal palace. He invited Cao Su to temporarily take charge of affairs in Chau. Then he changed into monk's clothes, ascended to a high throne, and instructed all monks and nuns to diligently practice and propagate the Dharma to save sentient beings. Having finished his instructions, he held the staff at his knees, sat still and chanted. Cao Su said: "If the great mandarins live in such freedom, why don't they leave behind a poem to set an example for the world?" He opened his eyes again and told him to bring back paper and ink. He took the pen himself and wrote: "The head is thirty-one, the middle is nine and the bottom is seven, this old man said everything, the turtle's eyes turned red." He threw the pen and passed away.

VIII - NGO BINH TIN

Mr. Ngo Binh Tin, surnamed Tu Tai, is from Minh Chau. In the year of Shaoxing during the Song Dynasty, he became an official at the court. Because of quarreling with Tan Coi, he was expelled. He returned to the village to build a hut and meditated day and night, meditating on the Buddha's name and reciting Buddha's name. He bought a trunk and slept in it at night. At the beginning of the fifth watch, he knocked on the box and shouted loudly: "Mr. Ngo Binh Tin, let's go home! If the Three Realms are not at peace, we should not stay, the Western Pure Land has a connection. Mr. Ngo Binh Tin, go home quickly!". He heard the sound and immediately got up to meditate and recite the Buddha's name.

Going to the translation shop in Tieu Son, he sat in meditation. Moments later, he called his entourage and told them to listen. Everyone heard the melodious music coming from the West. IX - HO NHON

Mr. Ho Nhon, nicknamed Dat Phu, from the Former Tang Dynasty, was an official in the Song Dynasty. After becoming an intellectual, he was often close to Attorney Thanh Chieu. One day when he was sick, his son invited Thanh Chieu to his house. Thanh Chieu told him: "Dai Binh was always close to each other with this Hue Hanh, how could he not understand the final big event?". He said: "Is it true that when the mind is pure, then the salvation is pure?". Thanh Chieu asked: "In all times, are there absolutely no impure thoughts?". He replied: "Not yet." Thanh Chieu said: "In that case, how can we attain a pure mind?" He asked: "The sutra says that by saying Amitabha Buddha in one sentence, you can destroy the sins of birth and death for eighty million eons, what is that?". Thanh Chieu said: "Amitabha Buddha has great vows, great blessings, and the Buddha's luminous divine power is inconceivable, as clearly taught in the Sutras. Therefore, once the Buddha's name is spoken, all sins will disappear. Just like the sun standing in the shadow of snow and frost, it is no longer possible!". Hearing the explanation, he became enlightened, so he single-mindedly recited Buddha's name, and asked someone to invite the Sangha to come to his house to help him recite. A month later, Thanh Chieu, the Lawyer, came again. As soon as he saw it, he immediately said: "Why are you here so late? It's disturbing Avalokiteśvara, Dai The Chi's arrival has been waiting for a long time." Thanh Chieu and the monks recited the Buddha's name in unison. He happily clasped his hands and passed away.

He asked me to learn and explain the meaning to him. He understood the principles of cause and effect, tried to do good deeds and often went along the path of gathering paper and letters. Layperson Banh Nhi Lam saw this and knew that he was a person with good roots, so he invited him into Van Tinh Cac and advised him to recite Buddha's name. He was originally illiterate, but practiced very diligently, and then gradually learned to read and write.

A little while later, he took over the position of manager of animal release and burial at the Dieu Te festival in To District. Whenever he saw dead bodies or human bones, he always lamented the impermanence of human life, so his practice of reciting Buddha's name became even more diligent. When he was 69 years old, while still healthy as usual, he suddenly said goodbye to his relatives and friends and set a date to leave this world. When the time came, he closed the door and quietly stayed in the room. My colleagues rushed in to take a look and saw a Buddha statue on the altar, a pair of candles burning brightly, and a strange, fragrant incense. As for Mr. Duc Tam, he died sitting, facing west. It's just alcoholism, because I've been addicted for so long that I haven't been able to quit. Layperson Lai Thien Dung explained the sins of people who drink alcohol, he tried to avoid them. He also replied: "Amitabha Buddha!".

In the 8th year of the Republic of China, his legs were swollen and it was difficult to walk. One day he told his nephew to place an incense burner facing the West and said: "The Western world of Ultimate Bliss is very beautiful! You see how many shining precious lotus flowers there are. I will return to the Pure Land today." The nephew said: "How can your leg become swollen and weak?" He said: "The mind goes, not this body, flesh and blood!". The nephew obediently set up the incense burner, and while the nephew lit the incense, he sat cross-legged facing West, clasped his hands and recited a few words to Buddha, and passed away at the age of 75.

Excerpted from the series Thanh Hien Luc Tuc Bien

D 2 - FEMALE TRUSTEES

I - PHUNG THI

Phung Thi Phap Tin, from Quang Binh, wife of Tran Tu Cung in Tran Giao. As a child, Phung Thi was always weak. After returning to the Tran family, her illness became increasingly worse. At that time, Zen Master Tu Tho Tham propagated Buddhism in Vuong Thanh, and Phung Thi came to seek treatment. Deep Zen Master told me to be vegetarian and recite Amitabha Buddha. Phung Thi trusted.

After returning home, Phung Thi became a vegetarian, put on makeup, wore rough clothes, and diligently cultivated pure karma. All meritorious deeds: chanting Sutras, reciting Buddha's names, repentance ceremonies, giving alms, etc. are dedicated to praying for the Ultimate Bliss. It didn't take long for the illness to heal. Phung Thi still managed her family business and diligently cultivated her karma for ten whole years. Thi's face did not have the slightest hint of laziness, not a trace of pride, her mind was at peace, her body was healthy and her appearance became more and more fit every day.

One day, Phung Thi suddenly composed a verse that said: "Depending on karma for many years, working in vain as a buffalo plow is truly pitiful. The burden of body and mind will soon be freed from the yoke. From now on, I will no longer be afraid of being in trouble." When the family saw that verse, they were surprised and asked why. Phung Thi said: "In the world of pure mind, because of delusional thoughts, I fall into reincarnation. This person's karma will be fulfilled tomorrow. I will immediately return to the West. My wish is very satisfied. Is there any wonder?"

In September of that year, Phung Thi fell ill until December. One night, Phung Thi told the person who was guarding her illness: "I have been divinely journeyed to the Pure Land, worshiped at the feet of Amitabha Buddha, Avalokitesvara and Mahasthamaprapta looked at me. Hundreds of millions of saints joined hands to celebrate that I will be born in the Pure Land. It will be like a palace, a treasure pond, rows of trees, beautiful and bright, just as the Quan Sutra said. Whoever goes there will know for himself, it cannot be clearly described." The patient guard quickly called Tran Tu Cung to come and recounted the above words. Tu Cung knew that his wife was about to be reborn and immediately joined his family to recite Buddha's name with Phung Thi. In the early morning, Phung Thi lay on her right side and passed away, at the age of 36. Three days later, when entering the shroud, everyone heard a strange scent. When she brought the body down and pried open the coffin lid to see, Phung Thi's face was still as bright as when she was alive.

Excerpted from the series Lac Ban Van Loai

---o0o---

II - NGO THI

Ngo Thi, Lu Hoang's wife, both husband and wife were knowledgeable about Buddhism and united in their pursuit of purity. Both servants are also men. A person who liked meditation, not long after falling ill, still smiled and talked happily and passed away. A person who kept the precepts asceticism, or sometimes did not eat all day and only drank a bowl of water to worship the Buddha, one day the maid suddenly saw a large golden lotus flower appear before her. On the flowers, we can only see the bold legs of people sitting cross-legged. A few days later it was clear to the knees, a few days later it was clear to the abdomen and chest. A few days later, the whole head and face were clearly visible, and all good features were present. It turned out that the one sitting in the middle was Amitabha Buddha, on the left was Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and on the right was Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva. Before long, the palace, the pond, and the Saints all appeared clearly in front of us, for three years like this without a single hidden moment. Someone asked if they heard the Buddha preach? The maid replied: "I only have the heavenly eye but not the heavenly ear, so I have not yet heard the Buddha's sermon." Not long after, she told herself the date and time of her rebirth and then passed away.

Ngo Thi worshiped Avalokiteśvara very sincerely. In the quiet room, there were dozens of jars filled with clear water. Every day, chanting the Great Compassion mantra, we saw Avalokiteśvara radiating light into those jars. Anyone who is sick should drink that water and immediately be healed. Even though that water has been left for a long time, the smell still does not change. In the winter of the Cold season, other countries are frozen by the cold, but that country is still the same as usual. That's why people at that time called Ngo Thi "Quan Am Huyen Quan".

Excerpted from the series Pure Land Literature

III - VUONG THI

Vuong Thi is Ma Vinh Dat's wife. Mr. Vinh Dat specializes in purifying karma, the story is recorded in the story of Mr. Ma Vu. Vuong Thi also practiced Tu Van's method of ten thoughts of dedication. She often recites the verse to destroy hell, that is, the four verses in the Avatamsaka Sutra: "The weak desires of humanity are fully understood. The three worlds are all Buddhas. You should contemplate the dharma realm and the nature of the world. The mind is created all by yourself."

One night, Vuong Thi dreamed that the master of hell came to thank her and said: "Thanks to your merit of reciting verses, in hell there are many sinners who were born into Heaven."

Later, while lying sick, Vuong Thi chanted Buddha's name continuously, until her last breath. Both her relatives and the female servants had a dream and saw Thi returning and said: "I have been born in the Pure Land!".

Excerpted from the series Lac Ban Van Loai

IV - FOUR PEOPLE IN THE FRONT STREET

1) Gong Thi, Mr. Ton Bien's mother, recites Amitabha Sutra and Buddha's name every day. One day, when Thi was sick, she invited Lawyer Thanh Chieu to come to her house to preach the pure and solemn scene of Ultimate Bliss. Before the Master finished speaking, Gong Thi sat down and passed away.

The old servant named Vu also fasted and recited Buddha's name. She dreamed that Gong Thi came back and said: "I have been reborn in the Pure Land, seven days later you will be able to return." Exactly seven days later, Ms. Vu passed away without being sick.

2) Venerable Lady often recites Buddha's name and recites mantras. When she was sick, she invited Lawyer Thanh Chieu to come and tell her: "Having been sick for a long time, I am very bored with this life of excess. I don't know how to quickly escape this world of impurities and suffering, and attain pure and wonderful joy?" The Master explained to him the causes and conditions of the Pure Land. The Venerable Lady was very happy and dedicated her heart to the Pure Land. That night, Ton Nu dreamed that the Master gave her a bowl of medicine, and she immediately drank it. After waking up, I felt like I was gone. Three days later, Ton Nu told her family: "The holy crowd has arrived, the golden lotus throne is very beautiful and bright. I will go!". Having finished speaking, the woman raised her hand to make a seal and disappeared.

3) Thi Thi, the wife of Mr. Tram Thuyen, together with her husband practiced pure karma. Lawyer Thanh Chieu, following the Quan Sutra, painted the painting "Nine products of rebirth" for daily contemplation.
