Five years later, the two knew the date and time in advance, walked hand in hand to the pine forest, looked at each other and smiled: "We can stay here forever!". The attendant heard that, but did not understand. In less than a week, two people fell ill at the same time. Zhou Dynasty, 3rd year of Thien Hoa, on the 5th day of the 11th month, Dharma Master Hue Mang sat cross-legged, facing the West, chanting Buddha's name. When the crowd saw Amitabha Buddha appear, the Dharma Master immediately clasped his hands and passed away. There was a chant: "Good ear!". The sweet fragrance filled the entire temple, and the sound of heavenly music echoed throughout the void.

On the 17th of that month, Zen Master Phap Am also sat upright, facing the West, chanting Buddha's name, and passed away. The Buddha's appearance, fragrance, heavenly music, etc. are the same as when Dharma Master Hue Mang passed away, and at the same age as 38 years old.

The crowd built a tower for the two of them in the pine forest

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

III - INCREASED ORGANS

Monk Tang Tang from Tay Ha became a monk when he was young. He humbled himself to worship people, respected everyone, and did not spare any hardship. Seeing the monks' old robes, he secretly washed them and mended them with tweezers. He often takes off his shirt and sits in the grass to give blood to mosquitoes. Every day, I recite Buddha's name countless times, diligently and without delay. At the time of his death, the heavenly beings from the lower realms to the higher realms first came to receive him, but the Venerable refused. Silence for a moment, the Venerable told the crowd: "Just now I went to the Pure Land and saw the noble people scattering flowers in the sky." Having finished speaking, the Venerable clasped his hands and recited the Buddha's name and passed away.

Excerpted from the series Tong Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

IV - DAO KIET

Dao Kiet, a Dharma Master of the Duong family from Ha Dong, became a monk at the age of 20 and then went to Thanh Chau to listen to Master Ha Ky Luan preach the Truth Luan. After the Luan Master passed away, he went to many places to study the Luan Canon and opened lectures in many places.

One day he examined himself: "If you follow words and talk, your mind will be confused. Coming to true wisdom will not arise through right concentration and timing!". He then stopped preaching and studied meditation with Chan Hue Zen Master in Mac Coc. He penetrated dependent origination, which the Zen master praised as beneficial.

He was naturally quiet, had few desires, and did not care about suffering or happiness.

Later he became the monk of The Nham pagoda.

In the first year of Trinh Quan, on July 28, he fell ill and passed away. The whole pagoda heard strange scents and heavenly music. Also on this day, the two daughters of Mr. Phan Xuoc, a lay friend of the Dharma Master, dreamed of Mr. Xuoc sitting on a lotus in the sky and said: "Father has been reborn in the Western Pure Land, now come to receive Dharma Master Dao Kiet." Then he flew straight towards The Nham Pagoda. When the Dharma Master passed away, the crowd saw Mr. Xuoc appear and stand in the air.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

V - SPIRIT ELEMENT

Master Than To Luan's family name is Vuong, from Ha Dong, Dharma friend of Master Dao Kiet. When Dharma Master Dao Kiet stopped preaching to study meditation, the Commentator preached like that. In the second year of Trinh Quan, the Commentator became the monk in The Nham. All meritorious acts performed by oneself transform others, and the Commentator solemnly dedicates them to the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

In the 17th year of Trinh Quan, on February 23, the Commentator met the assembly to say goodbye, then sat down and told the assembly to read the Quan Am Sutra twice. The Commentator clasped his hands and listened attentively, then recited six Amitabha Buddha verses to himself. The commentator told the crowd how many times a person chants and follows. So until evening, the Commentator still sat upright and serious. They came closer and looked carefully, and saw where he had left. That night, Dharma Master Tri Khoan was sitting at Nhon Tho Pagoda. He saw the Commentator come to say goodbye and told him to try to uphold the Dharma to repay the Buddha's grace. This morning, the Dharma Master learned that Master Than To Luan had passed away yesterday afternoon.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

VI - MINH CHIEM

Master Minh Chiem's ​​family name is Do, from Hangzhou. When he was young, he had the will to leave the world, gave up the exam, and became a monk at Ung Giac Pagoda in Prefaceng Son. During the Sui dynasty, he was the master of many dharma thrones in the capital. Having his own alms, he made offerings to the monks and wrote poems describing the Mahayana Sutras. A little later he went into hiding at Tri Cu pagoda in Thai At mountain. In old age, he overcomes the Pure Land. Some people criticized him for being late. He said: "I can still see the Buddha after ten recitations, so I don't have to worry about being late!".

At the beginning of Trinh Quan's reign, he entered the inner hall and sat on the throne. After receiving his son's food, the Great Master extensively lectured on the art of ruling the country of the wise monarch, using kindness to protect sentient beings as the basis. The king was very pleased and immediately issued an edict spreading throughout the country: Every year for three big months, every month for six days, strictly prohibits killing meat, and ordered the establishment of many pagodas in all places.

In October of the 2nd year of Trinh Quan, feeling sick, the Great Master knew the date and time in advance, so he went to Hung Thien pagoda in the capital to set up a ceremony to say goodbye to the crowd. At that time, assistant officials such as Phong Huyen Linh and Do Nhu Hoi all attended. That same day, the Great Master returned to Tri Cu Pagoda, day and night commemorating the West diligently without fail. On October 27, the Great Master suddenly called his attendant and said: "Buddha has come." After a while, he said again: "The two Bodhisattvas also came! I was at the Sutra Contemplation place and accomplished the 12th dharma contemplation. Now the Buddha and Bodhisattva have come to take me back to the Pure Land." Having finished speaking, the Great Master clasped his hands happily and passed away. Life expectancy is 70 years old.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

Buddhist Patriarch Ky

---o0o---

VII - ENHANCEMENT

Master Khac Can, surnamed Truong, from Hunan, was naive from childhood. At the age of twenty, he became a monk at Hong The hermitage in Thien Hoa, then received full ordination in Loc Son. The monk was illiterate, so he studied several recitation sessions for about 5 years before he memorized it. After that, for a full 10 years, the Master traveled all over the five musics, four mountains, and great forestry academies to study, but in the end he did not understand a single thing, and was still as foolish as before.

At the age of 60, he heard Dharma Master Minh Qua preach about the merits of reciting the Buddha's name, precious in "one-pointedness of mind, not disorder". If you are scattered, you should listen attentively to the sound of reciting, then the random thoughts will be eliminated, false thoughts will be eliminated, the mind will be pure, etc. From then on, the Master learned about the method of reciting the Buddha's name, so he dedicated himself to practice.

For six years, the Master's old nature was gone, and his mind was always free and clear. In his free time, the Master often told people: "Practicing is precious because "one mind is not disturbed". My karma is completely eliminated by reciting Buddha's name. In recent years, not only have I not been troubled, but my body and mind have been at peace."

One day, the Master sent someone to invite brother Ham An. The next day, Ham An arrived. As soon as he saw it, the Master smiled and said: "Khac Can, I would like to say goodbye to my brother!". Ham An asked: "Where are you going?". The Master replied: "Go to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss." Ham An said: "Are you talking crazy?". The monk said: "For the past six years, my mind has not been disturbed, reciting Amitabha, speaking clearly, seeing the Pure Land, knowing the date and time of my decision to be reborn. It is not a lie!". The monk immediately entrusted all the work in the hermitage to Ham An, then said: "Tomorrow at noon, I will say goodbye to you brother. Old brothers must take care of each other. You should try to specialize in practicing the Buddha's name to prepare for the Pure Land." That afternoon, the Master sat alone reciting Buddha's name without talking.

The next morning, the monk took a shower, changed his clothes, lit incense to worship the Buddha, and thanked the Patriarchs, he still went into the quiet room to recite Buddha's name. At noon, the monk slowly entered the temple and sat cross-legged, holding a rosary in his hand and silently reciting Buddha's name. It wasn't until two hours later that Ham An saw that he hadn't seen the Master moving for a long time, so he came closer to check and saw that the Master had passed away. Only then did everyone in the scriptures truly believe it, and at the same time, along with the monks Pho Am, etc., they all heard a strange scent. That was the 5th day of the seventh month in the year of Tan Suu, during the reign of King Guangxu of the Qing Dynasty. At that time, the weather was hot and there was a seven-day break, but the body still had no cracks. Those who saw it all praised it as strange and rare.

Excerpted from the volume The Story of Modern Life and Rebirth

---o0o---

VIII - MYTH

Great Master Tri Huyen, surname Tran, surname Hau Giac, from My Chau. When he was seven years old, the Great Master heard the Great Nirvana Sutra preached at Ninh Di Pagoda and immediately understood it as if he had learned it before. That night, the Great Master dreamed of Buddha's hand rubbing his head. At the age of 11, he became a monk. No matter what Sutra collection he studied, the Great Master mastered it all. At the age of 13, the Great Master went to the throne to give lectures, and the monks and laity all admired him.

During the reign of King Hi Tong of the Tang Dynasty, he took the title of Ngo Dat Quoc Tu and bestowed agarwood incense. Not long after, scabs appeared on the Great Master's pillow. His face was so painful that no medicine could cure it. A few years ago, the Great Master devotedly took care of a monk who was seriously ill. When saying goodbye to another place, that monk told the Great Master that if in the future there was any suffering in his body, he should come find him at Cuu Long mountain in the land of Shu. At that time, the Great Master remembered that advice and found Mr. Tang at Cuu Long Mountain. Mr. Tang asked a disciple to lead the Great Master to a creek to wash off the scabies. When he was about to wash, the scabies on his face suddenly spoke up, telling him not to wash and said: "You have read all the historical scriptures, surely you know that Vien Uong killed Trieu Tho during the Han Dynasty? You are Vien Uyong and I am Trieu Tho. I will forever follow you to avenge your hatred. But because you have always been a high-ranking Buddhist monk for ten generations, you cannot harm him. Recently, you have been respected and honored by the king and everyone, so I have been honored. I have the opportunity to torment you. Today, thanks to Venerable Ca Nha Ca, I will not harm you anymore." The great master splashed water to wash the scabies, and the scabies immediately healed.

From that day on, the Great Master admonished himself for thinking about his reputation, wrote Water Repentance to eliminate sin, strictly followed the precepts, and had few desires and contentment. The Great Master considered that in Saha it was difficult to attain patience, so he diligently practiced the path day and night six times to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. One day, suddenly heard a loud voice shouting in the air: "You will definitely be reborn in the Pure Land!". The master immediately asked whose voice it was. The sky replied: "It's Buddha!".

Another day, the Great Master saw a Bodhisattva come down to give detailed advice. At his deathbed, the Master told him to leave his body on the beach to give to birds and fish; The Great Master told everyone: "I have long wanted to return to the Western Pure Land, now is the time to be satisfied!". Having finished speaking, the Great Master turned his face to the West and passed away. Life expectancy is 73 years old.

Excerpted from the series: Story of Song Cao Tang

The Story of God Tang

---o0o---

IX - SELF-AWARENESS

Great Master Tu Giac is from Bac Lang. When he was young, he became a monk at Khai Nguyen Pagoda. Later, the Great Master studied the Law and Law at Thien Phap Pagoda. Diligent for nine years, thoroughly understanding the Tripitaka. The great master went to Trung Lam mountain to practice asceticism, eating only one meager meal of fruits and vegetables every day.

During the year of great drought, the Ambassador Tiet in Hengyang heard about the Great Master's virtue and personally went to the mountain to request the Great Master to pray for rain. The great master sincerely prayed to the Dragon God, and the rain immediately poured down. The Great Master has long wanted to cast a statue of Avalokiteśvara. After the day of praying for rain, donors from all public meeting places came and cast a bronze statue of Avalokiteśvara forty-nine meters high, with a majestic appearance. The following year, the pagoda also lost its form.

The great master then stood in front of the palace and made a vow to soon be reborn in the Pure Land. In the third watch of that night, two lines of golden light appeared. Amitabha Buddha stepped down from the golden light. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva follows on the left, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva follows on the right. The Buddha reached out his golden arm and stroked the Great Master's head and said: "Keep your vows and don't change them. Save others first. With the lotus in the precious pond, you will be reborn!".

In the 11th year of Trinh Nguyen, Tang Dynasty, on the full moon night of the second month, the Angel appeared halfway in the air, bent down and said to the Great Master: "It is almost time for you to return to the Pure Land!". The master raised his hand to thank the god. On June 14, the Great Master sat cross-legged in front of the statue of Avalokiteśvara and passed away. Since the Great Master passed away, that statue of Avalokiteśvara often shows many very inspiring things.

Excerpted from the series of Tong Cao Tang Truyen

Buddhist Patriarch Ky

---o0o---

X - THIEN DIEU

Great Master Thien Dieu from Lam Tuy once went to the Tripitaka to sincerely take out a volume, aiming at the book "Contemplation of Infinite Life Buddha Sutra". From then on, the Great Master concentrated on reciting Buddha's name and practicing the sixteen wonderful contemplations. When he passed through Lo Son and saw the relics of Great Master Hue Vien, his wish became even more fervent. A little while later, the Great Master went into hiding at Chung Nam Mountain to practice the Eightfold Samadhi for several years, feeling the treasures of the forest always appear before him. Then the Great Master went to Tan Duong to study the Infinite Life Sutra from Zen Master Dao Xuoc. Usually when the Great Master enters samadhi for seven days, he emerges. Zen Master Dao Xuoc asked to see his birthplace. The great master said: "The Zen master must repent of three sins in order to be reborn. The Zen master once placed the Buddha statue by the window while he himself was in the middle of the house. This is the first sin, which must be repented against the Buddha. The master often orders people to become monks, this is the second sin, which must be repented against the monks. Also, because building a house harms many insects, this is the third sin, which must be repented against all sentient beings." After hearing this, Zen Master Xuoc carefully examined and remembered his mistakes, then wholeheartedly repented. Not long after, one day coming out of meditation, the Great Master told Zen Master Xuoc: "You have cleared your sins. The next day, when will a white light shine, that is the symptom of rebirth!".

The great master came to the capital to teach and educate, and many people flocked to him. One day, suffering from a mild illness, the Great Master retired to practice the Dharma, then happily recited Buddha's name and passed away. Everyone listened to the heavenly music from the Great Master's room and walked straight to the West.

Excerpted from the series Buddhist Records

---o0o---

XI - DAI Hanh

Dharma Master Dai Hanh from Te Chau, studied Thien Thai teachings and then went to Thai Son mountain, braided grass to cover his body, and picked up fruits to support his stomach. Practicing the Dharma Flower Samadhi, I felt the manifestation of Samantabhadra. One day, he complained to himself: "Human life is impermanent, the time of death is not long. Where will I go?". The shaman went to the front of the Tripitaka to pray. Withdrawing from Amitabha Sutra. Starting that day, the Dharma Master immediately concentrated on reciting Buddha's name. 21 days later, in the middle of the night, suddenly his empty eyes lit up and saw the land of lapis lazuli, and saw Amitabha Buddha and two Bodhisattvas standing in the air. From then on, the Dharma Master's virtues spread more and more every day. King Hi Tong's title was "Ever Diligent Bodhisattva".

The next year, the lapis lazuli realm appeared again. The magician told the crowd: "Today the treasure appeared again. The day has come for me to return to the Pure Land!". And on that day the Dharma Master turned his face to the West, clasped his hands and passed away.

Excerpted from Tong Cao Tang Truyen

Buddhist Patriarch Ky

---o0o---

XII - CHI Thong

Master Chi Thong is from Phung Tuong. When he first became a monk, he met Tripitaka Dharma Master Pha Nhat Ra who taught him Tantra, and followed his teachings. Later, he came to Thien Thai, and after reading the episode "Pure Land Linh Thoai", he made a vow to pray for birth in Ultimate Bliss.

From that day on, he never spit towards the West, never sat with his back facing the West.

One day, he climbed onto the cliff of Chieu Thu, chanted 48 prayers to quickly be born in the Pure Land, and then threw himself down. His body fell into a grove of trees, the leaves were dense and soft so it was okay. He adjusted his clothes and climbed up to the cliff and swore: "Having made a great vow, this life of excess is boring. I hope the Holy Order will come and lead me!". Then he jumped down again, lying on the grass, momentarily regaining consciousness. The monks found him and helped him back to the temple. Not long after, he went to Phap Hoa mountain to practice Pure Land cultivation. Later, one day, he saw the White Crane and the Confucius landing on the flock, and saw the lotus buds blooming in front of him. He said: "The White Crane and the Confucius are the Pure Land. The precious lotus is the place of birth. The time has come!". The great master strictly followed the Buddha's rituals and passed away. At the time of cremation, five-colored auspicious clouds covered the fire, and relics appeared all over the body.

Excerpted from the series of Tong Cao Tang Truyen

Buddhist Patriarch Ky

---o0o---

XIII - DOAN PHU

Master Doan Phu was from Thien Thuy and became a monk under Zen Master Dao Ngo at Sung Phuoc pagoda. After receiving full ordination, the Great Master went to study the Abhidharma Pitaka everywhere, and also studied both the Sutras and the Vinaya. One night, the Great Master dreamed that the Holy Monk gave him a glass vase filled with sacred relics to swallow. The Great Master obediently swallowed all the relics, and the Holy Monk said: "The Tripitaka of the Great Teaching is contained in your stomach!". From then on, the Great Master had unhindered eloquence. When preaching the Sutra in Thai Nguyen, the audience gathered like a market. All three kings of the Tang Dynasty: Duc Tong, Thuan Tong and Hien Tong respected him as a master. Before and after, the Great Master preached the Nirvana Sutra and the Only-Consciousness Commentary in more than one hundred and sixty conferences. Every day, in his free time, the Great Master recites the Mahayana Sutra to pray for birth in the Pure Land. Having received a lot of alms, including more than tens of millions of taels of silver, the Great Master transferred all the donations to public works to repair pagodas and towers, but he was still satisfied with a simple small room and a low, narrow bed.

In the first year of Khai Thanh, on the first day of the sixth month, the Great Master turned his face to the west, lay down on his right hand and passed away. At that moment, the scent was fragrant both near and far. After cremation, more than three hundred relics were obtained.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

---o0o---

XIV - HUNG TUAN

Hung Tuan Dharma Master Chau, from Chengdu, is good at preaching, but not virtuous. The magician once stopped practicing and became a soldier, then became a monk again. Self-examination knows his mistakes, so the Dharma Master often chants Amitabha Buddha to eliminate his sins and be reborn.

In the Great Lich year of the Tang Dynasty, one day he suddenly fell down and died. He was arrested and brought to the King of Hell. The King told him he was guilty of breaking the precepts, etc., and then ordered the devil to take him to hell. The magician immediately cried out: "In the Quan Sutra, it is said: "A person who commits all evil deeds and endures the five transgressions, at the time of his death, recites the Buddha's name for ten recitations, each recitation destroys countless sins, and is immediately reborn." Even though this Hung Tuan has committed a sin, he has not committed the five transgressions, yet he has repented and recited the Buddha's name countless times. Even if I were to fall into hell, I would not have any regrets, but could it be that the Buddha's words are a lie!"

The King of Hell told him to go home, so the Dharma Master was resurrected and went to live in Tay Son, day and night dedicated to reciting Buddha's name.

Four years later, one day the Dharma Master gathered the assembly to say goodbye and said: "Please tell my friends in the city that Hung Tuan was able to be reborn because he concentrated on reciting Buddha's name, and was not a sinner who fell through the net." Having finished his instructions, the Dharma Master happily sat down and passed away.

Excerpted from the series Tuc Cao Tang Truyen

Buddhist Patriarch Ky

---o0o---

XV - DUY Cung

Monk Duy Cung, from Kinh Chau, was a monk but loved alcohol, meat and gambling. In his free time, he recites Buddha's sutras to pray for rebirth in Ultimate Bliss. Monk Linh Quy, a monk living in the same temple, and Monk Duy Cung were comrades in good conduct, so a neighbor gave the two Monks a verse to admonish them: "Linh Quy breaks the precepts, Duy Cung follows in your footsteps. There are thousands of hells, don't be afraid to push your head in." Monk Duy Cung said: "I am truly guilty. But if I hope to be reborn through the power of the Buddha ten times, I will probably fall into the evil realms!"

One day, Monk Duy Cung was sick. Monk Linh Quy had to go on official business. Along the way, he met two young men with good looks holding musical instruments. Monk Linh Quy asked where he was going. The two replied that they were coming from the West to process the Palace of Thuong Nhon. One person reached into the bag and pulled out a fist-sized lotus bud, the petals radiated a strangely beautiful light, then the two of them walked straight towards the temple. The next day, Monk Linh Quy returned to the new temple and found out that Monk Duy Cung had passed away at the time he met the two young men yesterday. From then on, Monk Linh Quy repented of his strict moral conduct, and soon became famous as a truly virtuous monk.

Excerpted from the series Buddhist Records

---o0o---

tom_tat: Ho Thuong Lao Ni strictly followed the precepts, reciting Buddha's name and chanting sutras every day very sincerely. There was a Taoist who visited the hermitage once a year. When he came, he and the Elder Ni discussed virtue and practice all day long before leaving.
noi_dung:
B 3 - MONKS

I - LAO NI

Ho Thuong Lao Ni strictly followed the precepts, reciting Buddha's name and chanting sutras every day very sincerely. There was a Taoist person who visited the hermitage once a year. When he arrived, he and Elder Ni discussed morality and practice all day before leaving.

One day, Lao Ni made an appointment with Dao Nhan. On the appointed day, waiting for the Taoist to not come, Lao Ni said: "I'm about to return to the Pure Land and want to say goodbye to that friend." Waited a few more days, but the Taoist still did not come. Old Ni told the person to carry the built-in tray and place it on the broken bridge near the hut. The old nun held a small stick of incense in her hand, leisurely sat inside and chanted Buddha's name. In a moment, fire suddenly burned in Lao Ni's body. People came to watch in large numbers like at a fair. Until my whole body was burned black, Lao Ni's chanting of Buddha's name still did not stop.

Excerpted from the volume "Sound Quality Literature Notes" by Ha Si Vien

---o0o---

II - TOAT KHAM

Nun Toai Kham, from Wuxi, became a monk when she was nine years old. When she was an adult, she met a nun who encouraged her to recite the Buddha's name, and she immediately developed a diligent mind to recite Buddha's name. A little while later, she became the abbot of the Bach Y monastery in Suzhou, and practiced reciting Buddha's name even more diligently until she was 50 years old before she received full ordination.

In March of the year she was 55 years old, one night, just as the rooster crowed for the first round, she called her disciples to come and said: "I'm about to return to Buddha!". The disciples all cried and said: "You are not sick, why would you say such a thing?". She said: "Why are you so stupid? There's no use crying. You should be diligent in reciting Buddha's name!" Then she sat cross-legged facing West with her disciples chanting Buddha's name in unison. When an incense stick withered, she became lonely. It was the 53rd year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from Western Kung Fu Practice

---o0o---

III - LAW TON

Nun Luat Ton is from Gia Dinh. When she was three years old, her mother passed away. Her grandmother took her to Vien Thong Temple to worship Buddha. She decided to stay there. As a child, she liked to worship Buddha. Growing up, I specialized in reciting the Lotus Sutra but suffered from not being able to understand the meaning. She then went to Kim Son and Sung Phuoc to seek help for several years. After returning to Vien Thong hermitage, she concentrated on reciting Buddha's name. Every year she often goes to the temple to worship Buddha and Sangha.

At the age of 53, suffering from a cough, she was confined to practice, taking rebirth as a promise.

On the full moon day of January, when she was 64 years old, she gathered the crowd to recite the Buddha's name in unison. When the sun was shining, she looked at them earnestly and advised them to practice courageously, then she clasped her hands three times and chanted "Namo Western Pure Land, Great Compassion Amitabha Buddha". After the performance, she sat respectfully and passed away. At that time, the fragrance of lotus filled the whole temple. It was the 55th year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from Western Kung Fu Practice

---o0o---

IV - BUDDHISM AND LIANHONG

Buddhist nun Buddha Ky, from Changzhou. Since childhood, she refused to get married. When she grew up, her mother took her to Vu Hoa hermitage to have her hair shaved, and then received full ordination. Later, she became the abbot of Sung Phat Temple in the city. She raised money to build an 8 meter tall statue of the Western Three Saints made of sandalwood. Every year, she invites pure virtuous Monks and Monks to come to the seven-period retreat to hold a meeting to recite Buddha's name. She often goes to temples to worship Buddha and monks. She bought 30 acres of field to make a permanent base for Thien Ninh Pagoda in Changzhou. Later, she was confined to a hermitage dedicated to cultivating pure karma.

Three days before passing away, she saw Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appear with two disciples accompanying her. Meanwhile, some people say they smell like chrysanthemums. She said it was the scent of blue lotus flowers. On August 30, the 56th year of Qianlong's reign, Upasaya came to visit. She told her to help her sit up, then gathered a group of nuns to recite Buddha's name for about two thousand sentences in solitude.

Excerpted from Western Kung Fu Practice

Watching Buddha Ky's mindfulness of rebirth. Nun Lien Huong was diligent in reciting Buddha's name. When she was 30 years old, even though she was sick, her strength to recite Buddha's name was even stronger. One day, she turned her face to the West, sat down, clasped her hands and recited Buddha's name, and passed away. It was the 13th year of Gia Khanh.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

---o0o---

V - ROMANTICITY

Nun Lang Nhien, from Gia Thien, when she was 18 years old, she saw the suffering of her sister-in-law who had a miscarriage, she vowed not to get married, then she asked her parents to be allowed to become a monk at Tinh Tri hermitage. After receiving the precepts, she dedicated herself to practicing Pure Land. Diligently reciting Buddha's name for many years, her recitation power continued, whether she was free or busy, her chanting of Buddha's thoughts was uninterrupted.

In the 13th year of Gia Khanh, she told her disciple, Nun Phuoc Duyen: "In the last three months, I have dreamed three times that I was sitting cross-legged in a lotus flower at the maintenance site. I am about to be reborn! You must dedicate yourself to reciting Buddha's name. Truth is natural and fruit is sure, your efforts will not be in vain. Try to remember and not forget!". On March 25, she was not sick, sat upright and passed away, at the age of 71.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

---o0o---

noi_dung:
C 3 - TRUSTEES

I - CROWN

Mr. Vuong Co, from Man Trung, from Dong Do, is the great-grandson of General Vuong Van Dan. Mr. Co's family has maintained the precept of not killing for seven generations. Mr. Co again made the intention to release up to one hundred thousand lives. He went to Jiangxi to study Zen with Hoi Duong and Vuong Ky, two great Zen masters. After returning, he authored the collection "Pure Land Decision Nghi Tap" to propagate the Pure Land dharma. In my free time, I never let go of the string. V - TRAN QUANYEN

Mr. Tran Quyen is from Vinh Trung, from Nam Kiem Chau. During the reign of King Huy Tong of the Song Dynasty, he held the position of Ta Tu Gian, but because of his harsh words, he had to be appointed as an official in a foreign province.

Mr. Quyen was originally fond of the Avatamsaka Sutra and called himself Hoa Nghiem Layman. When he met Dharma Master Minh Tri, he asked about Thien Thai's sect. Minh Tri Dharma Master used the subject to contemplate regardless of the situation, using the nature to cultivate non-action and explain it to him. Mr. Quyen immediately went in. From then on, he completely abandoned literature and dedicated himself to practicing Buddhist Samadhi. He once wrote the title of the Pure Land Ten Nghi Treatises of Great Master Tri Jia:

"The human mind is impermanent, the dharma is also indeterminate. There are countless differences between the mind and the dharma precisely because of this. Believing here is believing all over, so Hoa Nghiem says the Ten Faiths. Having doubts here is doubting all. Patriarch Tri Gia preached the Ten Doubts for that reason. Out of the net of doubt and into the place of complete faith, one will not leave this place and immediately attain salvation. The Pure Land is the place of salvation. There is the current Patriarch preaching the Dharma with the name of Infinite Life Buddha. That Buddha preached the Dharma without ever interrupting. Because of doubts, one can attain salvation. Because we are deaf to our ears, we don't listen. Because we doubt our mind, we are confused and unaware. Because we don't hear, we cling to impure habits, and then we believe that the lotus is a lie, but we don't even consider where our present body and blood come from?

All from hell. There is nothing real about that filthy prison! Because of relying on karma, from the true nature, in an illusory state but clinging to this and that, forever infatuated, the Holy Path is completely lost. Therefore, the Buddha Shakyamuni Tathagata, with a compassionate heart, stood in the middle of the filthy world and loudly called out: Praise the purity and joy of the Pure Land. He is the great Teacher at the shore of life and death who uses a dharma boat to transport sentient beings to the shore of the Pure Land. But Amitabha Buddha's pure shore does not make any distinctions, the true Dharma boat of Master Shakyamuni will never pass again. For example, an eight-sided lantern, a lamp that shines in eight directions, a mirror with East and West, but the light is still the same. Buddha Amitabha preached the Dharma which was everywhere in the light. Because he wanted to have a special place, Buddha Sakyamuni pointed to the West side. Therefore, only those who have reached the shore of the Pure Land can put an end to suffering. Those who have not yet entered the Dharma world cannot forget East and West! Regarding this method, if you have not yet reached the ultimate goal, you should not be attached to it, do not analyze this and that, just be mindful and confident. This is the profound intention of the two Popes, but also the firm belief of Patriarch Tri Gia. Faith is the mother of all good dharmas, but doubt is the root of countless evil karma. If one can follow the faith and dig out the roots of doubt, then people with heavy karma in the past will be able to hear, those who are deaf will be able to hear, those who are deluded will be enlightened and will know that they will be freed from birth and death, and will be reborn without being born in the Pure Land. Following the words of the Master, he came to meet the Father and then, according to the Father's wish, returned to assist the Master without leaving the Pure Land but in all ten directions, sitting safely on the lotus platform and dividing the Dharma Realm. From the time the two Popes established the law until now, there are as many people as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, who still refuse to believe, and who still doubt. I believed so I found a way to guide everyone to believe, this is Patriarch Tri Gia's compassion."

Later, he built a house in Lo Son. One day he told his family: "Last year, I had many hardships, I was only afraid of death interrupting my religious practice. Now I have escaped the cycle of life and death." Having finished speaking, Mr. Quyen passed away happily at the age of 65.

At that time, the Venerable Tuong Phong was in retreat at Van Tinh Cac (Suzhou), practicing the Samadhi of Buddha's name. One night in the winter of that year, he dreamed of three tall and majestic people with round halos on their heads, walking straight into the room and sitting upright, facing the South. Mr. Tuong Phong finished the ceremony and asked: "Where are the three Venerables coming to the temple?". The person sitting in the middle replied: "We are from the West!". He asked: "Are you from the Pure Land of Buddha Amitabha?". Answer: "That's right!". He said: "Dare to ask Venerable sirs, what is your noble name?". The three people asked in unison: "What is your name?". Mr. Tuong Phong said: "The Dharma disciple's name is Dat Van." The person sitting in the middle said: "You are lying." He replied: "My disciple is telling the truth, not lying." The person sitting in the middle asked: "What is your name?". He said: "The Dharma disciple's name is Dat Van." The person sitting in the middle said: "False words again." He replied: "It's not that the disciple lied, why do you think the disciple is lying?". The person sitting in the middle said: "All living beings consider falsehood to be true, and falsehood to be true, so they must be reincarnated into birth and death. If you are a wise person who clearly understands that falsehood is false, you will not be born and die. You must not be confused and forget your true mind. You must know that true mind is not mind, true knowledge is not knowledge. Perception is a demon. In Buddha, there is no perception. You must believe and not doubt!" As soon as he heard it, Mr. Tuong Phong immediately became enlightened, his mind was clear, and he understood his true heart. He then said: "The Venerable's teachings are the inconceivable Buddha Dharma. I dare to say, Venerable Sir, you have come here from the Land of Ultimate Bliss. I wonder if you have ever seen Amitabha Buddha." The person sitting on the left said: "You must see Buddha for yourself." The three people stood up together. Each person patted Mr. Tuong Phong's head and recited verses:

First person:

Must try diligently

Cultivate pure karma

The cause is sure to be true

Don't harbor doubts.

Second person:

Dharmas arise from the mind

Dharmas from the mind cease

Mind and dharma are inherently empty

It is impossible to grasp and let go.

Third person:

Buddha is born, mind and dharma are the same

Like a scene in a dream

Like an illusory samadhi

He understood a bit!

As soon as the three people finished speaking the verse, at first glance they saw Mr. Ma Vinh To solemnly bowing to the three of them. The three immediately shot up into the sky and flew towards the West. At the same time, listen to melodious music and the sound of Buddha's name throughout the sky.

Mr. Ma Vinh To turned to Mr. Tuong Phong, bowed his head three times and said: "Thank you for advising me to take refuge in the Three Jewels and specialize in cultivating pure karma. Now I have been born in the Pure Land to enjoy great peace and happiness, so I invite three Great Monks to come here and demonstrate the wonderful dharma to repay you." Having finished speaking, Mr. Ma Vinh To bowed to him three more times, then clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name and flew towards the West. Just as the late night bell rang, he suddenly woke up. At dawn, Venerable Tuong Phong wrote down the events he had heard last night into the poem "Mong Ky".

Later, Mr. Tuong Phong retreated to Phuoc Thanh Pagoda in Lu Giang. When he was about to die, he knew the date and time, sat down reciting Buddha's name, and passed away.

Excerpted from the series Nhut Hanh Cu Tap

XIV - SIXTH STICKER THUYEN

Mr. Luc Si Thuyen from To Chau, attending the Luong Hoang Sam ceremony to pray for his friend's recovery, he developed his mind to practice Buddhism. He went to Thien Ninh to receive the Bodhisattva precepts. Just met the time when Tich Can Bodhisattva from Ultimate Bliss came to the Jade Altar to teach the method of reciting Buddha's name, advising people to think about the cycle of birth and death and recite Buddha's name single-mindedly to seek rebirth in the Pure Land world. Bodhisattva preached the Dharma in 11 conferences. Therefore, those attending the festival have just begun to know how to dedicate themselves to the Pure Land. Mr. Si Thuyen also focused on visualizing and reciting the Samantabhadra Sutra. He lived for two years, then fell ill and had poor appetite, so he took the precept of eating meat (that is, eating salty food). The illness got worse and worse, knowing that he was about to die, he was very remorseful and ashamed, so he stopped eating fish and meat, constantly chanting Amitabha Buddha's name. He told his daughter to fast and recite Buddha's name, and not to cry and mourn when he passed away. Seven days later, the disease flared up. His eyes looked up into the air as if he saw something, and his mouth said: "White lotus! White crane! Good people!" He kept saying: "Buddha! Buddha! Buddha!". He turned over and lay on his right side. Suddenly there was a strange scent that filled the whole house. It was May 18, the 52nd year of Qianlong, and he was 39 years old.

The next year, on the first day of May, Mr. Si Thuyen descended to Ngoc Dan and told everyone: "The day before, I was about to fall. Thanks to my strong mindfulness at the time of death, I was fortunate enough to be accepted by the Buddha to lead me to rebirth in the West.

All people in life have a very urgent task, no one can avoid it, but most often forget it, do you understand?

Right now, your body is healthy and your spirit is strong, so who would have thought that tomorrow you will have to lie in bed sick, your soul separated, unable to distinguish between East and West, unable to distinguish between North and South. The eyes are dim, there is no way to hold on, then one must follow karma and cycle, suffering countless amounts of suffering. Only in those who, at the time of peace, devote themselves to Pure Land cultivation, at the moment of death, they see the Buddha coming to take rebirth in the precious lotus flower, have an immeasurable life span, enjoy pure joys, attain the level of non-regression, and continuously practice straight to Buddhahood. If you are willing to establish your resolve here, I will discuss with you the essential views of the Pure Land discipline. That is, I want to talk about "Faith", "Happy" and "Vows".

One is Trust. I firmly believe that the West has Pure Land, just like the West of this city has a mansion park. The Saha world here is in the East, like the eastern hamlet of this city. Saha is real, Ultimate Bliss is also real. Being in the same state of enlightenment, we should concentrate on remembering when we can return. Just like the field in the city, if you take a step from the eastern hamlet, you will reach the western park. Once you are confident in the Pure Land's decision, you can return home, and you must also be confident in the Buddha's recitation method, like believing in the matters of wearing clothes and eating meals. Wear clothes to avoid cold, eat rice to avoid hunger, recite Buddha's name to avoid birth and death. Believe today and don't believe tomorrow, not really believe. Even if there is even a moment of doubt in a lifetime, it is not really true belief. Starting from today until your last breath, always believing without a shadow of a doubt is true belief.

The second is Virtue. We firmly believe that there is a Western Pure Land, we firmly believe in the method of reciting the Buddha's name, but if we keep talking about empty praise, then what is the benefit of achieving rebirth and liberation? Therefore, if you believe today, the teachings will be followed today. Believe tomorrow, practice tomorrow. It is very undesirable to say: I am still young now, it is not too late to wait until I am older to practice. Take a look at the burial plots, how many graves of green-headed people are there! How many graves whose lives are short! Where can we be sure that we will have a long life? Nor should I say: I am now busy taking care of the country, the house, my parents, my wife and children. It is not too late to wait until I have free time to focus on religious practice. You should know that impermanence is quick, one day the angel of death will put a sickle in your neck, you can't tell him to wait until I'm free from work and then he will come! There are also people who practice vigorously at times, but are lazy at times. You must know that nourishing the fetus requires constant effort. Like a chicken incubating eggs, it is always necessary to continue to be warm before they can hatch their chicks. If you incubate today and throw them away tomorrow, the eggs will definitely rot.

Third is Prayer. A very urgent prayer. In life, there are not many people who believe in Buddha and recite Buddha's name, but most of them either pray for wealth and longevity in this life, or pray for blessings in the next life, and pray for a temporary relief from suffering in heaven and human bodies. Those are all wishes contrary to Buddha's will. The Buddha tried his best to tell people to quickly get out of birth and death, but people wanted to go deep into samsara. The Buddha carefully advised people to seek rebirth in Ultimate Bliss, but people wanted to stay forever in Saha. Thus, during one lifetime of practicing the religion, the effort is completely devoted to the flow. For example, like plowing a field and sowing grass seeds, the hard work is sometimes there but the fruit is completely empty. Therefore, if you are a person who has true faith, you must immediately practice true conduct. Having practiced true conduct, one must always develop true vows. Having finished this life of excess, he decides not to be born in heaven or in the human world, but only decides to be reborn in the Pure Land. Making a true vow like that and reciting Buddha's name is in accordance with the Buddha's teachings. It's not like it's a waste of time or effort. You should try to get it! You should be diligent!

Four years later, Mr. Si Thuyen descended again at Mr. Huynh Kinh Phu's house to promote his friends, his words were very important.

Excerpted from the series Nhut Hanh Cu Tap

XV - Ngo Nghieu Chuc

Mr. Nghieu Chuc in Suzhou works as a candle maker. Single, long-term, chanting Buddha's name day and night, living honestly. Because he had those good points, candle factories competed to hire him. While working, each time he poured a ladle of oil into the mold, he recited Buddha's name five or three times.

When he was 71 years old, one day he told the factory owner: "I have saved some money, intending to take care of my old age. Now I have succeeded in reciting Buddha's name. In a few days I will be reborn in the Pure Land. I don't need that money. I respectfully give it to you." The factory owner promised to do good deeds on his behalf. He was so happy that he led the factory owner to the place where the money was kept and counted one thousand taels of silver. The factory owner immediately divided them up and brought them to temples for monks.

On the appointed day, he sat down, clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name, and passed away peacefully. He had his last words so he used the coffin to shroud him. On the day of the cremation ceremony, there were over ten thousand people who came to take him away. At that time, it was the seventh year of Chong Trinh, Ming Dynasty.

Excerpted from the series Hien Qua Depend Luc

noi_dung:
D 3 - FEMALE TRUSTEES

I - CHUC THI

Congratulations to the aunt of the three Vien Hoang Dao brothers. Nhon often listened to her three grandchildren discuss Buddhism, so Thi devoted herself to reciting Buddha's name and chanting the Diamond Sutra.

One day, Thi told her family: "Amitabha Buddha taught, after three days he will come to pick me up!". When it was time, Thi took a shower and sat upright in the middle of the house. Relatives sat around Thi to watch. Moments later Thi Tu said: "Buddha has arrived! In the middle of his journey, he released a white light about two meters long." She said again: "I saw a tall and dignified monk. He called himself Tu Bo De and then transformed into one hundred or twenty monks." Among relatives, someone spoke up and said: "In the Diamond Sutra, there are 138 Subhuti in all, is that it?". Everyone lit incense and recited Buddha's name in unison. Chuc Thi clasped her hands and smiled and passed away. At that moment, a 9-year-old servant was dozing off when he suddenly screamed loudly and covered his face in tears. Asked for a reason, he said: "Just now I saw two tall people wearing golden armor, holding long poles in their hands, leading the way for the mistress. The stroke of the pole on my face hurt so much!". Everyone looked and saw that there was a bruise on his forehead. During the shroud, the place where Thi's body emitted a strange fragrance.

Excerpted from Vien Trung Lang Volume

---o0o---

II - PHAN THI

Phan Thi Quang Dam, wife of Minister of Justice Ly Duong Xuan in Du Ha. Duong Xuan is a good person, loves to give alms, and recites Amitabha Buddha every day. One year after his death, he appeared to Phan Thi and then went straight upstairs, opened the window and called out: "You must practice! You must practice!".

Phan Thi was knowledgeable in Confucianism, at first she often refuted Buddhism, but then she respected Master Van The Lien Tri, became a vegetarian, and practiced meditation. At night, Thi often sits cross-legged until morning, diligently reciting Buddha's name and doing charity work. When lending money to people, Thi neither took interest nor asked for it.

In the winter of the 39th year of Van Lich, Thi fell ill. By January of next year, Thi Tu knew that he could not be strong, so he willed his inheritance and told his family: "I, three generations ago, was Pham Sangha. Now I follow Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to the West." Then Thi immediately recited Buddha's name without stopping, curled up three fingers and passed away. By the time he was shrouded, his whole body was soft and gentle, his face was as bright as when he was alive.

Excerpted from Ngu Duc Vien Tap

---o0o---

III - WOMEN

Ngo Nu, from Thai Thuong. When she gave birth, she sat cross-legged and came out. Growing up, she respected the Three Jewels and lived with her filial parents. She refused to get married, no one advised her to do so, she immediately swore by heaven. At first she learned the words from her brothers and sisters, and later she read and recited the Buddhist scriptures and understood the general meaning. Early in the evening she respectfully bowed to Buddha. She dreamed that the divine teacher gave him the Chuan De mantra in Sanskrit. If anyone has colds, she writes a spell to cure them. One day she learned about her past life. She said: "In my previous life, I was a Cao Tang in the Song Dynasty. In this life, I was born as a daughter of the Ngo family. My purpose is to guide my parents in practicing. By the age of 23, I will attain enlightenment."

In Sung Trinh's 4th year, at the age of 23, she went into retreat and focused on reciting Buddha's name. At the end of that winter, she fell ill. She wrote verses from then on and earnestly advised her parents to practice diligently and not to be lazy. At noon, she lay on her right side and passed away. When she was about to wrap the red light on her face. Her mother fixed her hair, and the strange scent from the top of her head drifted out the door all night without dissipating. The corpse was buried for 4 years, then the cremation ceremony was performed, the bones were as clear as jade, the top of the head turned a golden color. Her parents built a tower to worship.

Excerpted from Tuc Vanh Sanh Tap

---o0o---

IV - LU THI

Lu Thi Tri Phuoc, wife of Trinh Quy Thanh in Huy Chau. Quy Thanh was originally a Buddhist who was well-versed in the teachings and enthusiastic about good deeds. Lu Thi always helps her husband. She is a vegetarian and recites Buddha's name thousands of times every day. She has a gentle nature, loves her subordinates and never scolds her servants.

In the 5th year of Sung Trinh, when she was seriously ill, Thi asked Dharma Master Co Duc to impart the five precepts, and asked about the principles of the Pure Land. After being explained by the Dharma Master, Thi Nhut single-mindedly prayed to the Pure Land world. Mr. Quy Thanh placed an incense burner in the hospital room and recited the Avatamsaka Sutra. In the chapter "Entering the Dharma Realm", he explained 53 passages of Thien Tai's knowledge to Thi. Wherever she heard it, she understood its meaning. After reciting the Sutra, Mr. Quy Thanh urged again: "Hundreds of lifetimes and thousands of lifetimes are in this one moment. Try your best to return to the Pure Land, don't hesitate!". She then loudly recited Buddha's name all day and night for up to half a month. Her biological mother and daughter came to visit. She apologized and asked to leave, saying: "Please don't bother me!".

On the 8th day of the 11th month, at first sight a lotus flower appeared in front of her, in the air she transformed into a Buddha and raised her hand. She was very happy and hurriedly bathed, clasped her hands and turned her face to the West, recited Buddha's name continuously, then lay on her right side and passed away, at the age of 39. At that time, it was noon. In the afternoon, when I touched the top of Thi's head, the heat was enough to warm my hands.

Great Master Nguu Ich wrote down Thi's story of rebirth, and praised her as a heroic person among Pure Land Buddhist nuns.

Being seriously ill and reciting Buddha's name loudly day and night for half a month is "great diligence". A mother and child come to visit and not pay attention to "ending their love affair". The lotus flower and the Buddha appear, walking on the wall and reciting the Buddha's name means "determining to be reborn".

Excerpted from the series Linh Phong Tong Luan

---o0o---

V - TU THI

Luc Sinh's wife lived in Gia Dinh, her husband died, Thi specialized in cultivating pure karma. She burned all of the debt papers, some amounting to thousands of taels of silver, without asking for anything. She used all her personal belongings to do good deeds.

Early in the evening, he worshiped Buddha, chanted Buddha's name, and chanted Sutras for ten years without missing a single day.

One night, Thi called her family to come and said: "See that light from the West? It's time for me to be reborn!". She clasped her hands together and loudly chanted Buddha's name and passed away.

Giving away money and personal belongings is "leaving worldly contamination". Helping people and giving alms is "kindness". Ten years of practice without missing a single day is "diligence". Oh ! Pure Land practitioners who have the above three things can be called rare, but they are also advantages that will ensure their rebirth.

Excerpted from Vang Sanh Tap

---o0o---

VI - TWO LADIES PULLING THREAD

Mrs. Phi, the wife of Tram Xuan Giao in Ho Chau, was widowed when she was young. She raised her children by herself as a thread-spinner. She is a vegetarian. The church has a three-world Buddha statue with the body of Avalokiteśvara made of sandalwood. Every day, Phi recites one volume of the Diamond Sutra and recites the Buddha's name a thousand sentences as a meditation. Even when busy with work or sick, Phi is never late.

In the 11th year of Sung Trinh, the epidemic raged, Mr. Truong The Mau, her son-in-law, took her into his home. She only brought with her Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara's bones. She lived on a separate floor, every day chanting dedications, she prayed that the incense smoke would reach the Buddha of the three worlds, for three years like that. One day, suddenly, incense smoke swirled around her floor both day and night, then on the white lime wall emerged a solemn and beautiful statue of the Buddha of the three worlds. Word spread from far and near that more and more people came to worship every day. Some people took clean chalk and rubbed it, and the phenomenon became clearer and the color became brighter and brighter.

Four years later, she asked her son-in-law to take her back to her old house. She sprinkled, burned incense and worshiped Buddha, chanting sutras. On the morning of the third day, she showered, changed her clothes, then sat upright and chanted Buddha's name. At noon, she suddenly called out: "Buddha has arrived! Goodbye everyone!". Having finished speaking, she recited Buddha's name for a few hours and passed away. Life expectancy is 73 years old.

Excerpted from Chau Ngu Thua Thuc Tap

Mrs. Tran, from Thuong Thuc, worked as a fabric threader. She believed in Buddhism and recited Buddha's name to the sound of a cart all day long, without stopping for thirty years. One day, she called her son back and said: "Don't you see that phan phan! I'm here to be reborn!". Having finished speaking, she clapped her hands and laughed loudly. After she finished mixing water to bathe and wash herself, she clasped her hands together and passed away. At that time, it was the 10th year of Thuan Tri.

Thuong Tho Mr. Thuc Nguon was still indifferent at that time. When he heard the news, he personally came to see her. He still saw her sitting upright and steady, with a strange, sweet scent throughout the house. Later, when he composed the book "Pure Land Uoc Thuyet", Thuong Tho wrote it down as evidence.

Excerpted from the series Pure Land Testament

---o0o---

VII - LY THI

Ly Thi, mother of Mr. Luu Dao Long. At the age of 40, Thi became a vegetarian and recited Buddha's name. She cleaned a clean house to worship Avalokiteshvara morning and evening. Every time, she recites the Buddha's name a thousand sentences, whether in times of great cold or great hardship, there is no shortage of them. She engraved a copy of the Diamond Sutra for publication.

Every time her birthday comes, she instructs her daughter-in-law not to have a party, but to only celebrate together for one day or three days.

Twenty-five years later, she invited monks to her house to recite the Sutras for seven days and nights. She dreamed that Avalokiteśvara gave her a rosary and said: "Give me this rosary. The number of beads is the time limit for your rebirth!". Thi then took the rosary and counted fifty-three beads.

The following year, on the third day of the May month, Thi called her family members and said: "Today I am returning to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, so together chanting the Buddha's name will help me to be reborn." The daughters-in-law sat beside Thi's bed and recited Buddha's name. Thi sat upright on the bed, facing west, and passed away.

Excerpted from the volume Vajra Tri Nghiem Ky

---o0o---

VIII - THE THREE LADIES SHOW STRANGE THINGS

Truong Thi, a widow in Thuong Thuc, lives a poor life, specializes in reciting the Buddha's name, regardless of place or time, her recitation of Buddha's name is unfailing.

One day, Thi suffered from diarrhea and died, leaving behind a pair of old, tattered, smelly pants. People threw those pants into the river. Suddenly, from those dirty pants, many lotus flowers emerged in five bright colors, floating and filling the entire river surface. Seeing that strange thing, everyone clasped their hands in respect, then picked up the torn pants, washed them, and brought them to the village hut to make table pants on the Buddha's table. At that time, it was the year of Shunzhi of the Qing Dynasty.

Excerpt from Retribution Van Kien Luc

Luc Thi is from Thuong Thuc. She was widowed at the age of 20. She became a vegetarian and kept the precepts of reciting Buddha's name. Polite, Thi never argues with anyone. Thi died at the age of 67. When Thi's clothes were burned, the fire was extinguished, suddenly a yellow light shone, and more than twenty Buddha statues appeared in the ashes. The whole village rushed to see it, and they all burned incense and worshiped together. It was the third year of Kangxi.

Excerpt from Retribution Van Kien Luc

Tu Thai Nghi, Tu Hao Hien's mother, lived in Tien Duong. She worships Buddha very respectfully, chanting Amitabha Buddha every day. She painted a Buddha statue, around the statue dotted several thousand circles to record the number of recitations. Every time she finishes reciting a painting, she folds it up and puts it in a yellow cloth bag.

In the 34th year of Kangxi, she passed away. On the day she passed away, her family members burned the yellow cloth bag in a pot. Suddenly, they heard an explosion in the pot, everyone gathered to watch, and saw a five-colored light shining up, spreading to brown. On that brown color, there is a temple surrounded by railings. In the temple, there are dozens of lotus flowers. On each lotus, there is a Buddha sitting cross-legged with his hands clasped. On both sides of the Buddha, there are gods standing there. Each image is like a white chalk painting. Anyone who saw it also said it was a strange thing in life. The next day, when he picked up the ash, he turned it over to the bottom of the bag to look at it, and the bottom side showed the same image as the top side. Only behind each Buddha statue, there is an old woman holding a dustpan and standing there waiting.

Excerpted from the episode Concentration

---o0o---

IX - DUONG THI

Duong Thi is from Ngu Son. Because my mother's side of the family had always studied Buddhism, she respected the Dharma from a young age. After becoming the Truong family's daughter-in-law, Thi immediately bowed to Master Duc Chon, took the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, and then cut off lust.

At the age of 27, seriously ill, Thi made a vow to pray for rebirth in the Western Pure Land, invited Amitabha Buddha's statue to worship, and chanted Buddha's name loudly day and night. On the fifth day, the scent of sandalwood filled the whole house. On the seventh day, she saw Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and said: "The lotus seed has received half of the work, the remaining half is waiting to see your tricks!". She clasped her hands and asked: "What should I do?". Bodhisattva said: "Let go and go." She immediately got up, sat cross-legged, clasped her hands, recited Buddha's name, and was reborn.

Excerpted from the episode Tuc Vanh Sanh

---o0o---

X - GIANG THI

Giang Thi, Mr. Nghiem Nhuan's successor in Du Hang. Mr. Nghiem was originally a disciple of Van The, practicing the Pure Land Dharma.

Since returning to Nghiem's ​​family, Giang Thi has practiced religiously very enthusiastically. Late at night, as soon as the cock crowed for the first round, Thi got up, knelt in front of the Buddha's table, recited Buddha's name a thousand sentences, and then recited sutras and mantras. Even though she was a noble family, she did all the work of lighting lamps and incense, down to washing water, drinking water, etc. She did it herself, never ordering servants.

In the 7th year of Khang Hi, on the 6th of the third month, after finishing the early morning class, Thi felt tired and lay down temporarily. A moment later, Thi suddenly said loudly: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has arrived!". She poured water, finished bathing, got into bed, lay on her right side, and passed away. At the time of shrouding, Thi's body was still bright and her hands and feet were soft.

Excerpted from the series Pure Land Complete Poetry

---o0o---

XI - MOTHER AND CHILD RETURN TO BUDDHA'S REALM

Ms. Dip was a vegetarian for 40 years and took refuge with the Venerable Co Dam. Every day she bowed to the Hoa Nghiem Sutra, one word at a time, and completed three sets. At the age of 81, she saw the Saint appearing in a golden-colored body, immediately recited Buddha's name and passed away.

Mrs. Diep's daughter is Lang Thi, wife of Mr. Tran Dinh Bieu in Ngo District. At the age of 40, she also took refuge with the Venerable Co Dam, day and night six times Thi Thi performed the Great Compassion Repentance. Bowing to the Avatamsaka Sutra is covered with two sets. In her old age, Thi specialized in reciting the Great Compassion Mantra and Buddha's name to pray for rebirth in Ultimate Bliss. One day, Thi was slightly ill and saw Avalokiteshvara incarnate. She called her daughter over and said: "Buddha's light illuminates the whole house. Mom, go to the West!" Having finished speaking, Thi closed her eyes and was 69 years old. It was the 34th year of Qianlong.

Thi's daughter, who became the Chau family's daughter-in-law, also practiced very diligently. Every day she recites the Lotus Sutra and recites Amitabha Buddha's name. There are many people who are close to us and are inspired to practice.

Excerpted from the series Thien Nu Nhon Truyen

---o0o---

XII - BA DU

Ms. Du is the mother of Venerable Chieu Minh.

When the abbot of Cao Man Pagoda in Duong Chau, the Venerable took her to a house next to the pagoda. At first, she missed home very much. Whenever she talked to the Venerable, she would mention the familiar things about home and property. The monk then explained the dharmas of suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self and advised her to single-mindedly recite Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land. She did not comply, so the Venerable hid his face. She sent someone to invite the Venerable, but he did not come. She didn't know how to make an effort to recite Buddha's name, but every day she recited Buddha's name, it was empty because chanting Buddha's name was a suffering for her. Three years later, she became accustomed to reciting Buddha's name every day. She spontaneously developed a heart of faith, accepted the Bodhisattva precepts, and worshiped and recited Buddha's name very diligently, morning and night. The monk came to visit and asked if he still missed home? She replied: "Reciting Buddha's name is very good! I no longer miss home."

One day, while she was sitting in the yard reciting Buddha's name, the West suddenly shone with light, all the houses and forests were hidden, and she saw the world of Ultimate Bliss. So happy, she stood up and walked straight past, and at first she was no longer seen. From then on, her six senses were quiet, and in all periods of time there were no false thoughts. Only one Buddha sentence continues in the mind. Not long after, one night she dreamed that she was in a thatched house, in which there was a woman in labor. She was startled and said: "Why did I come to this place? The suffering of birth and death is terrible and terrifying. I have always wished to be born in that world of Ultimate Bliss!". She quickly ran out of that house and suddenly woke up.

The next morning, she told the Venerable Chieu Minh: "My life is over. Please invite the monks to recite Buddha's name and help me to be reborn." Then, while the monks chanted the Buddha's name in unison, she sat upright, facing the West, and passed away. At that time, it was the 27th year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from the volume Thien Nu Nhon Truyen

---o0o---

XIII - MU DUONG

Mu Duong is from Hangzhou. When she was fifty years old, she suffered from leprosy, her back stiffened, and she moaned day and night. Monk Lu Dinh returned from the capital to Thien Muc to visit her house. The woman's son invited the Master to visit her at the back of the house. She sobbed and said to the Master: "I'm very sick! Do you have any way to save me?" The monk said: "Yes! But I'm afraid she won't drink it." She said: "If it's really like that, I'll drink it." The Master said: "Listen carefully! Illness comes from the body, the body comes from false relationships. If you can let go of the body, the illness will disappear on its own." She asked: "How can I let go of my body?". The Master said: "You let go of your whole body, single-mindedly thinking of the Western Pure Land world, specializing in reciting Amitabha Buddha. Amitabha Buddha is the Great Physician who can cure the suffering of all sentient beings. Sincerely reciting Buddha's name, Buddha himself came to save you." She asked: "Is Buddha really coming?". The monk replied: "Come! I'm just worried that you don't really care about reciting Buddha's name!".

After the Master left, she immediately recited the Buddha's name and remembered the Western Pure Land, each day more and more earnestly. Five months later, she told her son: "Amitabha Buddha has arrived! Four days later, I will return to Pure Land. I welcome Master Lu Dinh to give my thanks." At that time, Master Lu Dinh had already returned to Thien Muc and could not be invited from far away.

On the fourth day, ten monks were invited to the house to help recite. Mu Duong rose up and sat down, clasped her hands and recited Buddha's name and passed away. It was the 36th year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from the volume Thien Nu Nhon Truyen

XIV - DU THI

Du Thi Chon Tu, wife of the Chau family in Ngo District, was widowed at the age of 32. At the age of 36, Thi became a vegetarian and worshiped Buddha. When she was over fifty years old, she entrusted the housework to her daughter-in-law and concentrated on cultivating her karma.

At the age of 70, in June, Thi dreamed of going to the river bank, on the river there was a large boat carrying about a dozen people of Bhikkhunis and Upasakas. A person in the boat called Thi and said: "Go to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss!". She thought to herself that if she doesn't go now, she'll wait until the end of the year to go. There was a voice inside the boat saying: "Wait for the next boat!".

On September 6, Thi dreamed that Amitabha Buddha appeared to guide her. After waking up, Thi knew that the time for her rebirth had come, so she invited Master Van Ky, her refuge teacher, to come to her house so that she could give thanks and say goodbye. The monk encouraged his efforts. She became more and more devoted to reciting Buddha's name, and the strange, sweet scent was heard everywhere, inside and out.

In the early morning of the 11th, Thi took a bath, changed into new clothes, and then sat down to recite Buddha's name. A moment later, Thi lay on her right side and passed away. In the 36th year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from the Pure Land Saint Sage Luc

XV - WOMEN'S WAGE

Luong Nu is from Fen Duong and has been blind since childhood. There was a monk who told a woman to recite Amitabha Buddha. The woman diligently recited Buddha's name. Three years later, my eyes were clear. From then on, her faith deepened, day and night she recited Buddha's name without fail.

One day, she saw a phantom necklace descending from the sky. At the same time, Buddha and Bodhisattva also came to take her. She immediately said goodbye to her relatives, clasped her hands and passed away.

A 4 - MONKS

I - OBEDIENCE

Great Master Tuan Thuc from Tri Bach, from Thai Chau. His mother dreamed of swallowing a pearl and giving birth to him. When he grew up, he went to seek salvation from the Venerable Nghia Toan in Dong Dich Son, and diligently studied law. He entered Quoc Thanh Pagoda, in front of the statue of Samantabhadra, he knuckled his fingers, and took the oath to vow the teachings of the Thien Thai sect. Then he went to Buu Van Pagoda to see Dharma Master Nghia Thong.

He once spent 90 days practicing the Eightfold Samadhi, working day and night with absolute diligence without rest until his legs cracked and his mouth vomited blood, but he still took death as a promise. At first, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara incarnated, pointed at his mouth and pulled out a few snakes. Bodhisattva's fingertips dribbled orange juice into his mouth. He felt healthy, his mind was at peace, and all his illnesses and sufferings disappeared. After that, the top of his head grew three fingers taller, his voice was as loud as a rose, and his wisdom and eloquence were unhindered.

Master Nghia Thong passed away and returned to Thien Thai.

In the second year of the Supreme Path, he lived in Buu Van, joined the Sangha to specialize in purifying karma, and vowed to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the year of Ham Binh, he went to Dong Dich Son to instruct the masses to practice reciting Buddha's Samadhi. In the year of Tuong Phu, he went to To Chau to preach Sutras at Khai Nguon pagoda. Then he returned to Hangzhou to master Linh Son. The court respected him and gave him the title of Master Tu Van Sam. He brought up Master Zhijia's release of living beings to Wang Qinruo, a governor in Hangzhou. Kham Nhuoc submitted a request to use Tay Ho as a place to release animals. The court complied.

He interpreted the Sutras to compose the repentance ritual, complete the three contemplations, and return to the Pure Land. Again, at the request of Ma Luong Trifu, he compiled the collection "Pure Land Quyet Nghi Hanh Nguyen Nhi Mon".

In that volume, the general outline of the subject of rites and rituals is as follows: There are two dharmas of Buddhism: A- Hinayana dharma with no ultimate meaning. B- Mahayana willow Dharma. In Mahayana, there is a division between definitive meaning and non-transparent meaning. Now discussing the Pure Land Dharma is the ultimate Dharma of Mahayana Buddhism. The Pure Land Dharma fully integrates cause and effect, it is truly the most profound part of Buddha Dharma. The Lotus Sutra says: "If you examine carefully the ten directions, there is no other vehicle, there is only one Buddha vehicle", which is what it says about the Pure Land Dharma. So then all the impure realms and the pure realms in the ten directions are reduced to the same in one moment. A thought of form and mind spreading throughout the entire dharma realm are natural tools, not dependent origination and approval! One thought is like that, so is one bit of dust. Therefore, in each world there are all realms, in each thought there are all minds. Every thought, every thought, covers each other, overlapping endlessly and without hindrance. At the same time, there is neither hidden nor obvious. Everything is perfect and accomplished, there is no better or worse. My mind is like that, sentient beings and Buddhas are inherently the same. Thus, the mind passes through tens of thousands of millions of worlds, but in reality it is only a waterfall born in one's own mind. The nine stages of lotus conception do not go beyond the moment of sacrifice. Those who believe and understand this comprehensive theory have no reason not to understand it. Those who are confused about the subtle and wonderful principles of this world are also confused everywhere. Therefore, in the Contemplation Sutra, it teaches: "The Tathagata Buddhas are the body of the Dharma Realm, entering the minds of all sentient beings... That mind becomes Buddha, that mind is Buddha." Now just to resolve doubts, let everyone understand that: The solemn treasures and the nine levels of cause and effect in the Pure Land are all located in the hearts of living beings. Only when the nature of reason is so complete can it be put to such complete use...

And here are two methods of meditating and contemplating in the practice of vows: People who want to practice the method of contemplation of rebirth should live in a quiet place, with their bed facing the West, for ease of visualization and to show the right direction. Sit upright in the lotus position, head and spine facing each other, neither stooping nor bouncing. Regulate breathing. Calm your mind.

In the Sutras, there are many contemplative meditation methods taught, but ordinary ordinary people cannot practice them all. Now I will explain two things. Of those two things, depending on your preference, choose one and practice, but you can't practice both. But for those who have good roots, there is no problem.

A- After controlling the body, anger and mind, think to yourself that your practice is worthy of being reborn in the Pure Land. Then I thought I was born in the Pure Land sitting cross-legged in a precious lotus flower. Imagine the lotus buds. Imagine the lotus blooming. Right when the flowers bloomed, I thought there was a 500-color ray of light shining on my body, I thought I opened my eyes. Imagine seeing Buddha and Bodhisattva. I thought I saw a solemn scene. Imagine waking up to worship the Buddha and then sitting and listening to the wonderful Dharma, listening to all the sounds of birds singing, leaves rustling, water flowing, music vibrating, all expressing into words the Buddha Dharma that I inherently like to hear. Everything you see and hear must be in accordance with the Sutras. When you think you are above it, it is very necessary to be steadfast in your mindfulness and not let your mind be agitated. Thoughts appear as clearly as the eyes, but after a long time they will be released.

B- Imagine Amitabha Buddha with a golden body sixteen meters tall sitting on a large lotus flower. Looking at a white hair between the Buddha's eyebrows, that hair is 15 meters long, five inches in circumference, eight regular corners, hollow and transparent like a crystal tube, swirling to the right. That feather is clear and clearly illuminates the Buddha's golden face. When contemplating like this, keep your mind focused and don't let it get distracted.

Afterwards, you should consider and see that by remembering, either it has come to pass or it has not come to pass. It is all due to the cause of remembrance that it appears. It has no true self-nature, the whole thing is emptiness. Like a reflection in a mirror, like moonlight under water, like a dream, like magic, empty, false, neutral, inconceivable. Thinking and knowing like this, the mind does not grasp at first, but the mind becomes calm, and can achieve Buddha-recitation Samadhi.

In the year of Thien Thanh, he lived alone in the Nhat Quan hermitage, a hermitage on the east side of the temple gate, day and night thinking about the Western Pure Land. After finishing preaching the Vimalakirti Sutra, he entrusted the teaching chair to Master Zen, one of his senior disciples. He composed a verse of thanksgiving to show that he was about to pass away.

In the first year of the Ming Dao year, on the 8th day of the 10th lunar month, suffering from a mild illness, he gave up medicine and still gathered together to teach the essential dharma. After preaching the Dharma, he asked to visit the statue of Amitabha Buddha. They again asked for the statue of Avalokiteśvara to be brought back. He knelt down, lit incense and prayed: "I observe that Avalokiteśvara is neither born nor destroyed. The Buddhas of the ten directions live together, please accept this incense stick. Buddhas prove that I will be reborn in the Pure Land." Someone asked where he was going. He replied that it was Pure Light. That afternoon, he sat cross-legged and passed away. Life expectancy is 69 years old. People saw a very large star falling on the top of Linh Vu Mountain, with bright red light.
