noi_dung:
C 4 - BELIEVERS

I - DUONG GIA VI

Mr. Duong Gia Vi, from Kiet An, a student during the Van Li period of the Ming dynasty.

When he was young, he was very eager to learn and did not read books, especially Buddhist scriptures. At the age of 13, he strictly observed the precept of not killing. Even if it were a bug or mosquito, he would not harm it. At the age of 24, when he was sick, he dreamed of going to the underworld to meet Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at the Minh Duong palace. After waking up, he bribed the pomfret to release it and invited the monks to come to his house to recite the Buddha's Sutras.

A few days later he said: "I am about to be reborn! The green lotus flower appears before me, isn't that the Pure Land scene?". From that moment on, he loudly recited Buddha's name day and night. One night, he told his family to turn off the lights and said: "I am always in the light of Buddha, I don't need the lights." Asked what he saw, he replied: "The precious lotus blooms in four colors." Asked if he had seen the Buddha, he replied: "I saw Amitabha Buddha appearing in the form of a thousand feet tall. Avalokiteśvara also appeared in the same form as the Buddha. I just did not see Mahasthamaprapta." Having finished speaking, he got up and recited incense: "Amitabha Sutra, the merits are indescribable! Indescribable! Indescribable! I have been reborn as a high-ranking person!". Then he peacefully passed away.

Excerpted from Vang Sanh Tap

---o0o---

II - TRAN DAO DAN

Mr. Tran Dao Dan from Ngo Giang has been a vegetarian since childhood. In the 26th year of Gia Tinh, he took refuge and received the Five Precepts from Dharma Master Ky Vien. Every day he went through six sessions of chanting, never leaving his mouth open of Buddha's words.

In the 15th year of Van Lich, in the ninth month, he knew the date and time in advance and went to say goodbye to his friends. On the night of the 17th, his wife had just lit a lamp to knit. He hugged his wife goodbye, then sat on the bed. He took off his shoes and socks, tied them together and said, "Tomorrow morning I won't put my feet on anymore." His wife quickly called their children to stand and watch him and chant Buddha's name in unison along with him. At midnight, he quietly passed away, his body still sitting upright on the bed.

Excerpted from Thanh Hien Luc So ​​Bien

---o0o---

III - THROUGH DI AN

Mr. Qua Di An from Tien Duong took refuge with Great Master Lien Tri. He was originally a filial person who liked to do virtuous things. When he was old, he served Buddha very sincerely. He joined forces with Master Nguyen To to form an association to recite Buddha's name and chant the Avatamsaka Sutra. After a while, he said: "My life is almost over, I have to urgently take care of my food and return to the Pure Land." Then he confined himself to a separate house, chanting Buddha's name day and night and meditating on the West. One day, he sent an appointment before his rebirth and said goodbye to his friends.

Two days before the appointment, his relatives came to visit him, and everyone looked sad. He said: "There is birth, there is death, what is there to be sad about? I am stopping the mantra, imagining the Pure Land in front of Amitabha Buddha. Don't let love disturb my mindfulness!" He sent someone to invite Master Nguyen To to join him in reciting the Buddha's name in unison. Indeed, he was mindful and clear, and passed away peacefully on the day he had promised.

Excerpted from Vang Sanh Tap

---o0o---

IV - DO CU SI

Do Layman, from Thuan Thien, lived in hiding on the street next to Thuy Quang pagoda in Tay Son. For nearly thirty years he concentrated on reciting Buddha's name. When anyone came to visit, he just clasped his hands and chanted Buddha's name. Later, he predicted that he was about to die, so he spent nine days praying to Buddha to repent. Every time he read the urgent words in the repentance text, he choked up and shed tears. After nine days of repentance, he sat upright and passed away. Ten days later, when he was buried, his body was still as fresh as life. That day, five-colored clouds covered the road. People in Tay Son all praise each other as a rare miracle.

Excerpted from Vang Sanh Tap

---o0o---

V - CO NGUYEN

Mr. Co Nguyen's name is Buu Trang Layman, from Ung Thien. He was a famous scholar of the Gia Tinh period. When he was young, he was famous for his talent, writing good poetry, writing well, and drawing well. At the age of 40, he completely quit all his previous jobs, became a vegetarian, lived alone in a small building, and specialized in meditation. Women, even relatives, were never allowed to see his face. Every night until the beginning of the fifth watch, he played a loud drum and chanted Amitabha Buddha loudly.

Nearby there is a meat restaurant. When I heard the sound of chanting Buddha's name, I woke up and became a pig. One day the butcher woke up late and angrily scolded his wife for not waking him up. The wife said: "Haven't you heard that at this time Mr. Dao Nhon is playing a flute and reciting Buddha's name? People at that time were worried about practicing and you were worried about creating bad karma. You don't know your sins, so why do you come back and scold me?". Hearing his wife's words, the butcher was surprised, considered his own mistakes, and felt very remorseful, so he broke his knife and quit his job as a butcher. Therefore, many butchers in that country were also impressed and changed their profession to other jobs.

Mr. Co Nguyen was very close to Zen Master Van Coc at The Ha Pagoda, and together with the Zen master founded a Western association.

Great Master Ham Son Duc Thanh, a senior disciple of Van Coc Zen Master, one day came to The Ha and saw a lay person sitting in a very serene manner. The Great Master approached and saw that the lay person's eyes were not blinking, his face looked like someone who had left this world. Moments later, the lay people entered the stupa hall to worship the Buddha's relics. The top of the stupa suddenly appeared with dazzling five-color light like a precious curtain. The Great Master was surprised and asked this matter to Zen Master Van Coc. The Zen master said: "That is a treasure, he is contemplating the West!".

A little while later, Mr. Co Nguyen became slightly ill. He invited a few monks to come to the building to recite Buddha's name. Family members ran to report: "The whole house can smell the scent of lotus." The monks all congratulated him. But he remained calm as if nothing, leisurely telling the monks: "For more than half a month now, I have been sitting in the lotus flower, seeing Amitabha Buddha's body growing across the entire empty world, the world is golden in color. The Buddha smiled at me, held my hand, and covered me with his robe. I will give birth to Ultimate Bliss."

His sons cried and asked: "Father, he has returned to the West and has settled down, but what will happen to us now?". He laughed and said: "You guys think I'm alive! I'm dead! Don't look at the sun: it rises in the East and sets in the West. Is the sun really setting?" Then he set a timer in advance. When it was time for him to shower, change his clothes, sit upright, facing the West, and pass away. The fragrant lotus scent lasted for three days before dissipating.

Excerpted from Ham Son Mong Du Tap

---o0o---

VI - CHAU NGUYEN CHANH

Mr. Chau Nguyen Chanh, a famous scholar in Hai Diem, had the will to learn the virtues of Saint Hien and was very strict every day. When he was over 60 years old, when he was able to penetrate meditation, he lived alone in a house behind the garden, not receiving guests or asking about housework. Every morning, he recited a volume of the Lotus Sutra, and in the afternoon he meditated.

One day, Mr. Tran Tac Luong, his student, came to visit and asked: "You are already old, why don't you temporarily introduce the precept to alcohol?". He said with a serious face: "Are you trying to tell me to take care of my blood? You don't know that I have control over life and death!". Tac Luong shivered in fear and retreated. In July of that year, he told his son: "I have no duty here so I should go." The son asked: "Where do you plan to go?". He replied: "Go to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss!". My children and grandchildren tried to hold him back.

On the first day of December, he became slightly ill and stopped eating. Family members are busy shopping for things. He said: "Don't be in a hurry! This is at midnight on the eighth day, not right now." When the time came, he wanted to leave this world, but said: "In all my life, I have never betrayed anyone. This winter, the worker behind the house cleared the grass and leveled a plot of land next to the garden alley. He wanted to wait until the first day of Tet so that it would be convenient for me to move on. I have nothing to repay his kindness!" He told him to bring back paper and pen, then personally wrote the exam to thank the worker, and told his children and grandchildren to send the women in about two or three hours after his death. Even if they came, they should not cry. After finishing his instructions, he still sat still and closed his eyes before passing away. At dawn, relatives gathered around and cried. He suddenly opened his eyes, shook his head and waved his hand to leave. When all the women came out, he closed his eyes and walked straight.

Excerpted from the collection of Phap Hoa Tri Nghi Nghiep

---o0o---

VII - CHAU DINH CHUONG

Mr. Chau Dinh Chuong is from Yunnan and has a truly gentle nature. When doing business, he doesn't count whether he wins or loses, if he has extra money he shares it with the poor. If anyone came to discuss something with him, he would laugh and not answer. Even if someone mocked or scolded him, he would only laugh.

Every morning, early in the morning, he recited one volume of the Diamond Sutra, one volume of the Amitabha Sutra, and one volume of the Avalokiteshvara Sutra, then dedicated it to the Pure Land. He was very satisfied with that job. He once said: "I don't leave my daily use, I don't let my mind crave, that's enough."

At the age of 87, during the Qingming Festival, he went to the tomb to pay his respects to his ancestors. Returning home, he immediately told everyone: "Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva all came to welcome me!". Then he said again: "Avalokiteśvara told me to abstain from eating fish and meat for five days before I can return to the West." And starting that day, he only ate white porridge with boiled vegetables. After five full days, he bathed, changed clothes, put on a hat, and told his children to chant the name of the Tathagata. As for him, he recited the Sutras as usual. After reciting, he sat upright and passed away. The next day, there was a strange scent coming from his body, his face was still as fresh as life.

Excerpted from the episode Vajra Linh Ung Luc

---o0o---

VIII - PAGE QUANG HOAN

Mr. Trang Quang Hoan is from Phuc Chon, from Gia Hung. When he was young, he studied Confucianism, when he grew up he studied medicine. By the time he was forty years old, he was bored with life's work and specialized in practicing the art of nurturing life. A little while later, when he fell ill, he sadly lamented: "Can I not be a leisurely person in this world?". He created a garden, piled rocks to make mountains, planted cotton, repaired ornaments, and then spent all day singing in it. One day, seeing the flowers wither and fall, thinking that his life was impermanent, he immediately destroyed the garden, closed the door and meditated while chanting the Diamond Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, etc.

Then he went to Hangzhou, met an old man and discussed Buddhism together. The old man asked: "You study Buddhism, but who is your teacher?". He replied: "I don't have a teacher." The old man said: "You must have read the book "Phuc Khi" by Lieu Tu Hau! On the impermanent and wonderful path without a guide, there is no way to get lost. Recently, there was Great Master Lien Tri at Van The pagoda, why don't you come and study?" He obeyed and went to Van The Pagoda to meet Great Master Lien Tri. The Great Master taught about the Buddhist recitation method. He asked for refuge and received the Five Precepts. When he returned home, he planned to recite fifty thousand Buddhist verses every day. Practicing for less than half a year, the mind becomes clear. At the age of 80, he went to Van The again to receive the Bodhisattva precepts.

He was often worried that people in the land did not understand the Dharma and that most of them were inclined to follow pagan religions. He then took key words from the Sutras on the Pure Land to create the collection "Pure Land Tu Luong Tap" to advise people. From then on, gradually people in the land were inspired and returned to the Dharma.

Excerpted from the Pure Land Tu Luong Tap

---o0o---

IX - BAO TONG TRIEU

Layperson Bao Tong Trieu, from Tanh Tuyen, from Shaoxing. His family was originally a vegetarian, followed the Five Precepts, memorized the Lotus Sutra and the Shurangama Sutra, and recited it once a day.

One day, his father ordered him to look at the paper goods in Gia Hung. He was angry at him, tore up the paper and punished him to kneel. After a moment of standing up, he finished reciting ten volumes of the Shurangama Sutra.

A little while later, he studied with great Zen masters such as Tu Ba, Tan Moc, etc. When he was almost old, he went two or three times to interview Great Master Lien Tri, then asked for refuge and received precepts, and devoted himself to cultivating pure karma.

He studied Phuong Son Hiep Luan and Vinh Minh Tong Canh Luc and received favorable explanations. Self-titled "Thien Co Layman". He has a collection of works called "Thien Nhac Minh Khong".

When he was about to die, he told his family to prepare a vegetarian feast, then invited his Dharma friends to come to his house and chant Amitabha Buddha in unison. When the sun was about to set, he clasped his hands in thanks to everyone and said: "Farewell, gentlemen!". Then he sat down and passed away.

Excerpted from Thien Nhac Minh Khong Tap

---o0o---

X - LA DOAN MAI

Layperson La Doan Mai from Thai Thuong. My father dreamed that a monk came to his house and asked to stay, and in the morning he was born as a layman. When he was four years old, the layman clearly remembered the appearance of his parents from previous generations, including the name of the village, and often recounted it to his family members. When he was five years old, one day the layman ran around the pole and fell dizzy, so his mother beat him. The layman cried tiredly and fell asleep. When he woke up, he no longer remembered the events of his previous life.

Lay people are very smart, when entering school everyone decides that lay people will be in the class. But his father saw that lay people were always weak, so he did not let him take the exam. The layperson studied with Zen Master Nghiet Nham to understand the wonderful principles, and took the title "Vo Thien Layperson". Then the layperson concentrates on returning to the Pure Land.

When his father was old, the layman took on all the housework, not bothering his old father, and diligently took care of him. People at that time praised lay people as filial people.

In the fall of Kangxi's 40th year, the layman became seriously ill and wanted to write verses and pass away. At first I heard a loud call in the air: "Layman Thang Lien, you still have a century to live!". Then the illness healed immediately. Relatives were surprised, so together they called the layperson "Thang Lien".

People in the land rarely know how to practice. Lay people encouraged the establishment of Buddhist recitation conferences in four places, thanks to which the sound of reciting Buddha's name spread throughout the entire district.

In the fall of Kangxi's 52nd year, the layman fell ill, counting for 12 years. Relatives are worried, but lay people remain calm. A few days, the layman dreamed of someone saying: "You advise people to recite Buddha's name because they have great merit, so their life will be long." After waking up, the illness seemed to disappear.

Lay people have a very benevolent nature, and all the things they do are educating them, taking care of the elderly, diagnosing the poor, releasing living beings, etc., all they practice with all their heart and soul. Normal lay people only think about the suffering of others, without considering the harm to themselves. Here is one of many things: In the winter of At Mui year, two neighbors borrowed 100 taels of silver from a lay person to do business. When the boat arrived at Thien Phi temple in the pre-lost era. The whole boat of seven people returned, about to go to the public door to denounce. The lay people heard about it, called everyone together and said: "When you come to the mandarin, you will be subjected to torture and interrogation. If it is the thief, then it's okay, but if not, then why not! Besides, there are two people here in a far away country, during the days of being imprisoned, who will bring them food and water?". Then the layman promised not to have to return the borrowed money, and told the two neighbors to leave the matter behind. Seeing this is enough to see the charitable heart of lay people.

At the age of 71, in the Doan Duong period, Hoai Tay lay person came to visit. The lay person was very happy and said: "I want to compose the book "Western Quy Truc Chi" to advise people to recite Buddha's name. Please write it on my behalf, so that it can be engraved soon!". Hoai Tay accepted.

On June 2 of that year, lay people said goodbye to their relatives and friends, earnestly advised them to practice, and promised to return to Pure Land on the 6th. The layman again told his family to take care of engraving the book "Western Quy Truc Chi".

On June 6, the lay person showered, changed his clothes, then sat down and said: "Seventy-one years, wearing this skin, today I throw it away, how free!" Having finished speaking, the layman immediately passed away. An hour later, the relatives were crying excessively, the layman opened his eyes and said: "Why do you have to delay me for seven days!".

Early in the morning of the 14th, the layperson said: "I will definitely go home today!". Next, Elder Can Hanh led a few friends to help chant. At the hour of the Dragon, the layman suddenly stood up and said: "The great monk has come to pick you up!". Then the layman clasped his hands facing the West and loudly recited Buddha's name and passed away. On the 16th, Hoai Tay brought the manuscript of "Tay Quy Truc Chi" and learned that lay practitioner Thang Lien had passed away on the day the manuscript was finished.

Excerpted from the volume Chau An Si Van Gao

---o0o---

XI - CHAU MONG NHAN

Mr. Chau Mong Nhan, originally named Tu Nhon, nicknamed An Si, is a famous scholar in Con Son. He was knowledgeable throughout the Sutra Pitaka, deeply believed in the Pure Land Dharma, and called himself "Layman Hoai Tay".

He once considered that: People in the world commit countless crimes, of which the two evil karmas of killing and adultery account for half of them. He then composed two sets of books: precepts for killing and precepts for sexual immorality.

The set of precepts is "Van Thien Tien Tu" in which the words are so urgent that anyone who reads them will be moved. He said to himself every time he went to temples to worship: "I hope that the Venerable Deity will develop the mind to go to this world, not to enjoy alcohol and meat. Should single-mindedly recite Amitabha Buddha to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land. This Tu Nhon, from now on until the rest of his life, if he kills a small animal, be patient with all relatives in my family, if anyone intentionally kills the life of a mosquito or ant, please punish the Venerable and destroy all the books I have composed. From now on, this Tu Nhon will let me know. For the rest of your life, if you see a fish in distress but do not pity and try to save it, but instead have the heart to kill, it is the same as the above vow. From now on, even if it is in a dream, if you see a person killing living beings but do not sincerely recite the Buddha's name, develop the mind to save, and return with joy and approval, it is also the same as the above oath.

The set of sexual precepts is called "Duc Hai Hoi Cuong", which clearly points out the countless sins and many sufferings of people who commit adultery. With the method of eliminating lust, he presented: A- Observe clearly all kinds of bad suffering, as the first means to end lust. B.- Observe that in this human body there are countless germs, used as doors for the contemplation of impurity.

C.- Observe the bodies of men and women, which are full of blood, pus, mucus, saliva and saliva, the skin covering dirt, to treat desire. D- Observe the dead person's body: green, bruised, cold and stiff, swollen and cracked, extremely stinky, giving birth to maggots, the skin and flesh rotting, bones falling apart... This is my current body, tomorrow it will be the same. Use it as a means to completely end lust. E- Visualize your body in a precious lotus flower in a seven-jeweled pond in the Pure Land. Flowers bloom, you see Buddha and Bodhisattvas and other solemn and pure scenes, you see yourself making offerings to the Buddha. When contemplating like this, make a sincere vow to be reborn in the Pure Land world, to completely escape the world of desire. This is the ultimate means of liberation.

In addition, he also composed the series "Quang Nghia Literature Acoustics" and the series "Western Quy Truc Chi".

In the 4th year of Qianlong, in January he told his family that he was going to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss. The family asked to bring him fragrant water so he could bathe. He said: "I used perfumed water to wash myself!". He said and laughed as usual but passed away. A strange scent permeates the whole house. Life expectancy is 84 years old.

Previously, he had a friend, Vuong Manh Lan, who was dedicated to cultivating the Pure Land and considered reciting Buddha's name every day as his most urgent task. In the 41st year of Khang Hi, in the winter, Mr. Lan got sick. In November, when he came to visit, Manh Lan said: "On the 17th, people consider Amitabha Buddha's Holy Birthday, I will return to Pure Land on that day!". He promised to come and deliver. On the morning of the 17th, he arrived and saw Manh Lan, although he was sick, his expression was bright and cheerful. He said: "You should develop Bodhi mind! The Sutras teach that people who practice without developing Bodhi mind are like plowing a field without sowing seeds." Then he clearly explained the meaning of the "Four Great Oaths". Mr. Manh Lan nodded happily. He said goodbye and would return shortly. After lunch, he returned to the time when Manh Lan had recited Buddha's name and passed away halfway through the afternoon. At that time, it had been more than three hours, but Mr. Lan's body was still upright, his face unchanged.

Excerpted from the series An Si Complete Poetry

---o0o---

XII - KHUONG KIEN LONG

Mr. Khuong Kien Long is from Ngo Huyen and has a generous nature. During the year of famine, he used all his assets to cure poverty, so his family became poor. He studied ophthalmology to make a living. He originally liked the art of eternal life (cultivating immortals).

One night, he dreamed that he came to a high mountain and deep cave, the cold wind blew chillingly, he quickly looked for someone. At first, the sky filled with nothingness. On the treasure palanquin sat a person cross-legged, his body tall and golden. He clasped his hands, looked up, and prayed: "Because of my many sins, I have strayed into this dangerous place. Please save me!" The golden relative asked: "Are you willing to make a vow?". He bowed and said: "From now on, this Kien Long vows to be a servant of the Buddha." The relatives said: "Very good! Tomorrow there will be a Bhikkhu to guide you in practicing, be careful not to miss it!". He suddenly woke up. That morning, the Monk indeed came to the house. He asked about the method of practice. The Master said: "The essence of practice is nothing but reciting Buddha's name. Those who can recite Buddha's name will be determined to be born in the West, those who can recite Buddha's name will achieve irreversible attainment, and those who can recite Buddha's name will quickly attain perfect enlightenment." Kien Long was very happy, from then on he recited Buddha's name over ten thousand sentences a day. His chanting of Buddha's name was very clear and loud, echoing throughout the entire village.

In the 43rd year of Qianlong's reign, in the eighth month, he was slightly ill and told his children: "I single-mindedly seek rebirth in the West and have no attachment to anything else." On the full moon day, he composed a verse:

Completely escape the five defilements of suffering

Rebirth in the Pure Land

Bright and beautiful precious flowers

One thought leads to enlightenment

At noon on the 16th, he peacefully recited Buddha's name and passed away. Life expectancy is 75 years old.

Excerpted from the Pure Land Saint Sage Luc

---o0o---

XIII - TRAM BINH

Mr. Tram Binh, nicknamed Kinh Phu, is from Truong Chau. At the age of 15, he suffered from asthma. At the age of 30, his illness became worse. He developed the intention to go beyond this world and recite Buddha's name very earnestly. At the age of 50, his illness became more severe, from January to May, he was bedridden. He vowed to be a vegetarian.

Duong Quang Van visited the patient and advised him to recite the Diamond Sutra. Quang Van helped him sit up and showed him how to read the entire book. By the third day, he could read three books a day. Half a month later, he recovered. From then on, every day he recited three volumes of the Diamond Sutra and continuously recited Buddha's name. At night he often meditated until morning. Asthma gradually went away, but my back became hunched. Five years later, one night while meditating on the Buddha's name, he vowed to attain perfect enlightenment for all living beings. Immediately his spine suddenly creaked and his back straightened like a normal person. Then he came to receive the Five Precepts from Great Master Lu Dinh.

He often said: "All things in the world are born and die without stopping, there is only one sentence Amitabha Buddha is the most peaceful!". He also said that his practice of reciting the Buddha's name was very effective. During times of serious illness and whole body suffering, just one clear Buddha sentence was never forgotten in his mind.

In the 46th year of Qianlong, November, he was mildly ill for a few days. Early in the morning of the 30th, after washing, he cross-legged, faced the West and recited Buddha's name. His wife stood nearby and he told her to leave. A moment later, seeing him sitting quietly for too long, his family came to see that he had passed away.

His wife also became a man and recited Buddha's name, then became a nun.

Excerpted from Nhi Lam Cu Hau Tap

---o0o---

XIV - TRAM TRUNG HUC

Mr. Tram Trung Huc from Ngo Huyen, a famous physician of the Qing Dynasty. He loved giving alms. It's different for poor patients who don't take medicine money, but also help with rice money. His wife died early, he did not patch things up, he diligently cultivated pure karma every day.

Whether at the beginning of the road, or by the bridge, or in the city, he wrote the name of Amitabha Buddha and essential words to advise people to recite Buddha's name. When he encountered a seriously ill person, he lamented and said, "My strength cannot save me." The patient cried and prayed. He said: "You must recite the Buddha's name. The Western Pure Land world has Amitabha Buddha. If you sincerely recite the Buddha's name, you will be able to eliminate the heavy sins of birth and death for countless lifetimes. Do you believe it?" The patient replied: "Yes!". He asked again: "Can you concentrate on reciting Buddha's name?". The patient obeyed again. He said: "If it's true then the disease can be cured." Then he gave medicine. Always exceptionally effective. Therefore, there are many people who believe in him and develop the mind to become vegetarian and recite Buddha's name.

When he was over 70 years old, he passed away with mindfulness and peace. Nearly a few decades later, the people of that country, when discussing the ranks of lay people cultivating pure karma, put him first.

Excerpted from Nhi Lam Cu Hau Tap

---o0o---

XV - NATIONAL DETERMINATION

Mr. Quy Dinh, national name Tinh Trai, from Minh Chau, held Hoc Du position in the continent. He was originally a person who cultivated pure karma and founded the Western Refuge Association.

In the year Gia Thoi, he built the Pure Land Institute in Tieu Giang and built a stone tower at the pond to store the bones of people in the land. Every month, on the 8th and 18th, the Sangha and laity meet in the monastery, chant Sutras and recite Buddha's name. He engraved "Reciting Buddha's name" to advise people to recite Buddha's name.

Ke Cong, a blacksmith, became blind at the age of 70. He received Buddha's name. Recite all four diagrams and your eyes will become clear as usual. In three full years, Mr. Ke completed 17 paintings. One day, while reciting Buddha's name, Mr. Ke suddenly died, and after half a day he came back to life and told his son: "I have seen Buddha and Bodhisattva in the world of Ultimate Bliss. Demon Hoc Du is the one who guided me to practice, so I should share the merit of six statues and give them to him, and thank him in my place!". Having finished his instructions, he headed to the West and passed away.

In the 4th year of Gia Dinh, Mr. Dinh Quoc dreamed of Thanh Dong and said: "Buddha sent me to tell you: After three days you will be born in the Pure Land." When the time came, he showered, changed his clothes, then sat down, recited the Buddha's name and passed away.

Excerpted from Buddha Tong Ky

---o0o---

XVI - HUYNH THUA HUE

Mr. Huynh Thua Hue from Hangzhou is detail-oriented and does not follow customs. He worshiped his mother very fondly. Having a love of giving alms, when he met someone without a shirt, he immediately took off the shirt he was wearing and gave it to him. When he met someone lacking food, he immediately emptied all the money in his pocket and gave it to them.

Van Khai So, his sister-in-law, took him to Van The pagoda to take refuge with Great Master Lien Tri, whose dharma name was Tinh Minh.

Later, he suffered from vomiting blood for three years and his illness got worse. Van Khai Chu visited and advised him to recite Buddha's name. Because he was so sick and tired, he did not recite. Khai So said loudly: "If you die, where will this thing that you currently know suffer from go?". He was startled and asked: "What should we do then?". Khai So said: "There is nothing better than reciting Buddha's name!". He asked: "Are you telling me to recite Amitabha's self-nature or Amitabha's Ultimate Bliss?". Khai So replied: "So you think it's two?". He came to his senses and immediately invited Dharma Master Hue Van to come to his house to worship the Buddha statue. The shaman explains the cause and effect of the Pure Land. He was very happy and prayed to the Dharma Master to come down and become a novice monk. After receiving the precepts, he told his relatives not to come near him, only to let a young man take care of him. Then he concentrated on reciting Buddha's name and silently chanting the Lotus Sutra. Seven days later, all family members smelled the fragrant lotus scent. He smiled and said: "Don't bring a thing, don't take away a thing. The full moon rises to the top of a high mountain, only then can you truly see your true face!". He told people to invite monks to recite Buddha's name and buy fruit and flowers to worship Buddha. When the monks recited the vow "To defend the West" to the part "Radiate light to guide, and submit to bring harmony", he suddenly stood up, sat upright, his face was joyful, his eyes were fixed on the Buddha statue, and he passed away.

Excerpted from Ham Son Mong Du Tap

---o0o---

XVII - EARLY LITERATURE

Mr. Van Khai So is a compatriot of Huynh Thua Hue. When he was young, he was often sick. He was determined to escape birth and death. He went to Van The to take refuge with Great Master Lien Tri and received the Buddhist recitation method, whose Dharma name was Dai Thanh.

On the day Master Lien Tri passed away, Master Duc Thanh came to Van The to mourn. Khai So bowed and prayed to become a monk. Great Master Duc Thanh said: "The Four Elements cannot even bless the Buddha nature, let alone a piece of hair that can hinder it! You have the duty to take care of your parents, you should not become a monk yet!". He stopped.

Not long after, feeling sick, he said: "I will go straight to the West, my illness has nothing to do with it!". When he was seriously ill, his mind was in turmoil and he could not control himself. He was very afraid and asked people to invite monks to help recite. The next day, the commotion was still the same. He calmly said: "The root of life and death cannot be uprooted by someone else!". Then he forced himself to stand up and wash his face and rinse his mouth. After dressing, he knelt before the Buddha's table, burned incense on his arm, and prayed to someone who would repent all night without getting tired. In the morning, he went back to his room and sat down. His mind was calm and clear and the Holy Realm appeared. He immediately prayed to the monks to cut his hair, then put on his cassock to say goodbye to everyone and passed away.

Hearing the news, Master Duc Thanh praised: "Mr. Van Khai So is worthy of being called Liet's mighty man."

Excerpted from Ham Son Mong Du Tap

---o0o---

XVIII - GENERAL HUC AND THIEN HOA

Truong Chung Huc, from the Tang family, makes a living as a chicken meat maker. When he was about to die, he saw someone driving a flock of chickens and shouting: "Peck!" Surgery! The chickens gathered around to peck at Huc, his face and eyes were bleeding, the pain was unbearable. When the monk Hoang Dao heard the news, he went to display the Buddha statue and advised Huc to recite the Buddha's name. Mr. Huc immediately recited with enthusiasm. After a while, suddenly there was a strange, fragrant scent throughout the house, the chickens disappeared, the bleeding stopped, and Mr. Huc sat up and passed away.

Truong Thien Hoa, also from the Duong family, worked as a cow slaughterer. When he was seriously ill, he saw a few dozen cows coming and speaking in a human voice: "If you kill us, we must pay for it!".

Mr. Hoa urged his wife to invite the Monk. The Monk said: "In the Quan Sutra it is said: "If any living being has created evil karma and is worthy of falling into the evil path, but with all his heart recites Amitabha Buddha's name for ten recitations, then his sins will be eliminated and he will be reborn in the Pure Land."

Mr. Hoa said: "Hell fire is coming, we can't wait for the incense burner!". He immediately held fire in his left hand, incense in his right hand, and loudly chanted Buddha's name toward the West. After less than ten breaths, he suddenly said: "Buddha has come to give me the precious lotus throne." After saying that, he stopped breathing.

Excerpted from Buddha Tong Ky

---o0o---

noi_dung:
D 4 - FEMALE TRUSTEES

I - CONTACT THREE BA BA

Dien Ba lived on a farm in Thoi Chau. Husband and wife believe in the Three Jewels, often create Buddha statues, release sentient beings and monks, and give alms. Her husband recites the Lotus Sutra every day, while she only specializes in reciting Buddha's name. Practicing like this for more than twenty years.

On August 23, the 14th year of Shun Tri, she told her son to quickly go pick up her two younger sisters, because she would return to the West that day. When her relatives were present, she advised everyone to stay and try to practice. The whole family was in tears. She recited the verse:

At the age of fifty-six, the big event is over

My husband and children are very sad!

Now I walk straight to the Pure Land

The wisdom on the other shore is bright and clear!

Having finished speaking, Dien Ba sat cross-legged, clasped her hands and passed away.

Tuong Thi is from Hung Hoa. At the age of 40, her husband died and after the burial, Thi cried and told her son: "When impermanence comes, no one can take the place of anyone else. For example, if I die now, you won't be able to do anything. From now on, I will continue to recite Buddha's name and not care about anything else!" The son agreed with his mother and built a thatched hut near the house for her to live in. Thi was then banned from reciting Buddha's name for a full five years. On the 20th day of the 17th year of Thuan Tri, Thi told her to buy planks for the ceremony, because she would return to Pure Land on the 23rd. She said goodbye to her friends. When the time came, Thi went to sit in recitation of Buddha and passed away. A moment later, fire suddenly erupted from Thi's body, burning both her body and her body.

Ms. Ha from Changzhou and her husband, Mr. Phan Thuong Cao, practiced pure karma together. Every day, she recited the Diamond Sutra, morning and night repenting and reciting the Buddha's name, praying to be born in the Pure Land. In the 17th year of Kangxi, she got sick in July. She planned to return to life at noon on the 29th. On the 29th, all the children gathered together and invited their friends to come to the house and recite Buddha's name in unison. Unfortunately, at noon, Mrs. Ha happily passed away.

Excerpted from the Lien Tang

---o0o---

II - TWO GIRLS

Ms. Huynh Tuan was orphaned as a child. Every day she followed her grandmother to bow to Buddha and chant Sutras. When she grew up, she promised to marry the Luc family. She suddenly became seriously ill. She was determined to leave this world and told her helper to bow to Buddha and repent. When the bridegroom was told he was coming to visit, his family wanted to lead him to his bedside, but she waved his hand and refused to let him. That afternoon, after inviting the monks to come to her house to receive precepts, she called the guy named Luc and said: "From now on, the fate is broken, don't think about it. You should also start early and don't be infatuated forever." Having finished speaking, she asked the monks to take down their hair. After shaving her hair, the monk monk thanked her three times, then she sat upright and passed away. More than an hour later, her body still remained intact. The next day, her family changed clothes for her body. A strange scent suddenly emitted from her body, and pink light shone on her cheeks and eyebrows.

Mr. Wang Jingshi's daughter in Jiangsu promised to marry Tu Canh Thieu. At the age of 17, she received precepts, morning and night, worshiping the statue of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Not long after, Canh Thieu became ill and died. The day she received the funeral card, she immediately wore cloth clothes and straw sandals, built her own house, and practiced as a monk for five years. One day she said goodbye to her relatives and promised to return to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss. When the time came, her left hand crossed the mudra, stood up straight and passed away.

Excerpted from the volume "Sound Quality of Text Notes" by Ha Si Vien

---o0o---

III - TU THI

Tu Thi is from Tong Giang, the wife of Mr. Duong Phat Trai. At the age of 32, Thi became a vegetarian, recited Buddha's name and recited the Great Compassion Mantra to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land world. Every day, early in the morning, she lit incense and recited Buddha's name a thousand times, recited the mantra 21 times, and then took care of the housework. In the evening, the photographer meditated on Buddha. She practiced like that for 29 years without missing a day.

In the summer of Qianlong's 35th year, Thi fell ill. Early in the morning of June 8, Thich chanted as usual. After reciting the mantra for a moment, the family heard the sound of Thi's chanting echoing out of the alley. They were surprised and went into the Buddha worship room to see, but Thi had already sat down, smiling, and had passed away.

It was hot weather at that time, and three days later, Thi's corpse was still as fresh as life. When Thi's clothes were burned, all the flames turned into five-colored lotus flowers. Everyone who sees it praises it as a miracle in life.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

IV - AM COORDINATE

The wife of a soldier in Tong Giang, widowed without children, lives in a thatched house south of Pho Chieu pagoda. She has a straightforward nature, when she sees a woman's fault, she always criticizes her to her face. That's why most of the women there respected her.

Every day, she chants according to a schedule: early in the morning, she recites the Diamond Sutra two times, then takes care of work, and at night closes the door to recite Buddha's name. She practiced like that until she was old without any delay.

One day, a monk passed by in front of the house. She clasped her hands and asked: "I heard that Vajrayana does not destroy the body. The person who recites this Sutra will also be able to have the flesh indestructible, right, Venerable?" The Monk replied: "Yes!". She immediately sat down and passed away that same day. The poor family did not have shrouds, the body sat naked for three whole days, despite the hot weather that did not change, a strange scent fragrantly scented the whole house. Admiral Duong Cong Thiep's wife personally came to the house to arrange the funeral and built a monastery right on that plot of land, naming it "Sitting Death Am" (Sitting Death Am). Using linoleum to wrap her body and bury it in the hut, it is still intact.

A little while later, the wife of an official in the country, whose husband died, came to practice at that hermitage. Every day she devoted herself to reciting Buddha's name. She did not step out of the hermitage for a full 50 years, except once to go to Dai Hung Son to pay homage to the Venerable Khe Coc to receive dharma precepts. In the year of crop failure, she cooked grass and ate it. If a woman makes an offering, if she is not a good person, it is better to go hungry than to accept it. Before and after, there were two or three disciples, but because the suffering was too much to bear, they all left. The older she got, the more diligent her rituals became. When she was nearly 90 years old, not sick, she recited Buddha's name and passed away peacefully, at that time around the Qianlong era of the Qing Dynasty.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

---o0o---

V - MU TAO

Mu Tao, mother of Mr. Ba Thien Ho in Changzhou. Thien Ho likes to do good deeds and worships Lu Chon Nhon. He often inquired about the celestial arts of the Hon and preferred to sit quietly and respectfully. One day, he went to Suzhou and was given the book "Tay Phuong Xa Chi" as a gift. In that volume, there is a passage about immortal magic, pointing to the Pure Land. Thien Ho had just started in the Buddha vehicle, but still had doubts, so he asked the True Man. Lu Chon Nhon said: "Do you have any doubts anymore? When the great disaster comes, we Thien Immortals will have no way to escape. Lac Bang is very pure and peaceful. You should try! In addition to reciting Buddha's name and worshiping Buddha, you should also recite the Diamond Sutra to pray for rebirth." Hearing Chon Nhan's explanation, Thien Ho no longer had any doubts, from then on he was determined to practice Pure Land. That year, Ms. Cao was 64 years old and fell ill. Hearing the news, Thien Ho quickly returned from To Chau. When he arrived home, his mother was already out of breath, only her chest was not yet cold. While the family was preparing for the coffin, Thien Ho cried loudly, bowed to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, recited the white-robed mantra one hundred and two thousand times, vowing to reduce his lifespan by a century to pray for his mother to live. He cried until his tears and nose wet the hem of his ao dai. The next morning, Mrs. Cao suddenly stirred and wanted to drink, and in just a few days she was healthy. She narrated that: When she first died, two demons led her through Thanh Hoang's Earth Lands and then to Dong Nhac Palace. The Quan Palace said that thanks to her son's sincere prayers to Guan Yin, she was granted a longer life. Then Phu Quan commanded the ghost to bring his mother back, so she came back to life.

Thien Ho advised her to practice Pure Land. Ms. Cao immediately became a vegetarian, three times a day recited the Buddha's rosary to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land. Twelve years later, she was 76 years old, on the full moon day of the ninth month, she said to Thien Ho: "Mom is about to return to Pure Land, please invite your relatives to say goodbye to you." After saying goodbye to everyone, Ms. Cao took a shower, changed her clothes, and passed away peacefully.

Thien Ho has an aunt, Hua Thi, who is also a young man reciting Buddha's name but has not yet specialized in it. Thien Ho took her to his house and advised her to let go of all predestined relationships and single-mindedly recite Buddha's name. Hua Thi obeyed. That year, Thi was 65 years old. From March to June, there are three full months of reciting Buddha's name without interruption. One day, when Thi bowed to Thien Ho, he was startled and asked why. Hua Thi replied: "I'm over 65, I've always been crazy in my dreams, I've never had a peaceful day. Since you taught me how to recite Buddha's name until now, I've been reciting Buddha's name in the morning until it's already evening, and in an instant, reciting Buddha's name at night has already brightened the day. There's nothing more peaceful in life than here! If it weren't for you, I wouldn't be like this, so I bow to you." Therefore, Heavenly Protector praised the purity and solemnity of the Land of Ultimate Bliss and said that if one can be single-minded, the Holy Realm will manifest itself. When the Holy Realm appears, you should not be greedy. Three months later, at midnight, Hua Thi was sitting and reciting Buddha's name when she saw a flying golden lotus flower appear in front of her, then turned into hundreds of thousands of millions of countless lotus flowers flying into the void, shining brightly across the sky and earth. That morning, Hua Thi went to worship Thien Ho and told the story. From that day on, Thi's appearance was as youthful as someone about thirty years old. At that time, it was the 42nd year of Qianlong. The whole day, besides reciting Buddha's name, Thi said nothing else. At night, Thi only lay down to rest for about an hour, and then meditated and recited Buddha's name.

Excerpted from the collection of Western Gong Practices

VI - DAO THI

Dao Thi's name is Thien, her name is Quynh Lau, from To Chau, the wife of Mr. Banh Hi Lac, the niece of layperson Banh Nhi Lam. As a child, Thi was very smart, good at poetry, and often sang sketches with her younger sister, Ms. Dao Nhon, early in the evening. Not long after, Dao Nhon got sick and died. She quit being a poet and didn't work anymore. Reading the Announcement Sutra, she appreciated the ascetic fate of the Buddha's previous life. She then made a great vow, vowing to attain the Dharma of Endlessness. Describes the Grace Sutra and the Diamond and Amitabha Sutras... the handwriting is both beautiful and straight. Every day, Thi diligently recites Amitabha Buddha's name. After returning to the Peng family's house, every day she and her family discussed the dharmas of suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self. Early morning is Thi's time to recite Buddha's name. She studied the Lotus Sutra, Shurangama, Avatamsaka, etc. Sutras on Mahayana were easily understood.

In the fall of the 44th year of Qianlong's reign, Thi wrote ten poems recreating ten poems "Secret Poems" by the lay practitioner Banh Nhi Lam, the sentences all refer to the Pure Land, the words are very profound. During the East, Thi felt sick and knew she couldn't be strong. She recited Buddha's name without hesitation. Early the next year, Thi invited her biological mother to say goodbye. Then Thi said: "The Great Venerable has come. I will go!". The patient asked: "What about the old lady?". She said: "The Western Pure Land is very good, the next day I will take the old lady back with me." After saying that, Thi closed her eyes and was 25 years old. It was January 25, the 45th year of Qianlong.

In the 49th year of Qianlong, the great Western scholar Tich Can Bodhisattva descended to the Jade Altar to promote the Pure Land Dharma for his disciples. One day, layman Nhi Lam came to ask about the birthplace of his deceased teacher friends. Bodhisattvas all answered clearly: People are born in Heaven, people are born in humans. There were four people who returned to the Pure Land: 1.- Huong Son Lao with the dharma name Thiet Dinh. 2.- Great Master Lu Dinh's dharma name is Te Hoi. 3.- Vow to the Great Dharma Master named Buddha An. 4.- Tram Kinh Phu lay people (Agarwood). When asked about Dao Thi, Bodhisattva said that he was born on the border of the Pure Land (also known as Giai Man Quoc). Moments later, Dao Thi descended to everyone and said: "Those of you who are aiming for the world of Ultimate Bliss must train your mind like iron and stone, on the outside not be deluded by worldly desires, on the inside not let your thoughts manipulate you. That is where lotus flowers grow in the mud. If you recite one Buddha sentence, you will have a light, if you recite a thousand Buddha sentences, you will have a thousand lights. That light comes from the mind, not from the outside, because it is formless. Amitabha Buddha often does not leave them. If you have the slightest obstacle, then the light will not appear. When reciting the Buddha's name, the mind must always be enlightened to generate the power of reciting the Buddha's thoughts. When reciting the Buddha's name, the voice must be earnest to generate the power of impermanent vows. There is no place where the Buddha's name is not called Buddha's name. Only then can the Buddha's name be immeasurable. It is necessary to know immeasurable wisdom, immeasurable supernatural powers, and immeasurable compassion. If you do not generate immeasurable thoughts, how can you see? received the Buddha's name. I pity all sentient beings! If desire is not eliminated, good roots will be encroached, you must quickly recite Buddha's name!

A few months later, layperson Nhi Lam came to Ngoc Dan again to ask about Dao Thi: "It's very good to know that you have reincarnated! But Mr. La Dai Son and Chau Trong Quan, men with strict precepts and great oaths, still have to be stuck in the cycle of human blessings. As for you, your precepts are not yet perfect, your practice is not yet pure, but how can you be reborn? What is the scene like when you are reborn? After rebirth, what will the enjoyment be like? How did you come to life? Have you seen the Buddha yet? Have you reached the level of non-regression? Please explain so that everyone can understand and practice. This is also in accordance with your original vow to save living beings. That day, Tich Can Bodhisattva taught: "Last month, I was at the border to preach the Dharma and then came here, so Dao Thi relied on my divine power to come with me. Now I did not visit the border, so Dao Thi could not come. On a normal day, Dao Thi's virtuous practice was not up to Dai Son's, but when she was about to die, Dao Thi's mindfulness was far superior to theirs. She was grateful to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara to guide her. At the time of her death, she saw the golden lotus flower appear and was reborn. She was at the border. The seven treasures of the world, dressed naturally, have not yet seen the Buddha, but every day the great Bodhisattvas in the Pure Land preach the Dharma two times. Those who are diligent will reach the age of five hundred years here. From the time they were born, Dao Thi will be very diligent and will be able to be born here in the future.

Tathagata Bodhisattva, when the original Master Shakyamuni Buddha came to this world, attended the Dharma assembly of Vimalakirti and Infinite Life.

Excerpted from the series Thien Nu Nhon Truyen

VII - UONG THI

Uong Thi from Ngo Huyen, wife of Mr. Ly Canh Hi, 26 years old widow, has a son only 7 months old. She was sad, but when her friend brought a human skeleton painting to give her, she was excited and had the intention to go out into the world. She received the Buddhist recitation method from Venerable Ta Ta. She was a vegetarian, and early and late in the evening, she bowed to the West to worship Buddha and vowed to quickly be reborn in the Pure Land.

She encouraged more than a hundred people, even male and female servants, to convert to Buddhism. Among them were a dozen vegetarians who specialized in cultivating pure karma. She came to study ethics with Great Master Thiet Dinh Van Hoc. Listening to the Great Master preach the sentence "The mind is the Buddha", Thi had some enlightenment. At the age of 34, she received the Bodhisattva precepts from the Great Master Lu Dinh Te Association and often recited the Pham Vong Sutra. She made up her mind to prick herself and take the blood from the left tongue of the Lotus Sutra and the Amitabha Sutra. Suffering from not having enough blood to write, there was a monk who told him to take inspiration from the hour of the Rat and the hour of the Horse, thanks to which his wish could be fulfilled. Thi had liver disease, and every year in the fall, the disease would flare up.

In Qianlong's 49th year, the disease became more severe than usual. Someone advised me to be nutritious. She said: "In this world to study the Dharma, there are many obstacles that cause one to retreat. If I can leave my retribution body and soon see the Buddha and hear the Dharma, that is my wish. I wish for nothing else."

In November, she suffered from dysentery and was paralyzed in bed for several days, but Thi still did not stop chanting and thinking about Buddha. On the 10th day, Thi told the patient: "Tomorrow I will return to the Pure Land!". When asked which product, Thi said it was Middle-class, Upper-birth. The next day, Mrs. Phuong came to visit. She said: "It's very nice of you to come, please take a bath for me." After bathing, Thi sat cross-legged quietly. After a while, she told everyone to recite the Buddha's name in unison. Just as it was noon, she clasped her hands and passed away. The fragrant scent of sandalwood fills the whole house. Thi was 38 years old that year.

Three years later, the daughter of the Ha family in that neighborhood fell ill and died. At the third watch, he recounted: "I was taken to Minh Vuong's palace. The king told me my crime and ordered the ghost to use a mace to beat me. Before the ghost could strike, I suddenly saw a group of people supporting a religious person from the West who had come to educate the darkness. That religious person had a golden body, a solemn and beautiful appearance. I looked carefully and saw that she was a teacher from the Ly family in Van Nien Kieu. Minh Vuong knelt down to receive the procession, proclaiming Bodhisattva. The teacher told me to release me and personally led me. I went to see the sufferings in hell. Finally, she told me to fast and recite Buddha's name, single-mindedly praying for the Pure Land, and when the time came, she commanded me to return to the earthly world, so I was resurrected.

VIII - LAN TUONG FEES

Ms. Phi Lan Tuong is from Ngo Giang, wife of layperson Banh Nhi Lam. She has a gentle and calm personality and never scolds anyone in her whole life, even though she is the owner of a rich house. When she encountered something unsatisfactory, she just kept quiet. When she was a girl, her grandmother Vuong liked to do Buddhist work, she had a passionate heart. After living with the lay practitioner Banh Nhi Lam for six years, she gave birth to two daughters. Ke Banh, a lay practitioner who practiced Pure Land, often preached about the method of escaping suffering. She immediately stopped eating fish and meat and lived alone in a small garden. Every day she taught and read the Mahayana Sutra with two girls, dedicating it to the Pure Land.

In the 55th year of Qianlong's reign, in the fall, she suffered from lung disease and blood loss. Her health was very poor. She went to Van Tinh Cac to receive the Upasaka precepts with Venerable Tuong Phong and then returned home to worship Buddha and chant sutras, more diligently than before. Binh Sanh, when she had her own surplus, she immediately did Buddhist work. At that time, she gathered all her personal belongings and money, and asked layman Banh to come to Van The to become a great water boy, vowing to be together with all sentient beings in the Pure Land. The day in Van The to open the Kinh, everyone in the Banh family heard a strange scent. Her illness became more serious and she lay in bed for five days. She often turned to the West and prayed: "Please Amitabha Buddha come to pick me up!".

On the 8th day of the 9th month, the lay practitioner Peng returned home from Van The and exhorted: "The Pure Land's devotion is enough, let go, don't be attached to this redundant life!". She replied: "I'm not attached anymore, I'm just worried about not being able to be reborn soon!". In the middle of that night, she suddenly recited Buddha's name loudly for ten sentences, then peacefully passed away.

IX - SECONDARY PROMISES

Hua Tiet Phu, surnamed Tien, from Thai Thuong, at the age of 20 married Thai and gave birth to Hua Chieu. Six years later, Mr. Chieu died, and she devoted herself to taking care of her husband's parents. In the 37th year of Qianlong's reign, the court gave her the "Tiet Father" plaque.

Since childhood, she has believed in the Buddhist recitation method. One day, her mother was seriously ill. She bowed to Buddha and prayed for her mother's health. Every day she recited Buddha's name a thousand times, and her mother's illness immediately healed. After being widowed, she practiced meditation even more diligently and sincerely. She always gave her own money to help the poor, save those in need, and bribe birds and fish to release animals. Every day she recited the Diamond Sutra and recited Buddha's name to pray for birth in the Pure Land. When she was old, she became a vegetarian.

In January of the 57th year of Qianlong, she dreamed that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared and set a date to receive her. When the time came, on February 4, she lit incense, recited Buddha's name, then sat cross-legged and passed away. Life expectancy is 72 years old.

X - TONG NHU NHON

Tong Nhu Nhon, from Truong Chau, Thai's wife studied and gave birth to Co Van Dieu. She worships her mother-in-law very attentively. Her mother-in-law worshiped Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara on a daily basis. When she passed away, she left her a ceramic statue of Avalokiteśvara, which she worshiped very respectfully for more than ten years.

One day, Thi's son, Mr. Co Tan Phuong, dreamed that two great monks wearing monk robes came to the house and seemed to want to stay. The next morning, I met a man on a boat carrying two statues to sell. The first picture is the monk Quan The Am painted by Ngo Dao Tu, the second picture is an embroidered statue of Avalokiteśvara. Mr. Phuong immediately bought it, asked a worker to repair it, and then offered it to Nguyet Thinh hermitage in the village. The following year, Tan Phuong dreamed again that those two great men said they were going to another place. Mr. Phuong hurried over to the hut to look and saw two rolled statues placed in a tree trunk. Mr. Phuong invited him to his house to worship in the private room. Every day Thi Tong stood next to Amitabha Buddha and respectfully bowed.

One day, on the brick surface in the quiet room suddenly appeared the phenomenon of the Great Monk, exactly like Ngo Dao Tu's painting. Eight days later, on another tile surface, the phenomenon of Tong Tu Dai Tu, Thien Tai and Long Nu also appeared clearly. So he removed the bricks, hired a worker to follow the lines and carve them, and the light was good. Tong Thi appreciated this strange omen and immediately became a vegetarian and concentrated on reciting Buddha's name. Later, Thi became paralyzed, but every day she asked someone to help her to the Buddha's table to pray as usual, not to let it go out of fashion.

One day, Thi called the whole family together to advise and teach them, then told them in unison to recite Buddha's name and not to cry. She clasped her hands and raised them above her head, chanting mantras and chanting the Buddha's name. At first, a strange scent filled the whole house. Thi passed away peacefully at the age of 54. It was May, the 57th year of Qianlong.

Excerpted from the series Nhut Hanh Cu Tap

XI - TRINH THI

Trinh Thi is from Tong Giang, daughter-in-law of the Ngo family. She was widowed when she was young, determined to keep her life, built a quiet room, closed the door and recited Buddhist scriptures for over 20 years.

On July 19, in the first year of Gia Khanh, in the front yard of Thi's retreat, two large lotus flowers grew on a large rock. Just when the official Tu Khau Thai Hong Nghiep, Thi's uncle, a wise man, returned to the village and saw "a large lotus growing on a rock", he wrote an essay about that strange story engraved on the stone stele.

In December of that year, Thi told her family: "I am about to return to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss!". A few days later, Thi was not sick and recited Buddha's name but passed away.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

XII - MỤ BÁ BẤT QUẢN

A rich woman in Hangzhou came to Hieu Tu Temple and asked the Venerable Do Nguyen: "Practice which dharma in one lifetime to surely escape the ocean of suffering?".

The monk taught: "There is nothing better than reciting the Buddha's name! But reciting the Buddha's name is not difficult, but it is difficult for a long time. It is not difficult for a long time, but it is difficult for the mind to be single-minded. If you can not care about all worldly affairs, but concentrate on reciting the Buddha's name and sincerely vow to be reborn, when the Buddha comes to take you and lead you to liberation." She was very happy, bowed to the Venerable and returned. She entrusted all the housework to her daughter-in-law, while she built a private retreat to practice.

More than a year ago, she came to the monastery and told the Venerable Do Nguyen: "Since thanks to the Venerable's teachings, I have given up all housework and only focus on reciting the Buddha's name. By looking at myself, I can also be called not lazy, just suffering and having difficulty being single-minded. I hope that the Venerable will kindly teach me more!"

The monk said: "Even though you have given up housework, in your heart you still remember your children, grandchildren, and relatives. The love has not ended yet and you want to be of one mind! From now on, you must work hard. First of all, you should uproot all love, let go of everything in your heart, and only then can you be of one mind!"

She lamented: "The monk's teachings are very correct! Even though my body is not concerned about my family, my mind cannot leave. From now on, I will make hundreds of decisions and not be able to control them."

After returning to her retreat, she was more diligent in reciting Buddha's name than before. Every time she thought of her family, she immediately told herself: "Hundreds of things don't matter! Hundreds of things don't matter!", to eliminate that remembrance. If anyone asked about housework or life's work, she would only answer with the words: "A hundred things are unmanageable! A hundred things are unmanageable!", then chanting Buddha's name. Therefore, the title "Ba Bat Quan" spread throughout the village, and people no longer called her by her old name.

Almost two years later, she came to the monastery to thank the Venerable Master and said: "I have followed the Venerable's teachings, reciting the Buddha's name has achieved single-mindedness, and have seen the Buddha. In a few days I will return to the Pure Land!".

Two days later, she was not sick, sat upright and was reborn. At that time, it was the first year of Gia Khanh.

Excerpted from Nhiem Huong Tap

CHAPTER EIGHT - MEDITATION OF DETERMINATION

Author: Master AN QUANG

Vietnamese translation: HT. THICH TRI TINH

tom_tat: Since ancient times, in countries where Mahayana Buddhism is widespread, especially China, self-power and Buddha-power have often become opposites, creating great obstacles for people to study the religion, even though both from Buddha Shakyamuni's mouth...
noi_dung:
PREFACE TO VOLUME

Since ancient times, in countries where Mahayana Buddhism has been circulating, especially China, self-power and Buddha-power have often become opposites, very difficult for people to study the religion, even though they were both preached from the mouth of Buddha Shakyamuni and compiled by Venerable Mahakasyapa and Ananda.

For the personal benefit of a group of people with great capacity who came to seek the Dharma, the Patriarchs in Zen Buddhism used the direct view of the true mind to realize the nature of Buddhahood to preach, sometimes in an anti-Lien sect. But those words are a translation for the occasion and are not commonly used words for everyone.

A class of arrogant and conceited monks, according to their narrow knowledge, following that echoing sound, solemnly stand up to attack the Pure Land sect and despise those who practice pure karma, and then commit the crime of defaming the Buddha, destroying the Dharma, and disrespecting the Sangha. Because the practice of reciting the Buddha's name for rebirth is the root of the vow Amitabha Buddha made, Buddha Shakyamuni taught and the Buddhas of the six directions praised it, now the Pure Land practice is slandering the Buddhas. From the Buddha's teachings, the Pure Land teachings are the true teachings, and to reject the Pure Lands is to slander the true teachings. In the Avatamsaka assembly, Samantabhadra, in the Prajnaparamita assembly, Manjushri, and countless great Bodhisattvas all made vows to be reborn in the Pure Land; The Great Master Ma Minh had advice for cultivating the Buddha's name in his treatise On Faith; Nagarjuna Bodhisattva received a prediction from the Buddha to be reborn at the Mausoleum Dharma Assembly, along with countless great Patriarchs of the Mahayana sects, not only the Lien sect but also the Zen sect, the Hoa Nghiem sect, especially the Dharma Hoa sect, down to the Duy Thuc sect, Mr. Thien Than, Mr. Khuy Co, etc., all strongly praised and propagated the Pure Land sect. Nowadays, Pure Land monks who despise people who recite Buddha's name are defaming the Sages and Sangha. Destroying the Three Jewels is the cause of the retribution of Avici hell.

Master An Quang, a high-ranking monk of modern times, took pity on those impulsive people and relied on the voice of Dharma Master Mo Lien in Hong Loa Son to recite this set of sermons, to close the door of hell for them.

The original title is PURE LAND DETERMINATION. In this Vietnamese translation, I have revised it as MEDITATION TINH Quyet Nghi.

This episode criticizes Zen monks' misconceptions about the Pure Land Dharma with a profound and rigorous argument. The Great Master clearly explained the sect of Buddha recitation based on the teachings.

This volume can be a guideline for people who are still hesitant about two paths: practicing Zen or practicing Purity? And it is a solid driver for those who have already developed Buddha's mind.

For Zen practitioners, this volume only shows that there is no need to hesitate and practice reciting Buddha's name to ensure liberation in the future. For Pure practitioners, this volume will guide you to the goal of lotus transformation and dispel the evil teachings of foreign demons.

People who study Buddhism must practice Buddhism, which means they must aim at the goal: CERTIFICATE BUDDHISM, then they must truly be Buddhist disciples.

We should consider ourselves: can we just overcome the sufferings of samsara by ourselves to reach Bodhi, or do we need to rely on the power of Buddha?

We must calmly consider the pros and cons, and not be too arrogant and become impulsive.

A person with a bit of intelligence would never waste time starting a fire by rubbing wood in front of a burning torch.

Only those who are too arrogant are too arrogant to be proud of their own legs, then walk through the forest and climb mountains to cross to Thien Truc land while the ship is waiting at the wharf and the plane is waiting at the airport!

In the Mahavaṭaka Sutra, Buddha taught: “During the time of the loss of dharma, sentient beings can only rely on the power of reciting the Buddha to escape samsara.”

In the Prajnaparamita Sutra, the Buddha dedicated himself to chanting the Buddha's name to answer Manjushri Bodhisattva's question about the question: how to achieve Supreme Enlightenment?

In the Amitabha Sutra, the Buddha repeated the sentence many times: "All sentient beings should make a vow to be born in Amitabha Buddha's Pure Land..."

Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and Manjushri's Prajnaparamita Sutra made the same vow: "I pray that when I am about to die, I will see Amitabha Buddha face to face and immediately be reborn in the Pure Land."

Manjushri Bodhisattva told Great Master Phap Chieu: "If you want to quickly become a Buddha, there is nothing better than concentrating on reciting Amitabha Buddha...". And Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva advised Tu Manh Tripitaka: "If you want to transmit the Dharma to save yourself and others, you should concentrate on reciting the Western Pure Land of Amitabha and vow to be reborn..." (See the full story in The Road to Ultimate Bliss, volume 1).

O dharma friends! Fellow monks! O those who wish to escape from the world of five evil defilements, those who wish to escape the path of reincarnation, those who have the will to save sentient beings!

What are you waiting for? Immediately follow the Buddha's teachings and the great Bodhisattva's advice and specialize in reciting the Buddha's name!

Why do you still hesitate to follow the example of the Patriarchs and Ancient Virtues and immediately make a wish to return to the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss! And do you still have any doubts when you understand the teachings, when you clearly know that before us, there have been countless people who have been reborn, who have achieved supernatural status and entered sainthood thanks to cultivating pure karma!

PL 2500 (1956) Van Duc Ashram

The enlightenment day of Shakyamuni Buddha

Han Tinh Bhikkhu Thich Tri Tinh
